ACCESS.title: Access and recovery
ACCESS.markdown:
# Access and recovery

The node owns Operator, Installer and Admin roles, in ascending authority. Browser sessions use `Authorization: Bearer <session-token>`; machine clients use `X-API-Key: <configured-role-key>`. Persistent keys are not session tokens. Query strings and `X-Auth-Token` are not accepted for persistent credentials.

`POST /api/v1/auth/bootstrap` accepts `{"adminToken":"<private key>"}` with 16–64 characters, only while unprovisioned in FactoryFirstBoot or PhysicalRecovery state. Protected normal APIs require provisioning. Admin manages role credentials through `/api/v1/auth/credentials`.

`POST /api/v1/auth/session` accepts `{"token":"<configured key>"}`. GET inspects the session; DELETE logs out. Never publish real keys or returned tokens in logs or screenshots.

## Lifetime and storage

Eight session slots have a 30-minute idle timeout and eight-hour absolute lifetime. WebSocket tickets are single-use, expire after 15 seconds and have eight slots. Obtain one via `POST /api/v1/auth/ws-ticket`; `src/lib/state/nodeStore.ts` owns the browser connection.

Credentials are stored as SHA-256 digests with 16-byte salts. This does not encrypt transport: the node serves HTTP/WS. Use an appropriately isolated local network.

## Recovery

First boot prints a generated AP key and offers Admin creation. Do not infer a production key from screenshots or the development-credential `test` build.

The runtime watches GPIO0 after a three-second startup grace period. A button held at startup must first be released; a subsequent approximately five-second hold triggers the factory-reset/recovery path. This is a destructive action, not routine login. Preserve configuration and installation records first. Safe/recovery plans keep lighting off and retain API/mDNS.

Sources under `LumigridLedNode/`: `components/auth/AuthManager.cpp`, `components/auth/include/AuthManager.hpp`, `AuthTypes.hpp`, `components/api/ApiAuth.cpp`, `main/LumigridRuntime.cpp`. See [API reference](API_REFERENCE.md) for handler-specific roles.

API_REFERENCE.title: HTTP API reference
API_REFERENCE.markdown:
# HTTP API reference

This inventory is generated from `LumigridLedNode/components/factory/FactoryApi.cpp`.
It lists registered methods, routes and handler guards, not guessed endpoints.
For request/response fields, read the named handler and its matching adapter in
`lumigrid-lander-main/src/lib/api/`. The original detailed reference is retained
as a [historical document](history/2026-10-21/API_REFERENCE.md), not the current contract.

## Transport and authorization

The node serves HTTP and WebSocket `/ws`. There is no registered SSE endpoint.
Normal protected routes require provisioning and an appropriate role. Browser
sessions use `Authorization: Bearer <sessionToken>`; automation uses `X-API-Key`.
No persistent credential belongs in a URL. See [Access](ACCESS.md).

Create Admin access once with POST `/api/v1/auth/bootstrap` and JSON
`{"adminToken":"<16–64 character private key>"}`. Login through POST
`/api/v1/auth/session` with `{"token":"<configured key>"}`. Use the returned
`sessionToken` for protected requests. POST `/api/v1/auth/ws-ticket` obtains a
single-use ticket for the WebSocket handshake. The browser implementation is
`src/lib/state/nodeStore.ts`; do not open a second competing connection.

## Common workflows

| Task | Contract / client owner |
| --- | --- |
| Read identity/capabilities/status | info, identity, capabilities, status; api/node.ts |
| Configure output topology | config GET, config/validate POST, config PUT; api/config.ts |
| Change networking | network/config GET/PUT and network/status GET; api/config.ts |
| Author/activate scenes | presets GET/PUT/DELETE and activate POST; api/scenes.ts |
| Live control/release | manual PUT/DELETE; api/manual.ts |
| Timeline/calendar | sequence and schedules GET/PUT; api/timeline.ts |
| Cue lists and show transport | cue-list, cue/control, show/control; api/cues.ts and showTransport.ts |
| Inspect output/memory/storage | diagnostics routes; api/diagnostics.ts |
| Update firmware | ota POST with raw application bytes; api/firmware.ts |
| Backup/restore | backup GET, restore/validate POST, restore POST; api/recovery.ts |
| Physical acceptance | factory/certification families; api/factory.ts, certification.ts |

Read current data before constructing edits. Preserve schema/version and
revision fields expected by the handler. Command receipts and jobs distinguish
acceptance from completion; observe status/snapshots and failures before calling
an operation applied. Preview frames and estimated power are not measurements.

Typical errors include 400 invalid payload, 401 authorization/session expiry,
403 provisioning/role rejection, 409 conflicting operation/state, 413 image size,
429 authentication throttling and 507 runtime memory admission. Exact JSON
`error` values and additional fields are handler-specific; clients must retain
the server response rather than turning every error into a connectivity message.

OTA is Admin-only, checks image/storage conditions and requires post-reboot
verification. See [Flash layout](FLASH_LAYOUT.md), including the effective
signed-OTA setting. Backup and restore are separate from credential
recovery; inspect validation/scope before applying a restore.

ARCHITECTURE.title: Architecture
ARCHITECTURE.markdown:
# Architecture

`main/main.cpp` enters the application; `main/LumigridRuntime.cpp` coordinates services. `RuntimeServices.hpp` computes the service plan from safe mode, commissioning, network and device configuration. Observed state is reported separately from requested state.

| Component | Ownership |
| --- | --- |
| board | Pin map, early inhibit, reset forensics |
| config / storage | Schemas, validation, migration, NVS |
| auth / api | Credentials, sessions, authorization, audit |
| factory | HTTP routes, WS snapshots, memory diagnostics, test runner |
| signage | Source priority, scenes, effects, composition, color, power |
| output | Output controller/executor, RMT, PCA9685 |
| scheduler / show | Clock, schedules, timelines, cues, transport |
| protocols | Art-Net/sACN reception, DMX routing |
| network / discovery / sync | Wi-Fi, MQTT, mDNS, fleet presence, peer playback |
| ota | Storage contract, image preflight, boot verification |
| control / certification | Commands, jobs, bounded certification evidence |

Sources enter through manual commands, scene/schedule/cue playback, DMX or factory operations. Priority determines ownership. Rendering/composition produce frames; color processing and modeled power limits precede the output controller. Driver success is distinct from command acceptance.

Memory admission governs scratch/output allocation. Factory and network-apply workers are lazy. First-boot/recovery plans keep access services while disabling lighting/protocol work. Discovery and sync require connected station LAN access.

## Web ownership

The SvelteKit project contains public content, docs and the external operator dashboard. `src/lib/api/` owns adapters; `src/lib/state/nodeStore.ts` owns live WS/snapshots; `src/lib/auth/storage.ts` owns browser storage.

`auth/nodeAuth.ts` and `fleet/registry.ts` use the guarded helpers in `auth/storage.ts`. Both storage-property lookup and operations tolerate denied persistence; authentication keeps tab-scoped session credentials in memory when session storage is unavailable. The strict API/storage boundary audit passes.

`embedded/dashboard.html` is a separate device interface. `scripts/build-embedded.mjs` minifies/compresses it into `LumigridLedNode/generated/dashboard_assets.hpp`.

Root `docs/` is the current documentation source. `scripts/sync_documentation.py` extracts route registrations/limits and bundles guides for the site, avoiding deployment-working-directory file reads.

CONFIGURATION.title: Configuration
CONFIGURATION.markdown:
# Configuration

`DeviceConfig` schema **4** is current. `ConfigStore` owns validation, migration and persistence. Network settings use schema **2**; authentication has separate storage from deprecated device credential fields.

Configure 16 channels and up to eight groups. Addressable channels have type, order and pixel count; all channels have enable, brightness, gamma and DMX patch fields. A name alone does not configure a channel: `channel_is_configured()` checks output-relevant fields.

Use GET `/api/v1/config`, POST `/api/v1/config/validate`, then PUT `/api/v1/config`. Inspect validation and command results. Applying may reconfigure outputs/services; acceptance does not prove completion.

| Model field | Declared default |
| --- | --- |
| Name / timezone | `lumigrid` / `UTC0` |
| Gamma | `gamma_x10 = 22` (2.2) |
| Soft start | enabled, 500 ms |
| Art-Net / sACN / MQTT / sync | disabled |
| DMX merge / timeout / layer | HTP / 2000 ms / 2 |
| MQTT port | 1883 |
| Global power ceiling | 0 (no configured ceiling) |

Defaults do not replace saved settings. `reset()` clears nested channel/group/supply storage explicitly; read normalized node configuration instead of assuming every C++ initializer survives reset.

## Power model

Units are milliwatts, millivolts and milliamps. `rated_full_power_mw` describes PWM full-duty load; `channel_limit_mw` is the local ceiling; `max_milliwatts` is a compatibility field. Up to four logical supply domains assign channel masks and derive usable power from voltage, rated current and usable-capacity permille.

`PowerBudget` and the final output guard share conservative command estimates: 5 mW of fixed idle per configured addressable pixel, 295 mW per full-scale RGB component and 380 mW per full-scale white component. Full RGB therefore estimates 890 mW per pixel, and full RGBW estimates 1,270 mW. PWM uses its configured full-duty load rating. These assumptions preserve the final guard's previous model and still require calibration against the actual fixtures.

Channel, supply and global ceilings scale active demand, followed by soft start and transient limiting. Each stage re-estimates the quantized commands; fractional loads remain exact until aggregate reporting rounds upward. Requested power represents the command before these limits, while limited power and supply loads represent the final confirmed driver commands. Renderer previews can differ from final output brightness.

A zero channel/global ceiling means no ceiling at that tier. A disabled supply domain is ignored; an **enabled supply with zero usable capacity** extinguishes its assigned active outputs, including unrated PWM. Fixed addressable idle remains in the estimate. If a ceiling is below that idle floor, the estimate can exceed the ceiling even with all active components zero.

Model states are `complete`, `partial`, `unknown`; missing ratings are not zero consumption. Positive budgets cannot fully constrain an unrated PWM load. Failed output plus failed blackout retains the last confirmed command estimate and marks it incomplete/unknown until a confirmed operation. `output.power.estimateComplete` qualifies the runtime snapshot estimate; measured power remains unavailable. These are software estimates, not current sensors or electrical/thermal certification.

## Network

Modes: `ap_only`, `sta_only`, `sta_with_ap_fallback`. Apply states: `idle`, `applying`, `waiting_for_network`, `rolling_back`, `failed`. Use `/api/v1/network/config` and `/api/v1/network/status`; preserve recovery access while changing connection details. AP passwords differ from Admin keys.

Sources: `LumigridLedNode/components/config/ConfigStore.cpp`, `ConfigApplyPlan.cpp`, `include/SignageTypes.hpp`, `NetworkSettings.hpp`, `ChannelConfiguration.hpp`, and `components/signage/PowerBudget.cpp`.

CONTRIBUTING.title: Development and maintenance
CONTRIBUTING.markdown:
# Development and maintenance

Work from the repository containing both projects. Check branch/remote/dirty files and preserve unrelated work. A standalone copy of the web folder omits shared docs and firmware build inputs.

The documentation sync hooks require Python 3.9+ on PATH as `python`, alongside Node.js. Firmware builds additionally require PlatformIO and its pinned platform/toolchain.

## Web

From `lumigrid-lander-main/`, with Node.js 20+:

```powershell
npm ci
npm run dev
npm run check
npm run test:unit
npm run build
```

`check` combines Svelte sync, copy lint and Svelte checking; report its failures separately from tests/builds. `npm run test` uses Playwright: inspect its server requirements first. The production adapter is Vercel; a build does not deploy.

## Firmware

After web dependencies are installed, from `LumigridLedNode/`:

```powershell
pio run -e factory
python scripts/check_invariants.py
python scripts/verify_partition_layout.py
python scripts/verify_runtime_math.py
```

`factory` is production. `test` enables runtime tests/development credentials. `rollback-test` intentionally requests OTA rollback. Neither test environment is a production release. Serial defaults are not device discovery.

Pre/post-build hooks generate embedded UI, check partitions/invariants and inspect ELF stack/image budget. Report the exact revision/artifact checked.

CMake also prepares and verifies the locked managed dependencies. For the exact known incomplete cJSON checkout, it preserves the original tree under `.pio/dependency-snapshots/` and lets the component manager restore the pinned archive, then verifies the actual package hash. Modified or unfamiliar dependency trees fail without being replaced. Keep these backups until local changes have been reconciled; do not disable component integrity checks. The preparation helper's regression suite runs with ESP-IDF's Python environment after the first firmware build: `"$PLATFORMIO_CORE_DIR/penv/.espidf-5.2.1/bin/python" scripts/test_prepare_managed_components.py` (POSIX shell).

To exercise the production effect renderer and catalogue API on a host, run from the repository root:

```powershell
python LumigridLedNode/scripts/test_effects.py
python LumigridLedNode/scripts/test_effect_catalog_api.py
```

The renderer harness requires Python and a C++17 compiler (`g++` by default, or the compiler named by `CXX`). AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer are enabled by default; `--no-sanitize` is available for hosts without those runtimes. It builds the production renderer and catalogue with a minimal GPIO enum stub. The API harness additionally requires a host C compiler (`cc` by default, or `CC`) and the repository's managed cJSON sources. It exercises catalogue responses, palette-ID validation, bounded JSON allocation, and error handling on the host. Host results are separate from a full ESP-IDF/PlatformIO build and physical RGB/RGBW/PWM output validation. Report which commands and sanitizer mode were actually run.

## Shared content

From repository root:

```powershell
python scripts/sync_documentation.py
python scripts/sync_documentation.py --check
python scripts/check_api_surface.py --strict
```

The sync script generates the route inventory, capability facts and web docs bundle. Commit guides/generated data together; do not edit generated sections. Public claims need an implementation, enabling condition and limit. Flags are not enforcement proof, intervals are not timing measurements, and previews are not physical evidence.

Edit embedded UI in `embedded/dashboard.html`, not generated C++. Managed-component READMEs/licenses remain upstream-owned.

EFFECTS.title: Effects and playback
EFFECTS.markdown:
# Effects and playback

The firmware catalogue contains **24 effects and 14 palettes**. Read `GET /api/v1/effects` and `GET /api/v1/palettes` from the connected node for its supported catalogue; an older firmware version may expose fewer entries. Effect metadata defines the label, description, speed control, secondary-color and palette support, spatial behavior, PWM recommendation, and parameter limits/defaults.

The effect IDs below are stable API names. Existing numeric effect IDs 0–11 and palette IDs 0–5 retain their identities; new entries are appended. Saved scenes continue to refer to the same effects and palettes.

## Choosing an effect

Addressable WS2812 RGB and SK6812 RGBW lanes can display position, color, and brightness changes across up to 256 pixels. Each of the eight PWM outputs is an independent single-channel dimmer. It can reproduce a brightness rhythm, but it cannot display a color gradient or a moving spot.

**PWM: yes** in the tables means the effect is recommended by the firmware metadata for a single dimmer. **PWM: no** means use an addressable lane for its intended appearance. In particular, the new spatial and color-only effects emit steady PWM duty; choosing them on a dimmer does not reproduce their pixel animation. Color wave also has a dimmer envelope, but remains marked as an addressable effect because its intended appearance is spatial.

For speed-enabled effects, `speedMs` is a timing duration: a larger value produces slower motion or change. It is the complete cycle for most repeating patterns. Candlelight, Living flame, Soft twinkle, and Confetti use it as a noise or event timescale. Random twinkle has a fixed 50 ms update interval and does not expose a speed control.

The parameter column lists the supported range followed by the default in parentheses. These are effect parameters, separate from layer opacity, scene brightness, and output brightness limits.

### Established effects

| API ID | Label | Appearance and useful distinction | Parameter: range (default) | PWM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `solid` | Steady color | An even wash of the primary color. | None | Yes |
| `breathe` | Smooth pulse | Brightness rises and falls smoothly while the selected color blend or palette changes with the pulse. | Minimum glow: 1–100% (4%) | Yes |
| `chase` | Moving comet | A bright head travels from the beginning to the end of the lane, followed by a short fading tail. | Tail length: 1–8 pixels (3) | No |
| `sweep` | Color sweep | The primary color progressively fills the lane, then starts again. | None | No |
| `reveal` | Soft reveal | The whole lane fades in together, holds, and repeats. It does not sequence separate lanes. | Fade length: 10–90% of the cycle (25%) | Yes |
| `sparkle` | Random twinkle | Crisp white accents appear over a steady primary-color background every 50 ms. | Twinkles: 1–12 per lane (2) | No |
| `gradient` | Flowing glow | A moving color gradient carries a soft brightness wave. Lower contrast makes the intensity more even. | Wave contrast: 0–100% (100%) | No |
| `strobe` | Beat strobe | The primary color switches on and off with a regular duty cycle. | Flash time: 5–95% of the cycle (50%) | Yes |
| `fire` | Living flame | A flickering color texture with a configurable height profile along the lane. | Flame height: 20–100% (70%) | No |
| `aurora` | Aurora glow | The primary color's RGB components gently change across the whole lane together. | Color depth: 1–255 (120) | Yes |
| `colorwave` | Color wave | A repeated sine-shaped color and brightness wave moves along the pixels. | Wave length: 10–255 pixels (50) | No |
| `staticpulse` | Static pulse | A smooth brightness pulse that keeps the primary color fixed. | Min dim: 0–100% (20%) | Yes |

### Additional effects

| API ID | Label | Appearance and useful distinction | Parameter: range (default) | PWM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rainbow` | Rainbow flow | A full spectrum moves along the lane at even intensity. It uses its own rainbow colors, independent of the palette selector. | Spectrum repeats: 1–8 (1) | No |
| `colorfade` | Color fade | The whole lane blends through the selected palette and back, holding at each endpoint without an added brightness pulse. | Endpoint hold: 0–40% of the cycle at each end (10%) | No |
| `scanner` | Soft scanner | A soft spotlight moves to the far end and back, with fractional pixel coverage for smooth motion. | Spot width: 1–64 pixels (6) | No |
| `theater` | Marquee chase | Spaced lights advance continuously along the lane. | Spacing: 2–32 pixels (6) | No |
| `twinkle` | Soft twinkle | Colored points gently fade in and out over black. Each pixel has a repeatable time offset. | Density: 1–100% (25%) | No |
| `candle` | Candlelight | An even primary-color wash follows an irregular, smoothly changing brightness rhythm. Depth zero gives a steady wash. | Flicker depth: 0–100% (35%) | Yes |
| `heartbeat` | Heartbeat | A stronger pulse, a softer second pulse, and a quiet rest repeat as one cycle. | Minimum glow: 0–80% (4%) | Yes |
| `ripple` | Center ripple | Soft fronts expand from the center toward both ends and disappear beyond the lane. | Ring width: 1–64 pixels (8) | No |
| `dissolve` | Dissolve | Pixels transition between palette endpoints in a repeatable shuffled order, then reverse. Choose a black endpoint for a fill-and-clear appearance. | Edge softness: 1–100% (15%) | No |
| `plasma` | Plasma flow | Several overlapping waves create a moving color texture. Increasing scale adds spatial detail. | Scale: 1–8 waves (3) | No |
| `lightning` | Lightning | A short cluster of primary-color flashes has varying flash strength, followed by a dark half-cycle. | Flashes: 1–5 per burst (3) | Yes |
| `confetti` | Confetti | Colored sparks appear abruptly over black, then decay into softer glows. | Density: 1–100% (15%) | No |

Density controls the proportion of eligible pixel events, not an exact number of lit pixels in every frame. The difference between the sparkle choices is deliberate: Random twinkle adds hard white accents to a lit background, Soft twinkle fades colored points in and out, and Confetti uses a fast appearance followed by a fade.

On a one-pixel addressable lane, color and brightness effects still have useful behavior, while spatial movement is reduced to the value at that pixel. A one-pixel Soft scanner is steady because its start and end positions coincide. Choose Candlelight, Heartbeat, Smooth pulse, or Static pulse when the aim is to animate a single dimmer.

## Palettes and colors

Palette-capable effects are Smooth pulse, Moving comet, Flowing glow, Living flame, Color wave, Color fade, Soft scanner, Marquee chase, Soft twinkle, Center ripple, Dissolve, Plasma flow, and Confetti. Other effects use the primary color or their own fixed color rule. The connected node's metadata controls which editor fields are available.

**Custom (0)** interpolates between the layer's primary and secondary colors. A named palette supplies its own colors, so editing the two custom colors does not replace that palette. Setting both custom colors to the same value gives palette-capable effects a single-color appearance; choosing black at one end allows effects such as Dissolve to move between color and darkness.

| Palette ID | Name | Color character |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Custom | The layer's primary-to-secondary blend. |
| 1 | Rainbow | A continuous green, red, blue, and green spectrum. |
| 2 | Ocean | Blue and teal through bright cyan. |
| 3 | Lava | Deep red through orange and pale warm tones. |
| 4 | Forest | Green through brighter yellow-green. |
| 5 | Sunset | The established red and warm blend continuing toward pale cyan. |
| 6 | Amber | Dark amber, gold, and soft warm highlights. |
| 7 | Ice | Deep blue through cyan to near-white. |
| 8 | Neon | Cyan, violet, pink, and vivid green. |
| 9 | Lavender | Deep violet through lavender to pale pink. |
| 10 | Candy | Crimson and rose through pink to warm cream. |
| 11 | Festive | Red, gold, green, and warm white. |
| 12 | Ember | Near-black and deep red through orange to gold. |
| 13 | Twilight | Deep violet and magenta through peach. |

Palettes 6–13 interpolate four fixed color stops. The original six palettes retain their established rendering math. Palettes describe RGB color; the existing output color pipeline handles RGBW conversion, gamma, brightness, and power limiting for the configured hardware.

## Building a scene

1. Configure the target channels, pixel type/order, and pixel count, then read their current capabilities. The scene editors identify all 16 outputs as addressable lanes A1–A8 and PWM dimmers P1–P8. See [Configuration](CONFIGURATION.md).
2. Open a scene and enable a layer on the target channel. Choose an effect suitable for that output. Set the primary color, or select Custom and a secondary color when the effect supports a blend.
3. Set speed and the effect's parameter. Begin with the catalogue default, then adjust it while observing the connected output. A wide spot or ring on a short lane can illuminate most of the lane at once.
4. Add another layer when needed and choose its blend mode and opacity. Normal blends over the lower layer; Add and Screen are useful for bright accents over a wash; Multiply can shape a lower layer with a brightness pattern. A black background behaves differently under each blend mode.
5. Save the scene to a preset slot and activate it through the normal playback controls. Saving a document and activating playback are separate operations. Inspect applied/failed status and actual output; a preview is not physical verification.

For PWM layers, the **Intensity** control adjusts the layer's opacity (0–255) and preserves its stored primary and secondary RGB colors. It controls the layer's contribution to the dimmer output. The effect's brightness envelope, blend mode, scene brightness, and channel limits still determine the final level.

These combinations are useful starting points:

| Aim | Suggested scene setup |
| --- | --- |
| Gentle ambient dimming | Candlelight on a PWM output, or Static pulse when a regular rhythm is preferred. |
| A restrained branded sign | A low-opacity Steady color base, plus Soft scanner in Add or Screen mode using the same custom primary and secondary colors. |
| Decorative stars | Soft twinkle with Lavender or Ice; use Add or Screen over a dim base layer. |
| A colorful moving texture | Plasma flow with Neon or Twilight; start at the default scale before adding detail. |
| A shuffled color reveal | Dissolve with Custom, one brand color, and one black endpoint. |

## Storage and playback

There are 32 preset slots and eight zones/groups. Current scene schema 2 stores up to three layers for each of the 16 output channels; the legacy scene schema stored content by zone. Blend modes are `normal`, `add`, `multiply`, and `screen`. Scene motion supports four tracks of six points. Timelines expose 16 steps; cue storage supports eight lists of 16 cues. These are model capacities, not throughput benchmarks.

Scenes, Timeline, and Cues dashboard pages author these documents. APIs separate storage, activation, motion, sequence, and transport control. See [API reference](API_REFERENCE.md).

Current scene-save requests use the 16-entry `channels` array. The dashboard serializers omit the redundant legacy `zones` mirror when sending that representation. `PUT /api/v1/presets` accepts JSON bodies up to **16 KiB (16,384 bytes)** for the channel layers and bounded motion data; runtime memory admission still applies. Larger scene bodies return HTTP 413 with `scene_payload_too_large`. Other handlers using the default JSON reader retain its **8 KiB (8,192 bytes)** limit. Use effect IDs from the connected catalogue and integer palette IDs; the current catalogue accepts palette IDs 0–13.

Priority, highest first: EStop, Factory, LiveDmx, ManualOverride, Scheduler, ScenePlayback, Fallback, Idle. Live input can override a saved scene; releasing manual control is different from saving a preset.

`SceneManager::init()` loads the saved active scene, tries slot zero if unavailable, then defaults to blackout if neither loads. It does not promise exact cue/timeline-position restoration after power loss. Setup, safe mode, configuration failures, and output faults can prevent playback.

Calendar operation uses the configured timezone and clock service. Validate clock readiness and schedules on the installation.

## Rendering and validation boundaries

The added effects compute their frame from the layer settings, pixel position, and time. They use fixed storage with no per-frame heap allocation or previous-frame history. The same inputs produce the same frame regardless of skipped frames or which other layer rendered first. This does not establish synchronization accuracy between separate nodes.

The animation timestamp remains a 32-bit millisecond value. It wraps after approximately 49.7 days, and a phase change at that boundary remains possible. The effect expansion does not widen that clock or alter the output drivers.

Host renderer checks are available through `python LumigridLedNode/scripts/test_effects.py` from the repository root. These checks exercise production rendering code on the host; they do not substitute for a complete ESP-IDF/PlatformIO build, target timing measurements, or physical RGB/RGBW/PWM validation. See [Development](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Hardware validation](HARDWARE_VALIDATION.md) for the separate workflows.

Sources: `LumigridLedNode/components/config/include/SignageTypes.hpp`, `signage/EffectRenderer.cpp`, `signage/LightingRuntime.cpp`, `SceneManager.cpp`, `AutomationEngine.cpp`, `include/ControlSource.hpp`, `scheduler/`, and `show/`. Catalogue API handlers are in `LumigridLedNode/components/factory/FactoryApi.cpp`.

FIRMWARE_RELEASE_CANDIDATE.title: Firmware release candidate 1.0.0-rc2
FIRMWARE_RELEASE_CANDIDATE.markdown:
# Firmware release candidate 1.0.0-rc2

Date: 2026-10-23. Source baseline: `e75c52c10c4b4dea87c2cdb72fe1915b7d638b26` (rc1 plus the CI environment correction).

This candidate continues the rc1 reliability work with fixes to backup/restore, persistent configuration, OTA verification, worker shutdown, frame consistency and factory-job cancellation. It is a software candidate for bench testing. Physical stability, RF/EMC, electrical safety and thermal acceptance have not been measured in this change. Record the final Git commit and the exact artifact hashes from the build manifest when testing; the version string alone is insufficient to identify a binary.

## Additional changes in rc2

| Area | Reproduced fault | Resulting behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Backup integrity | A valid export could fail its own parser; missing terminal records, altered checksums and duplicate records could be accepted | A v4 package requires its header, complete record sequence, exact count and raw-stream CRC; invalid or incomplete content is rejected before mutation |
| Backup fidelity and JSON safety | Short JSON strings were over-read; unsigned checksums were narrowed; palettes, motion speed, labels and protocol values could change | Bounded string copies and typed numeric checks preserve supported values; scene/configuration round trips and allocation failures have production-source regressions |
| Restore transaction | Snapshot errors, partial writes, stale readback and marker failures could still produce success; rollback touched unrelated records | Read-only affected-record snapshots precede a verified marker; every written payload is checked; rollback is limited to attempted records and incomplete recovery retains the marker |
| Board identity | A restore could replace the target serial/revision and legacy tokens | Restore retains the target identity, authentication fields and sync secret; Wi-Fi credentials remain outside the package |
| Persistent records | Network save mislabeled the schema; missing/corrupt primaries could hide valid backups; mirror failures were ignored | Compatible old network records migrate with checked results; valid backups load without silent repair writes; corrupt, absent and I/O-error states remain distinct |
| Interrupted restore at boot | Default seeding or successful config validation could overwrite the recovery condition | Active restore markers suppress default seeding; failed marker reads fail closed; outputs stay inhibited until explicit recovery |
| OTA image acceptance | A truncated upload could rely on an old image tail still in flash; boot selection could precede durable journal intent | IDF verifies the image against the bytes actually received; intent commits before boot selection; status exposes actual and persistence errors |
| OTA boot verification | Matching version strings could imply a false confirmation/rollback; unavailable NVS could bypass failure handling | Running partition and bootloader state decide the outcome; healthy dwell and rollback are latched; early startup faults can request rollback even before normal verifier initialization |
| Runtime ownership | A timed-out stop could clear the ownership flag and allow re-entry | Stop errors propagate; live tasks, callbacks and synchronization objects remain owned until acknowledgement; failed shutdown does not rebind Wi-Fi underneath a live service |
| Lighting state | Concurrent manual/scene changes could produce mixed frames; short live frames retained pixel tails; an older reset could clear a newer logical stop | Composition uses a consistent state under the existing mutex; unused live pixels are cleared; deferred stop reset is tied to the controller generation; restart clears old manual/frozen transitions |
| Factory jobs | Cancelled could be published before the worker stopped output; a full queue could leave orphan job state | Cancellation remains pending until the worker processes it; queue failures retain ownership or fail the rejected start; terminal jobs cannot be revived by late progress; HTTP and dashboard messages report acceptance until completion |
| Certification cancellation | Evidence-save failures and aborts could release a live burn-in job; rejected physical starts retained nonexistent session IDs | The service retains and retries owned cancellation until worker acknowledgement, blocks competing manual starts during certification, and records rejected physical tests as Blocked |

Restore is a checked multi-record operation, not an atomic NVS transaction. A power loss can leave a partial set of records. The durable marker causes recovery on the next boot; it does not reconstruct the lost in-memory rollback snapshot. A second partial restore is rejected while that marker is active. Retain/export known-good backups and use explicit recovery/recommissioning for an interrupted restore. Admission preserves the existing 16 KB reserve and checks both total scratch memory and the largest individual allocation; low-memory restores can return 507 without mutation.

## Changes inherited from rc1 relevant to board qualification

| Area | Defect addressed | Intended behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Early GPIO safety | Output mode could expose a low reset latch before `/OE` was raised; output-only pads could not provide meaningful readback | Preload safe levels, enable readable output pads, check all operations and refuse runtime startup if the early safety step fails |
| PWM output | A zero-frame prerequisite prevented normal nonzero output; recovery and gate failures could be reported incorrectly | Enable a valid frame only after initialization/recovery succeeds; keep faults inhibited and count gate failure as a failed commit |
| Stop during a commit | An interleaved commit could reopen the PWM gate or a clear operation could erase a newer stop | Serialize the final gate decision with the stop latch and retain newer stop generations |
| RMT transport | A timeout was treated as if hardware had released its frame buffer and channel | Track in-flight ownership, bound queue/drain waits and quarantine incomplete teardown until safe recovery is possible |
| Wi-Fi recovery | Late events and immediate connection failures could strand fallback/retry state | Gate events during stop, preserve recovery AP behavior, retry synchronous failures and bound callback shutdown |
| Network apply | Failed Wi-Fi stop and failed readiness allocation could be ignored | Keep live callback ownership intact, report transition failures and avoid waiting on a null semaphore |
| Configuration copying | Fixed-size copies read beyond short strings | Copy with source termination and destination bounds; sanitizer regressions cover short and legacy buffers |
| Internal acceptance plan | 46 entries were written into a 40-entry record; long IDs were truncated; incomplete evidence could pass | Bound the plan and IDs, require every required result, validate evidence and invalidate older schemas |
| Certification persistence | Commit failures could be reported as success and raw mirrored records exceeded available NVS capacity | Check storage results, preserve the previous committed generation, validate loaded records and use bounded lossless encoding |
| Release packaging | The workflow merged an 8 MB layout with a 4 MB image declaration | Enforce consistent 8 MB layout/image metadata, package exact binaries and their configurations/hashes, and publish CI artifacts |

The default firmware accurately reports that signed OTA verification is disabled. This change does not provision signing keys, secure boot or irreversible eFuse settings.

## Build and reproducibility

The build pins PlatformIO 6.2.0 in CI, the Espressif32 platform to 6.7.0 and ESP-IDF to the platform's 5.2.1 package. The embedded dashboard uses the checked-in npm lockfile. Build the production candidate and the diagnostic image separately:

```sh
python -m pip install platformio==6.2.0
npm ci --prefix lumigrid-lander-main
cd LumigridLedNode
pio run -e factory -e test
```

The GitHub firmware workflow is the canonical packaging command sequence. It uses the installed PlatformIO esptool package to merge the factory image with `--flash_size 8MB`, then runs `scripts/firmware_release_manifest.py`. Its artifact is named `lumigrid-firmware-candidate-<Git SHA>` and includes:

- Factory and test application binaries, bootloaders, partition tables and ELF files.
- Effective sdkconfig files and generated build metadata for each environment.
- The generated embedded dashboard, dependency lock and pinned build configuration.
- Source and artifact SHA-256 inventories, tool versions, image/partition validation and the factory linked-stack report.
- Explicit `hardware_validation: NOT_RUN` and `compliance_assessment: NOT_PERFORMED` labels.

Candidate packaging validates the complete bootloader and application images for both environments: ESP32 chip identity, the production flash header, segment boundaries, checksum padding, the payload XOR checksum and the appended SHA-256 digest. It records the successful image checks in each build's `image_integrity` field. Truncated/corrupt images, a missing digest and unexpected trailing data fail before publication. This contract covers the unsigned, unpadded output of the pinned build; signed or padded image formats need an explicitly reviewed packaging policy. The appended digest detects corruption and does not authenticate the producer or enable secure boot; see [Espressif's image-format reference](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esptool/en/release-v4/esp32/advanced-topics/firmware-image-format.html).

The final artifact records and staged copies must match the exact bytes accepted by image, partition and merged-layout validation. A binary replaced during packaging is rejected, including a structurally valid replacement; it cannot acquire a fresh success hash without repeating validation.

The manifest records current matching source inputs and successful packaging checks; it is not cryptographic proof of the compilation process. Build with a clean checkout, retain the build log and do not modify inputs during a release build. Use the factory binary for normal operation. The test image contains diagnostic/development flags and is not the product image.

The merged image is intended for fresh installation. It includes erased padding across NVS/OTA metadata. For an existing board, preserve its configuration using the appropriate [flash migration or application-only OTA procedure](FLASH_LAYOUT.md).

## Software verification

The committed workflow runs boot configuration/stack checks, partition and packaging regressions, board GPIO failure injection, output-driver and Wi-Fi recovery scenarios, configuration memory-safety checks, certification service/API/storage regressions, architectural invariants and runtime mathematics. Output, configuration and certification host harnesses exercise production source with AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer where applicable. Host stubs model error conditions; they do not emulate ESP32 peripheral timing or RF behavior.

Both ESP32 images must compile and satisfy the production partition/image budget. The factory ELF is checked for boot-stack limits. Building the diagnostic image does not mean its on-device suite has run. The final change report records the actual checks completed for this candidate.

### rc2 software verification

The rc2 workflow adds production-source host suites for persistent records, backup/export/ingest, restore transactions, runtime recovery, terminal jobs, factory cancellation and admission, lighting state, OTA boot verification and upload. It also runs the existing effects and catalogue API gates. Fault injection includes NVS writes/commits/readback, socket interruption, failed allocation, queued producers and delayed worker acknowledgement. AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer are enabled by the new host harnesses. LeakSanitizer is disabled in the restricted host runtime; the backup harness also tracks live cJSON allocations explicitly.

| rc2 host check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Persistent configuration | 44 scenarios passed, including 42 injected write/commit failure combinations within the matrix cases |
| Backup export, parsing and fidelity | 33 scenarios passed, including malformed/truncated packages, allocation failures, integer boundaries and full supported timeline tempo range |
| Restore transaction and rollback | 35 scenarios passed, including snapshots, partial writes, readback mismatch, marker failures and preservation of absent/unrelated records |
| Runtime recovery and shutdown ownership | 16 scenarios passed |
| OTA boot verification / upload and status | 24 / 25 scenarios passed |
| Output drivers / lighting state / terminal jobs | 30 / 13 / 5 scenarios passed; output total includes the PM teardown variant |
| Factory worker cancellation and lifetime | 8 scenarios passed |
| Factory cancellation and admission API | 17 scenarios passed, including active/pending certification exclusion and idle/no-service controls |
| Certification service / result and abort API | 31 / 20 scenarios passed |
| Wi-Fi recovery / bounded configuration strings | 25 / 6 scenarios passed |
| Boot configuration / stack parser / partition / release manifest | 8 / 7 / 3 / 10 checks passed |
| Board GPIO failure injection | Safe latch/readback and 27 injected failures passed |
| Certification storage | 22 scenarios passed, plus the codec-pattern matrix |
| Effects / catalogue API / embedded dashboard | 12 effect groups, real catalogue/scene-handler regression harness and embedded dashboard smoke passed |

| rc2 build and packaging check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Final ESP32 factory build | PASS; application binary 1,380,336 bytes, 56.9% of the 2,424,832-byte slot |
| Final ESP32 diagnostic build | PASS; application binary 1,580,704 bytes, 65.2% of the slot |
| Factory linked boot-stack gate | PASS; estimated acyclic direct-call path 5,616 bytes; indirect/ROM/interrupt use still requires target measurement |
| Source consistency across the final build | PASS; all 601 inventoried source inputs matched before and after compilation |
| Web application and generated documentation | PASS |
| Architectural invariants and runtime mathematics | PASS |
| Real merged-image candidate packaging | PASS; image contents, 8 MB configuration, partitions and artifact hashes validated |

The factory application SHA-256 is `227f2aaffb08d7464cfcba02f9b2bc9b071554db3abf9cc5f059b746e19a4140`; the diagnostic application SHA-256 is `b8fec989415d20edf964fe134c8fa1c1546f50a0e5155719fff2e24cd3a071cc`. The candidate manifest contains the complete inventories and the final source commit. Hosted CI status is reported separately from these local checks.

The values in the next table are retained as **rc1 evidence**, not measurements of the rc2 binary.

### Prior rc1 measurements from 2026-10-23

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Final ESP32 factory build | PASS; application binary 1,367,456 bytes, 56.4% of the 2,424,832-byte slot |
| Final ESP32 diagnostic build | PASS; application binary 1,571,776 bytes, 64.8% of the slot |
| Factory linked boot-stack gate | PASS; estimated acyclic direct-call path 5,632 bytes; indirect/ROM/interrupt use still requires target measurement |
| Diagnostic certification stack frames | Compiled service test 448 bytes; physical-output-engine test 1,168 bytes, with large certification fixtures on checked heap allocations |
| Output driver host regressions | 28 scenarios plus 1 PM-enabled teardown/quarantine scenario passed |
| Wi-Fi host regressions | 25 scenarios passed, including old-session events and bounded callback/event-queue shutdown |
| Certification service / API / storage | 20 / 17 / 22 scenarios passed; storage coverage also exercises 96 codec patterns and modeled capacity |
| Early board GPIO / configuration copy | Safe latch/readback and 27 injected GPIO failures passed; 6 bounded-copy memory-safety cases passed |
| Boot configuration / boot-stack parser / partition layout / release manifest | 8 / 7 / 3 / 10 tests passed |
| Effects and catalogue API | 12 effect groups and real catalogue/scene-handler regressions passed |
| Architectural invariants and runtime mathematics | PASS |
| Web application build and generated documentation checks | PASS |
| Real merged-image candidate packaging | PASS; binary contents, effective 8 MB configuration, partitions and artifact hashes validated |

Those rc1 runtime/build inputs were fingerprinted during the frozen final build and matched after it. The raw certification record is 8,000 bytes; the host fixtures store an initial session in 833 bytes and a representative completed session in 2,609 bytes. These sizes describe those fixtures, not guaranteed capacity for every note/configuration combination. No physical measurements or on-device diagnostic execution are included in these results.

## Bench acceptance before the lab handoff

Use the intended PCB revision, enclosure, antenna, supplies, wiring and supported maximum loads. The sequence below is an engineering acceptance proposal; the lab must confirm the product's applicable conformity scope and operating modes.

| Gate | Exercise | Evidence to retain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image identity | Read board identity, firmware version and application ELF hash; match them to the archived candidate | Git SHA, binary/ELF hashes, board serial/revision, flash size and effective configuration |
| Boot and reset | Repeat cold starts and software resets; observe `/OE` and all eight addressable data pins from power application through readiness | Serial log and scope captures showing safe boot behavior; actual pull-up/level-shifter behavior before firmware begins |
| PWM channels | Exercise P1–P8 individually through zero, intermediate and intended full duty; inhibit with `/OE` | Scope duty/frequency, mapping and current observations; no unintended active channels |
| Addressable channels | Exercise A1–A8, correct color order, maximum intended pixel count and combined updates | Visible mapping plus logic-analyzer timing/error evidence under concurrent Wi-Fi traffic |
| Failure recovery | Introduce controlled I2C faults, network loss/reconnect and logical stop during output changes | Fault diagnostics, inhibited PWM, truthful blackout status, AP availability and successful bounded recovery |
| State persistence | Save intended configuration, network settings and acceptance results; round-trip a v4 backup; reboot and read back; test controlled power interruptions during save and restore | Previous or new complete valid record, explicit capacity/write errors, preserved credentials/configuration and exported reports |
| OTA and rollback | Perform compatible application updates, same-version updates, truncated uploads and controlled rejected/interrupted updates; induce startup failure before configuration init | Correct running hash, healthy dwell/verification, recovery path and preserved configuration |
| Combined endurance | Run the intended output topology with network/API/protocol traffic and representative scene transitions for the agreed duration | Continuous serial logs, free/largest heap and task stack minima, reset/watchdog/transport counters, actual supply current and temperatures |
| Radio/EMC preparation | Confirm Wi-Fi modes/channels, antenna and transmission settings with the lab; supply requested RF test firmware separately | Frozen product configuration and the lab's agreed operating-mode/test matrix |

Report each gate as PASS, FAIL or NOT_RUN with its observations and instrument context. Missing observations, sentinel telemetry values and a `MARGINAL` stress-run result are not a pass. `scripts/hardware_coexistence_soak.py` can drive combined-load exercise, but its summary does not replace electrical measurements or review of the raw diagnostics.

### Limits requiring explicit disposition

- The current board capability flags declare no physical emergency-stop input and no addressable power gate. If RMT is stuck, software cannot guarantee that previously latched LED output is dark. Validate the actual hardware shutdown requirement and supply isolation design.
- NVS remains 16 KB. Encoded acceptance records reduce ordinary storage pressure, but full/high-entropy notes plus other stored content can still exhaust it. Verify the intended production content, export records and resolve any `persistence_failed` state before accepting a unit. No automatic whole-partition erase is performed by these fixes.
- Signature enforcement is disabled in the default candidate. Confirm the required production security/provisioning design and applicable product requirements before market release.
- No physical board, RF, EMC, thermal, electrical or long-duration measurements were performed by this software change. Previous reports remain evidence only for their original hardware and image.

## CE preparation references

CE marking is the manufacturer's conformity declaration supported by the applicable assessment and technical documentation. There is no general EU-issued permission certificate for attaching the mark; whether a notified body is required depends on the applicable legislation and assessment route. See the [European Commission's CE guidance](https://europa.eu/youreurope/business/product-rules-compliance/general-product-compliance/ce-marking/index_en.htm).

For this Wi-Fi product, have the lab confirm the Radio Equipment Directive scope and current applicable requirements. Retain the exact firmware/configuration identity in the technical file and agree the intended operating conditions to test. See [Directive 2014/53/EU](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014L0053), especially Article 17 and Annex V.

Espressif supplies [CE radio test guidance](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-test-tools/en/latest/esp32/development_stage/rf_test_certification/ce_certification.html) and [EspRFTestTool with dedicated RF test firmware](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-test-tools/en/latest/esp32/development_stage/rf_test_guide/rf_test_guide.html). Agree those images/settings with the lab and archive them separately from the product candidate.

FLASH_LAYOUT.title: Flash layout and updates
FLASH_LAYOUT.markdown:
# Flash layout and updates

Layout v2 targets 8 MB flash. `partitions.factory.csv` defines:

| Partition | Offset | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nvs | 0x9000 | 0x4000 |
| otadata | 0xd000 | 0x2000 |
| phy_init | 0xf000 | 0x1000 |
| factory | 0x10000 | 0x250000 |
| ota_0 | 0x260000 | 0x250000 |
| ota_1 | 0x4b0000 | 0x250000 |
| littlefs | 0x700000 | 0x100000 |

The `littlefs` label has the CSV `spiffs` subtype; the name alone does not establish a mounted LittleFS content store. ConfigStore/NVS owns configuration persistence.

## Build and wired migration

Build `factory`. Pre/post-build hooks generate embedded assets and check invariants, partition layout, ELF stack and image budget. `verify_partition_layout.py` checks layout/storage capacity.

An older partition layout requires wired migration. `scripts/migrate_flash_v2.py` verifies artifact headers/table/physical flash, backs up NVS privately, writes bootloader/table/OTA initializer/application, then verifies NVS preservation. Its default build directory is historical; pass the actual fresh build and port from `LumigridLedNode/`:

```powershell
python scripts/migrate_flash_v2.py --port COM_PORT --build-dir .pio/build/factory
```

Review the script and retain a backup first. Whole-chip erase is not a preservation migration.

## OTA

Admin-only POST `/api/v1/ota` accepts a raw application image. It checks maintenance conflicts, memory, image size, storage health, chip/image descriptor and project identity `lumigrid_led_node`, writes the next slot and persists a verification journal before reboot.

Boot policy requires 10 seconds of healthy dwell inside a 60-second window. Fatal startup, critical memory or timeout can request rollback. Inspect `/api/v1/ota/status`, recovery status and health after reconnecting. Upload completion is not boot acceptance.

The `signedOta` capability follows ESP-IDF's effective `CONFIG_SECURE_SIGNED_ON_UPDATE` setting. The checked-in defaults leave it disabled, so the default build reports `signedOta=false`. Image validation and rollback do not establish cryptographic signature enforcement. A signed production provisioning/update process remains separate work.

## Traceable candidate artifacts

The firmware workflow builds both `factory` and `test`, then packages their binaries, ELF files, effective configurations, source/tool hashes and the checked partition table with `scripts/firmware_release_manifest.py`. The factory image is the production candidate; the test image contains diagnostic/development flags. The manifest explicitly records hardware validation as `NOT_RUN` and compliance assessment as `NOT_PERFORMED`.

The merged image declares **8 MB** flash. It is a fresh-install image at offset zero: its padding covers NVS and OTA metadata and can erase saved credentials/configuration if written to an existing device. Use the preserving migration above for an older layout, or application-only OTA on a compatible layout. Do not treat the merged image as a preserving update.

See [firmware candidate and bench gates](FIRMWARE_RELEASE_CANDIDATE.md) before handing an image to a test lab.

The web flasher provides build guidance: no verified `latest_builds/manifest.json` release bundle is supplied by this checkout.

Sources: `LumigridLedNode/platformio.ini`, `partitions.factory.csv`, `scripts/pre_build.py`, `scripts/migrate_flash_v2.py`, `components/ota/`, `components/factory/FactoryApi.cpp`.

GETTING_STARTED.title: Getting started
GETTING_STARTED.markdown:
# Getting started

The target is `esp32dev` with **8 MB flash**. Verify the actual board and wiring against [LED node](LED_NODE.md). Begin commissioning with outputs disabled and a small known load.

## Build

Install web dependencies first: firmware builds use the embedded asset generator.

```powershell
cd lumigrid-lander-main
npm ci
npm run build:embedded
cd ../LumigridLedNode
pio run -e factory
```

`platformio.ini` pins `espressif32@6.7.0`, with ESP-IDF supplied by that platform. Serial defaults are COM3 and 115200 baud; select the actual port. Read [flash layout](FLASH_LAYOUT.md) before updating an existing device: application-only OTA cannot migrate a partition table.

For a board already on the current layout:

```powershell
pio run -e factory -t upload --upload-port COM_PORT
pio device monitor --port COM_PORT --baud 115200
```

Replace `COM_PORT`. These commands write hardware; they are instructions, not evidence of a completed flash.

## First access

1. Read the serial setup banner: `LumiGrid-Setup`, its generated Wi-Fi key and `http://192.168.4.1`.
2. Join that AP with the displayed key. There is no universal production Wi-Fi password or Admin key.
3. Open the device page and create a permanent Admin Access Key of 16–64 characters. Store it privately.
4. Configure channels, pixel counts/order, load ratings and supply assignments. Inspect validation results.
5. Test one channel at low brightness, then save a scene. Enable only needed protocols.
6. If joining a LAN, choose station/fallback mode, follow apply status and reconnect at the reported address.

Factory-first-boot planning enables API/mDNS while lighting, scheduler and protocols remain off. Provisioning and configured operation are distinct states.

## Daily access

Use the controller's device-hosted page on its network. The external web dashboard is at `/dashboard`. An HTTPS-hosted dashboard may be blocked from contacting the node's HTTP/WS endpoints; open the node page directly when blocked.

If access fails, check power, serial diagnostics, active Wi-Fi and `/api/v1/auth/status`. A provisioned node requires its configured key. Read [Access](ACCESS.md) before using physical recovery.

Sources: `LumigridLedNode/platformio.ini`, `main/LumigridRuntime.cpp`, `components/auth/AuthManager.cpp`, `components/factory/include/RuntimeServices.hpp`; web `src/lib/api/transport.ts`.

HARDWARE_CERTIFICATION.title: Certification workflow
HARDWARE_CERTIFICATION.markdown:
# Certification workflow

LumiGrid's certification service is an internal engineering acceptance workflow, not third-party regulatory certification.

`CertificationPlan.cpp` defines tests, categories, timeouts, evidence sources and per-profile requirement levels. Some tests require observations or external measurements. Read `/api/v1/certification/plan` rather than reusing an old list.

1. Identify actual device/build/topology.
2. Read plan/status, choose the intended profile and inspect required/optional tests.
3. Start the session/test through the UI or API.
4. Perform the requested observation/measurement before submitting results.
5. Inspect failures and abort if target/wiring is wrong.
6. Export `/api/v1/certification/report` with revision and measurement context.

Registered endpoints cover plan, status, start, test/start, test/result, abort and report. Factory tests/burn-in are separate; success there does not satisfy all certification requirements.

Output commands do not prove visible patterns. Power estimates are not current measurements. Logical E-stop is not a physical input: current board flags declare no physical E-stop input or addressable power gate.

## Candidate record and evidence rules

The `1.0.0-rc1` candidate uses plan version 2 and record schema 2: all 46 plan entries fit and their complete IDs are retained. Older records are not accepted as current evidence. Export existing evidence before updating; old reports remain scoped to the image, board and plan that produced them.

Every required test must pass before the session can pass. Pending, running, waiting, skipped, blocked or missing required results leave it incomplete. Instrument results require finite numeric values and matching units; explicitly failed results remain failures even when the number falls within tolerance. Public result submission cannot claim the internal automatic evidence source. Tests without implemented physical/reboot evidence remain blocked.

Persistence errors stop acceptance and leave the session incomplete with `persistence_failed`; export the in-memory report before rebooting. The existing 16 KB NVS partition is shared with configuration and credentials, so capacity must be verified on the intended production configuration. A successful API response alone does not prove recovery after power loss.

Exported `reportingFirmwareVersion` and `reportingFirmwareElfSha256` identify the image generating the report. They do not retrospectively establish the image that collected an older session. Keep the candidate manifest and original board observations alongside each report.

See [firmware candidate and bench gates](FIRMWARE_RELEASE_CANDIDATE.md) for the current software verification scope and hardware acceptance sequence.

Sources: `LumigridLedNode/components/certification/CertificationPlan.cpp`, `CertificationService.cpp`, `CertificationStore.cpp`, `include/CertificationTypes.hpp`, and `components/factory/FactoryApi.cpp`. See [validation checklist](HARDWARE_VALIDATION.md).

HARDWARE_VALIDATION.title: Hardware validation
HARDWARE_VALIDATION.markdown:
# Hardware validation

Source inspection proves implementation, host tests prove their model, and API success is a software observation. Electrical/installation acceptance requires actual measurements.

Record Git SHA plus dirty changes, build environment, artifact hash, board revision, flash size, supplies, loads/counts, wiring, network and instruments. Keep credentials/private backups out of reports.

| Area | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| First boot | Generated AP access, Admin creation, outputs off before configuration |
| Reset/recovery | Measured /OE/data behavior during power-up and reboot |
| Addressable | A1–A8 mapping, order, intended count, crosstalk |
| PWM | P1–P8 stepped duty and /OE inhibit |
| Combined | Intended RMT/PWM topology with Wi-Fi/protocol activity |
| Power | Actual supply/load alongside complete/partial/unknown estimates |
| Playback | Transitions, takeover/release, DMX timeout, cues/timelines |
| Multi-node | Matching manifests, measured timing, loss/reconnect |
| Storage/OTA | Backup/restore, rejection, boot verification/rollback |
| Endurance | Sustained load, memory/stack/reset/transport counters |

Record PASS, FAIL or NOT_RUN with evidence. Missing observations are not passes. Historical logs retain only their original scope.

Tools include factory/certification dashboards, corresponding API families, diagnostics and `scripts/hardware_coexistence_soak.py`. Review target/arguments before running; these tools can change outputs.

No new flashing or device measurements are claimed by this documentation change. See [certification](HARDWARE_CERTIFICATION.md).

LED_NODE.title: LED node hardware contract
LED_NODE.markdown:
# LED node hardware contract

The firmware targets ESP32 `esp32dev` with 8 MB flash. Its canonical topology is 16 channels: A1–A8 addressable and P1–P8 independent PWM dimmers. The PCA9685 has more chip outputs than the eight exposed by LumiGrid.

| Output | GPIO / interface |
| --- | --- |
| A1 | GPIO16 |
| A2 | GPIO4 |
| A3 | GPIO17 |
| A4 | GPIO18 |
| A5 | GPIO19 |
| A6 | GPIO23 |
| A7 | GPIO26 |
| A8 | GPIO27 |
| PCA9685 SDA / SCL | GPIO21 / GPIO22 |
| PCA9685 address | `0x55` (A0, A2, A4 high) |
| Active-low /OE | GPIO25 |

WS2812 accepts RGB/GRB; SK6812 accepts RGBW/GRBW. `MAX_FIXTURE_PIXELS` is 256. Topology admission also checks memory: a schema maximum does not promise every combination or fixed frame rate. Addressable output uses RMT; legacy SPI enum entries are not a supported new hardware family.

PWM outputs are independent dimmers. Compound RGB/RGBW fixture values remain for migration, not new configurations. Indices 0–7 mean A1–A8; 8–15 mean P1–P8. Group masks use those positions.

## Electrical boundaries

Early board safety holds /OE high and addressable data low. PWM enable depends on initialization and safe output state. Board flags report **no physical E-stop input** and **no addressable power gate**. Software blackout does not disconnect strip power.

Supply ratings, voltage, wiring, fusing, level conversion and environmental suitability must be established for the actual assembly. Power telemetry is modeled; see [configuration](CONFIGURATION.md).

Sources: `LumigridLedNode/components/board/include/lg_board_pins.hpp`, `board/BoardOutputSafety.cpp`, `config/include/OutputCapabilities.hpp`, `config/include/SignageTypes.hpp`, and `output/`.

PCA9685_BRINGUP.title: PCA9685 bring-up
PCA9685_BRINGUP.markdown:
# PCA9685 bring-up

Current transport is legacy synchronous ESP-IDF `driver/i2c.h`, `I2C_NUM_0`, using `i2c_master_write_to_device` and `i2c_master_write_read_device`. New-driver I2C APIs are rejected by the invariant policy.

SDA is GPIO21, SCL GPIO22, address `0x55` (A0/A2/A4 high), active-low /OE GPIO25. LumiGrid exposes eight independent PWM channels P1–P8.

1. Keep /OE inhibited and loads safely limited while checking board power/wiring.
2. Build current `factory` and verify expected pin/address constants.
3. Inspect startup and `/api/v1/diagnostics/output` for initialization/errors/state.
4. Configure one PWM channel with its load rating and test bounded stepped duty.
5. Measure duty and inhibit externally, then repeat across P1–P8 with addressable/Wi-Fi activity.
6. Record reboot, communication failure and recovery behavior.

I2C acknowledgement proves bus response, not correct duty or load behavior. A register write, host test or old boot log is not current physical acceptance.

Sources: `LumigridLedNode/components/output/Pca9685Driver.cpp`, `OutputController.cpp`, `components/board/BoardOutputSafety.cpp`, `include/lg_board_pins.hpp`, `scripts/check_invariants.py`.

PROTOCOLS.title: Protocols
PROTOCOLS.markdown:
# Protocols

## HTTP and live state

The node serves HTTP `/api/v1/` and `/ws`. The capability manifest advertises HTTP API 1 and WebSocket 2. No SSE stream is registered in the current route table. See [API reference](API_REFERENCE.md) rather than assuming old `/json`, `/edit`, `/update` routes.

Browser sessions and single-use WS tickets are described in [Access](ACCESS.md). HTTPS browser contexts may block plain HTTP/WS node access.

## Art-Net and sACN

Both receivers are implemented and off by default. `DmxRouter` maps channels/zones, handles ownership/timeouts and HTP/LTP merging. Defaults: 2000 ms timeout, live layer 2. Addressable patching supports wash/direct pixels; PWM channels are independent dimmers. Validate universe/channel ranges through the config API.

Discovery/subscriptions follow active configuration. Protocol implementation does not certify every console or maximum network load.

## Node sync

`NodeSync` uses UDP 6455, packet version 6, eight peers, nominal 100 ms interval and 50 ms during manual crossfade. Roles: Auto, Master, Worker. Sync requires configuration and a connected station on the shared LAN.

Scene/timeline/cue transport reports missing/mismatched content. Deploy matching content and inspect show manifests/status. Packet intervals are not measured phase error or guaranteed timing. Validate network loss and reconnect behavior physically.

## Discovery

mDNS discovery has 32 node slots, distinct from eight sync peers. Queries run every 10 seconds; sightings are online up to 20 seconds and stale up to 60 seconds. Presence does not grant control authority.

## MQTT

With MQTT enabled and a broker configured, `MqttService` publishes `<prefix>/state`, `<prefix>/event`, retained `<prefix>/availability`, and subscribes to `<prefix>/command`. Availability uses online/offline plus a retained last will. Periodic state is configured at 60 seconds; the runtime supplies prefix and command callback.

The reviewed service does not wire dedicated username/password or certificate provisioning. Do not describe it as a secured cloud fleet service. Validate broker/command integration separately.

Sources: `LumigridLedNode/components/protocols/`, `sync/NodeSync.cpp`, `sync/include/NodeSync.hpp`, `discovery/include/FleetDiscoveryService.hpp`, `network/MqttService.cpp`, and `main/LumigridRuntime.cpp`.
