RUNTIME_MEMORY_BUDGET.title: Runtime memory
RUNTIME_MEMORY_BUDGET.markdown:
# Runtime memory

The runtime distinguishes free 8-bit heap, largest 8-bit block, internal heap, DMA heap and minimum-ever heap. A single free-heap number cannot prove an RMT or JSON allocation will succeed.

`RuntimeMemory.hpp` declares setup/normal/max-topology targets, not measurements. The default post-topology/operation reserve is 16 KiB. Admission requires remaining total capacity and a sufficiently large contiguous block; output allocation also has internal-memory constraints.

Heavy operations may return `insufficient_runtime_memory`. Inspect diagnostics and reduce topology/competing work rather than retrying blindly. Factory/network-apply workers are lazy; setup suppresses unnecessary services.

Use `/api/v1/diagnostics/memory`, `/api/v1/health`, output and serial diagnostics. Counters include allocation failures, active services and task stack watermarks. The pinned Xtensa port's stack watermark units are bytes; do not apply a generic word-size multiplier.

Policy lives in `scripts/boot_memory_policy.json`, `check_invariants.py`, `verify_boot_stack.py`, `audit_runtime_hardening_stack.py` under `LumigridLedNode/`. ELF audits apply to that build only. Hardware acceptance needs setup/idle/full-topology/DMX/reconnect/heavy-operation measurements with exact revision and load context.

Sources: `LumigridLedNode/components/factory/include/RuntimeMemory.hpp`, `RuntimeMemory.cpp`, `components/output/OutputController.cpp`, `main/LumigridRuntime.cpp`. No fresh hardware memory measurements accompany this rewrite.

SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.title: Source-of-truth audit
SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.markdown:
# Source-of-truth audit

Audit date: 2026-10-21. Baseline `8afd6f04eb9fed6db82af102db07bfbed3e120ed`, branch `codex/lg-p0-boot-001`. Origin was fetched; main was already an ancestor, four commits behind. Pre-existing OutputController.cpp/.hpp edits were preserved and included in working-tree inspection. This is not hardware qualification.

The effect/palette capacity row below follows the current catalogue. The audit findings retain the baseline and evidence scope above.

| Public fact | Authority under firmware components | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 addressable + 8 PWM | config/include/OutputCapabilities.hpp, board/include/lg_board_pins.hpp | Eight independent dimmers, not all PCA chip outputs |
| WS2812 RGB / SK6812 RGBW | config/include/SignageTypes.hpp, output/ | Correct order/wiring and memory admission |
| 32 scenes, 8 zones, 3 layers | config/include/Capabilities.hpp, SignageTypes.hpp | Capacity, not throughput |
| 16 timeline steps; 8 × 16 cues | Same headers, scheduler/, show/ | Valid matching content |
| 24 effects, 14 palettes | config/include/SignageTypes.hpp: signage_effect_metadata and signage_palette_metadata; signage/EffectRenderer.cpp | Per-effect controls and PWM suitability; see [Effects](EFFECTS.md) |
| Local control | factory/FactoryApi.cpp, web API/embedded sources | HTTP/WS browser restrictions |
| Art-Net/sACN | protocols/, service planner | Disabled by default |
| Node sync | sync/NodeSync.cpp, RuntimeServices.hpp | Shared LAN, no accuracy guarantee |
| Startup scene loading | signage/SceneManager.cpp | Saved scene, slot zero, then blackout fallback |
| Power budget | signage/PowerBudget.cpp | Estimate, not sensor |
| OTA/rollback | post_ota, ota/ | Suitable layout/image and boot health |
| Certification tools | certification/ | Internal evidence workflow |

## Public corrections

The old landing page mixed capabilities with unsupported installation/support commitments, generic installation images, testimonials and absolute reliability/synchronization/flicker claims. Current content describes implemented workflows and links to guides. Preorder structured data is removed because source does not establish a commercial offer.

The old docs index linked missing Node Family, Embedded Integration, StyleSystem and Contributing pages. Its reader used deployment-relative filesystem paths and lacked a page loader. Current docs are bundled from the shared source with deterministic pages and validated links.

## Open gaps

- At the audit baseline, `kFeatureSignedOta` was true without established signature enforcement. The 2026-10-23 candidate now derives this flag from `CONFIG_SECURE_SIGNED_ON_UPDATE`; the default build correctly reports false. A signed production provisioning/update process remains open. See [candidate evidence](FIRMWARE_RELEASE_CANDIDATE.md).
- MQTT lacks a dedicated broker credential/certificate provisioning workflow in the reviewed service.
- Browser flasher referenced an absent release manifest; the page now explains installation prerequisites.
- Physical timing, combined-load endurance, electrical/thermal behavior and current-revision OTA recovery require target evidence.
- Historical reports remain scoped to their original build/context.
- At the audit baseline, the strict API-boundary audit found direct storage access in `src/lib/fleet/registry.ts` and `src/lib/auth/nodeAuth.ts`. The 2026-11-01 continuity batch moves those accesses behind guarded `auth/storage.ts` helpers, including session-only credential storage. The strict audit now passes; denied browser persistence is covered by the auth/storage regressions.

Change source first, then guides/translations. Regenerate/check docs to detect route/capacity drift. Record fresh hardware evidence separately instead of rewriting an older report as though rerun.

UI.title: Dashboard and public site
UI.markdown:
# Dashboard and public site

The controller serves its embedded dashboard at `/`, `/index.html`, `/dashboard`. Edit `lumigrid-lander-main/embedded/dashboard.html`; `npm run build:embedded` and the firmware pre-build hook generate compressed C++ assets. It is not the compiled Svelte dashboard.

## External dashboard

Svelte routes cover channels, live control, scenes, timeline, cues, schedule, sync, firmware, factory, certification, diagnostics, thermal, uptime, preview and visualizer. A route's existence does not establish a hardware sensor. Read connected-node capabilities and runtime state.

The current thermal page explicitly reports that a temperature sensor is unavailable on this hardware/configuration. It is not a functioning temperature-monitoring claim.

Select/login to a node, configure channels, save a scene and inspect actual output status. Accepted, applied and failed command states are distinct. Preview pixels are UI representations, not electrical/photometric measurements.

On current nodes, scene authoring exposes all 16 outputs: addressable A1–A8 and independent PWM dimmers P1–P8, with three layers per channel. Effect and palette controls follow the connected node's catalogue. Changing a PWM layer's Intensity updates its opacity while preserving its RGB colors; the output remains a single dimmer. See [Effects and playback](EFFECTS.md) for parameters, palette choices, and the scene-save payload limits.

API calls belong in `src/lib/api/`. `nodeStore.ts` owns WS/snapshots; `commandTracker.ts` reconciles commands; `src/lib/auth/storage.ts` contains storage access. Cue/timeline editors separate documents from playback state.

The storage boundary is not fully consolidated: `auth/nodeAuth.ts` also uses session storage and `fleet/registry.ts` accesses local storage. The strict cross-project audit reports these existing exceptions. Routes themselves do not directly access storage.

Firmware uses HTTP/WS; `transport.ts` constructs those schemes and reports blocked HTTPS-to-local requests. Open the device page when an HTTPS browser context blocks direct control.

## Public content

The landing page describes implemented workflows and bounded capacities. It does not promise installation contracts, testimonials, flicker certification, sync accuracy, environmental ratings or a firmware release. Documentation is built from root guides, with historical material labeled separately.

Sources: web `src/routes/dashboard/`, `src/lib/api/scenes.ts`, `src/lib/api/transport.ts`, `src/lib/state/`, `src/lib/auth/`, `embedded/dashboard.html`; firmware `FactoryApi::serve_dashboard`.

history/2026-10-21/ACCESS.title: LumiGrid access reference
history/2026-10-21/ACCESS.markdown:
> Historical document preserved on 2026-10-21. Use the [current documentation](../../README.md) for current behavior. Results below apply only to their recorded revision.

# LumiGrid access reference

| Situation | Access |
| --- | --- |
| First boot | Connect `LumiGrid-Setup`, Wi-Fi password printed on serial console (random per-device), open `http://192.168.4.1`. Create and confirm a new 16–64 character Admin Access Key. |
| Initial bootstrap | `POST /api/v1/auth/bootstrap` is state-gated: open only on unprovisioned nodes (`bootstrapAllowed == true`). No universal password, no MAC-derived secret. |
| Normal login | Enter the permanent Node Access Key in the dashboard; the node returns a browser session. |
| Recovery | Existing permanent keys and deliberate recovery policy apply. No universal setup authentication on provisioned nodes. |
| Factory reset | Physical BOOT/GPIO 0 hold for five seconds, then release to reboot. Erases access/configuration/network settings and restores genuine first boot. |

## Roles

- **Administrator:** controller ownership, network setup, access keys and maintenance.
- **Installer:** installation and configuration operations allowed by the node.
- **Operator:** normal show/lighting operation allowed by the node.

Administrator can change the Admin key, create/change Installer and Operator
keys, and disable Installer or Operator. All permanent keys require 16–64
characters. Rotation invalidates affected sessions; Admin rotation invalidates
all browser sessions. Secrets are never displayed after saving.

## Credentials and tokens

| Name | Meaning | Usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Access Key | Permanent role credential | Dashboard login or `X-API-Key` header for automation. Keep private. Never put it in a URL. |
| Session Token | Temporary browser token | `Authorization: Bearer <session-token>`. Memory/sessionStorage only. 30-minute idle timeout and eight-hour absolute timeout. |
| WS Ticket | Internal one-use WebSocket credential | Authenticated `POST /api/v1/auth/ws-ticket`; consumed on connection, expires after 15 seconds. The dashboard handles it internally. |

Bootstrap is a state-gated one-time commissioning path. Admin creation issues
the permanent Admin session in the same request. Once provisioned, bootstrap is
closed. Wi-Fi failure, reboot, configuration errors and OTA rollback do not reopen it.

For step-by-step setup, see [GETTING_STARTED.md](GETTING_STARTED.md).

history/2026-10-21/API_REFERENCE.title: LumiGrid LED Node API
history/2026-10-21/API_REFERENCE.markdown:
> Historical document preserved on 2026-10-21. Use the [current documentation](../../README.md) for current behavior. Results below apply only to their recorded revision.

# LumiGrid LED Node API

> **Status:** **IMPLEMENTED** (Unless explicitly marked as PLANNED, PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED, or CONCEPTUAL)

The LED Node exposes an HTTP API on port 80 and serves the operator dashboard at
`/`. All API responses are JSON and include `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## API Contracts and Constraints

The node strictly enforces memory budgets to ensure ESP32 stability. Clients must respect these constraints:
- Normal API response size: `< 8 KB`
- Large diagnostic response size: `< 16 KB`
- Backup payload size: `< 32 KB`
- WebSocket frame size: `< 4 KB`
- Incoming JSON request body size: `< 8 KB`

## Authentication & Authorization (LG-029)

LumiGrid uses node-authoritative authentication. The node is the sole authority for credentials, session lifecycle, and role assignment.

### Transport Security Limitation

> [!WARNING]
> **Transport Security Limitation:**
> HTTP on an untrusted LAN does not provide confidentiality against packet interception. Bearer tokens and API keys transmitted over plaintext HTTP are susceptible to network eavesdropping on an untrusted or open network. Production deployments requiring transport encryption require dedicated network isolation or future TLS capabilities.

### Accepted Credentials

1. **Browser / Web Dashboard Session:**
   ```http
   Authorization: Bearer <session-token>
   ```
   Ephemeral 256-bit random token issued by `POST /api/v1/auth/session`. Valid for 30 minutes of idle time, with an absolute 8-hour timeout.

2. **Machine / Automation API Key:**
   ```http
   X-API-Key: <long-lived-credential>
   ```
   Direct persistent credential for automated tools and scripts.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Query parameter tokens (`?token=`, `?auth=`) and legacy headers (`X-Auth-Token`) are strictly rejected by the node firmware.

### Role Hierarchy

Endpoints enforce the following role hierarchy:
- **Admin**: Full control (firmware OTA, backup/restore, network settings, credential management, factory recovery).
- **Installer**: Diagnostics, health, logs, channel bench testing, factory output tests.
- **Operator**: Read status, trigger scene presets, manual override, timeline and cue controls, read network/diagnostics.
- **Public**: Dashboard static assets, `GET /api/v1/info`, `GET /api/v1/auth/status`, `POST /api/v1/auth/bootstrap` (unprovisioned only), `POST /api/v1/auth/session`.

### Authentication Endpoints

| Method | Path | Min Role | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/auth/status` | Public | Check if node is provisioned and if bootstrap is allowed. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/auth/bootstrap` | Public (Unprovisioned only) | Provision initial Admin access key (16–64 characters). |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/auth/session` | Public | Authenticate node credential to open an ephemeral session. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/auth/session` | Operator+ | Authoritative check of current session role and time-to-live. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/auth/session` | Operator+ | Invalidate current session (logout). |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/auth/ws-ticket` | Operator+ | Generate a single-use, 15-second ticket for WebSocket handshake. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/auth/credentials` | Admin | Query configured credential roles (no secrets exposed). |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/auth/credentials` | Admin | Rotate a role credential (invalidates associated sessions). |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/auth/credentials` | Admin | Disable an Installer or Operator credential. |

### WebSocket Authentication

The live telemetry WebSocket (`/ws`) requires pre-handshake ticket validation:
1. Client requests ticket: `POST /api/v1/auth/ws-ticket` with `Authorization: Bearer <session>`
2. Client opens WebSocket passing ticket in subprotocol:
   ```ts
   new WebSocket(wsUrl, [`lumigrid-ticket.${ticket}`]);
   ```
3. Firmware validates and consumes the ticket during pre-handshake. Unauthorized connections are rejected.

Errors use this shape:

```json
{ "error": "invalid_credentials" }
```

`400` denotes invalid input, `401` authentication failure / session expired, `403` insufficient role permissions, `409` conflict / state rejection, `429` rate limiting (failed logins), and `503` subsystem unready.

## Operator endpoints

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/status` | Read canonical Schema 3 runtime snapshot (identical to WebSocket state). |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/dmx/frame` | Read on-demand raw 512-channel DMX universe frame (Installer+). |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/channels` | Read all 16 physical output channels (A1–A8 and P1–P8). |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/channel/test` | Test or identify a specific physical channel connector. |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/manual` | Apply live manual control override frame across 16 physical channels. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/manual` | Release live manual control override lease. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/presets` | List stored scene presets (or `?index=N` for singular preset fetch). |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/presets` | Save a scene preset in slot 0–31. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/presets` | Free/delete a scene preset in slot 0–31 (via `?index=N`). |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/activate` | Activate a preset. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/effects` | Read display names, descriptions, and controls for each effect. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/sequence` | Read the 16-channel, 16-step timeline. |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/sequence` | Save the timeline. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/config` | Read persisted node settings. |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/config` | Update persisted node settings. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/schedules` | List calendar automation cues. |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/schedules` | Replace all calendar automation cues. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/show/control` | Control unified Show Transport (Scene, Timeline, Cue) with leader authority. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/show/status` | Read unified Show Transport runtime status and mode. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/cue-lists` | List saved Cue Lists (index, name, mode, count, end action, checksum) (LG-034). |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/cue-list` | Read one Cue List document (schema 2, includes checksum and per-cue timing) via `?index=N`. |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/cue-list` | Strictly validate and save a Cue List (schema 2, optimistic checksum concurrency). |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/cue-list` | Delete a Cue List via `?index=N`; blocked with 409 while referenced by the active transport or schedules. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/scene-motion` | Delete motion tracks for a scene preset (via `?index=N`). |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/sync` | Read sync role, clock health, transport, master address, and discovered followers. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/fleet/nodes` | Read discovered fleet nodes table and self identity via mDNS. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/show-manifest` | Read compact CRC32 show manifest, playbackHash, and scheduleHash. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/health` | Read system memory, uptime, and telemetry. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/logs` | Read recent diagnostic logs. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/audit` | Read recent security and configuration events. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/backup` | Export node configuration and presets as JSON. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/restore` | Import configuration from JSON and reboot. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/ota` | Upload new firmware binary and reboot. |

### Activate a preset

```http
POST /api/v1/activate
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "preset": 2
}
```

The preset index must be between 0 and 31.

When the running lighting runtime accepts and loads the requested preset, the
endpoint returns:

```http
202 Accepted
```

```json
{
  "accepted": true,
  "preset": 2,
  "generation": 41
}
```

`accepted` means the request was accepted by the lighting runtime. It does not
claim that a physical output frame has already been committed to the hardware,
and a higher-priority live control source may still temporarily own the output.

If the scene cannot be activated — for example because the preset cannot be
loaded or the lighting runtime is not in an accepting state — the endpoint
returns:

```http
409 Conflict
```

```json
{
  "error": "scene_activation_rejected"
}
```

The `generation` value identifies this accepted scene request. Clients can
compare it with `appliedGeneration` from `/api/v1/status`. The request is
physically acknowledged only when `appliedGeneration >= generation`.

`/api/v1/status` also exposes `requestedPreset`, `requestedGeneration`,
`appliedGeneration`, and `sceneApplyPending`. A generation advances to
applied only after the render path successfully commits a frame through the
hardware output transaction. If output faults, the generation remains pending
and `outputFault` reports the failure.

Clients must therefore use node telemetry rather than treating the `202`
response itself as hardware acknowledgement.

### Scenes and effects

`GET /api/v1/effects` is the canonical effect metadata source for clients. Each
item includes an effect `id`, a human-readable `label` and `description`, and,
where applicable, a parameter label, unit, range, and default. Clients should
use this endpoint rather than exposing the internal `fxParam` name.

`PUT /api/v1/presets` accepts a scene `index`, `name`, `brightness` (0–255),
`transitionMs`, and up to eight channel definitions. A channel accepts `r`,
`g`, `b`, `pwmDuty` (0–4095), `effect`, `effectSpeedMs`, `fxParam`,
`pixelEnabled`, and `pwmEnabled`.

Scenes can also add one preset-wide finishing layer:

```json
{
  "overlayEffect": "strobe",
  "overlaySpeedMs": 0,
  "overlayParam": 50
}
```

`overlayEffect` is `none` or `strobe`. `overlaySpeedMs: 0` follows the
sequencer beat; otherwise it is the flash period in milliseconds.

### Live manual control (`/api/v1/manual`)

Live Desk v1 (LG-024) introduces non-persistent, lease-bound manual override across all 16 physical channels (channels 0–7 addressable A1–A8, 8–15 PWM P1–P8).

#### Apply manual control frame

```http
PUT /api/v1/manual
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: ******
```

```json
{
  "leaseMs": 15000,
  "channels": [
    { "index": 0, "r": 255, "g": 128, "b": 0, "brightness": 255 },
    { "index": 8, "pwm": 3072 }
  ]
}
```

- **Replacement semantics**: Each `PUT /api/v1/manual` completely replaces the previous manual override frame and active channel mask. It does not merge with prior manual state. Channels omitted from the `channels` array are released from manual control and return to their lower-priority source.
- **Server-derived channel mask**: The firmware derives the active 16-bit channel mask directly from the indices present in the `channels` array. Clients do not specify `channelMask` in the request body.
- **Lease duration**: `leaseMs` is clamped between `1000` and `60000` ms (default: `15000` ms). Overrides automatically expire and fall back to the lower-priority source (CueRunner, Timeline, or active Preset) if heartbeats cease.
- **Channel scoping**: Only channels included in `channels` are acquired or overridden. Unclaimed channels remain in their background playback state.
- **Safety pipeline**: Manual control commands pass through the identical `ColorPipeline`, `max_brightness`, per-channel limits, gamma calibration, global `PowerBudget`, and `OutputScheduler` transactions. Safety limits cannot be bypassed.
- **Authorization**: Requires `Operator` or `Admin` role (`403 Forbidden` if unprivileged).
- **Arbitration priority**:
  1. `EmergencyStop` (highest)
  2. `Factory` (bench/burn-in tests)
  3. `LiveDmx` (Art-Net / sACN)
  4. `ManualOverride` (Live Desk v1)
  5. `CueRunner` (playlist/cue execution)
  6. `Timeline` (step sequencer)
  7. `SavedScene` (default background scene)

Response:
```json
{
  "accepted": true,
  "channelMask": 257,
  "leaseMs": 15000
}
```
The response `channelMask` reflects the exact mask acquired by firmware (`257` = `0x0101` for channels 0 and 8). Clients must verify that this matches their requested mask, failing closed on any discrepancy.

#### Release manual control

```http
DELETE /api/v1/manual
Authorization: ******
```

Response:
```json
{
  "released": true
}
```

`DELETE /api/v1/manual` releases the complete `ManualOverride` control source state on the node, returning all previously overridden channels to background playback immediately without waiting for lease expiration. It does not accept a payload. Other control sources (such as `LiveDmx` or `Factory`) remain entirely unaffected.

### Timeline

The timeline contains 16 independently enabled tracks corresponding to the 16 physical output channels (A1–A8 addressable, P1–P8 PWM) with up to 16 ordered steps per track. A step has `presetIndex` (0–31) and `lengthBeats` (1–64). `bpm` is constrained to 10–500 and `enabled` controls manual playback.

### Device configuration

`GET /api/v1/config` returns canonical node settings:
- Node metadata: `deviceName`, `activePreset`, `fallbackPreset`, `watchdogTimeoutS`, `maxPowerMw`, `gamma`, `softStart`, `softStartMs`, `timezone`, `syncEnabled`, `syncRole`.
- Physical outputs: `channels` array containing 16 channel objects (`id`, `name`, `type`, `pin`, `maxCurrentMa`, `length`, `groupMask`).
- Groups: `groups` array containing up to 8 group objects (`id`, `name`, `channelMask`, `enabled`).
- For legacy client compatibility, responses also provide `zones` and `ports` alias projections.

`PUT /api/v1/config` updates persisted node configuration. It accepts canonical fields or compatibility aliases, and validates 16-channel and 8-group structures. Persisted configuration writes require the `Admin` role (`403 Forbidden` for `Operator`). Limits are: preset indexes 0–31, watchdog 0–3600 seconds, power 0–60000 mW, soft-start 0–5000 ms, and sync role 0–2.

### Calendar automation

`PUT /api/v1/schedules` accepts up to eight entries. `daysOfWeek` is a
7-bit mask with Sunday at bit 0 and Saturday at bit 6. A `preset` action
activates a scene; a `sequence` action starts the saved timeline at that
minute. A scene action stops a calendar-started timeline.

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "hour": 9,
      "minute": 0,
      "daysOfWeek": 62,
      "action": "sequence",
      "presetIndex": 0,
      "enabled": true
    }
  ]
}
```

### Show Transport v2 Coordinator

`POST /api/v1/show/control` provides explicit transport switching across Scene, Timeline, and Cue List:
```json
{
  "mode": "scene",
  "sceneIndex": 7
}
```
Or for Timeline:
```json
{
  "mode": "timeline",
  "action": "start",
  "bpm": 124
}
```
Or for Cue List:
```json
{
  "mode": "cue",
  "action": "start",
  "cueListIndex": 0,
  "cueIndex": 0
}
```
Supported Cue actions: `start`, `restart`, `stop`, `pause`, `resume`, `next`, `previous`, `jump`, `crossfade`. Every action is deterministic: invalid-state transitions (e.g. pausing a stopped transport, advancing past the final cue) fail with `400`/`409` instead of silently no-oping. Stops are classified with a stop reason (`operator`, `preempted`, `natural_completion`, `sync_lost`); only `natural_completion` executes the configured end action.

`GET /api/v1/show/status` returns unified transport coordinator status:
```json
{
  "mode": "cue",
  "generation": 42,
  "scene": { "index": 0 },
  "timeline": { "running": false, "bpm": 120 },
  "cue": {
    "running": true,
    "state": "fading",
    "pausedFrom": "stopped",
    "listIndex": 0,
    "mode": "auto",
    "cueIndex": 3,
    "nextCueIndex": 4,
    "currentSceneIndex": 7,
    "nextSceneIndex": 12,
    "elapsedMs": 450,
    "remainingMs": 1550,
    "manualFade": 0,
    "transitionProgress": 12345,
    "generation": 42,
    "activeChecksum": 9182771,
    "savedChecksum": 9182771,
    "contentStale": false,
    "remoteDriven": false
  }
}
```

#### Follower Read-Only Guard (409 Conflict)
Active followers (`activeRole === 'worker'` tracking a reachable leader) reject local direct playback requests (`POST /api/v1/activate`, `POST /api/v1/cue-control`, `POST /api/v1/show/control`) with:
```json
{
  "error": "sync_follower_read_only",
  "message": "Playback is controlled by sync leader 192.168.1.50",
  "leader": "192.168.1.50"
}
```
Show content editing (`PUT /api/v1/presets`, `PUT /api/v1/sequence`, `PUT /api/v1/cue-list`) remains permitted.

### Cue Lists (LG-034 — Cue Studio v2)

Cue Lists are the playlist/show layer above Scene presets. Persistence and transport are strictly separated: saving a Cue List never mutates the running show.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/cue-lists` | List saved Cue Lists (`index`, `name`, `mode`, `count`, `endAction`, `endActionName`, `checksum`). |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/cue-list?index=N` | Read one Cue List document (schema 2) including per-cue `sceneIndex`, `holdMs`, `fadeMs`, `curve`, and `label`. |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/cue-list` | Strictly validate and save a Cue List document (schema 2). |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/cue-list?index=N` | Delete a Cue List; blocked with 409 while referenced. |

#### Document model (schema 2)

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "index": 0,
  "checksum": 9182771,
  "name": "Opening Walk-in",
  "mode": "auto",
  "endAction": "hold_last",
  "cues": [
    { "sceneIndex": 3, "holdMs": 8000, "fadeMs": 1500, "curve": "ease_in_out", "label": "House up" }
  ]
}
```

- `name`: 1..31 UTF-8 bytes; cue `label`: 0..23 UTF-8 bytes; `cues`: 1..16 entries per list; up to 8 lists.
- `mode`: `auto` (hold/fade timed advance) or `manual` (operator T-Bar crossfade).
- `endAction` (`hold_last` | `blackout` | `restore_fallback`): executed **only** on natural completion of the final cue. Operator stops, preemptions (scene/timeline activation), and sync loss never trigger the end action.
- Strict validation rejects out-of-range timing (`holdMs` 0..3600000, `fadeMs` 0..60000), unknown curves/modes, overlong UTF-8 content, and missing scene references (`400 cue_scene_missing` with `cueIndex`/`sceneIndex`).

#### Save/run separation & optimistic concurrency

- `PUT /api/v1/cue-list` never starts, stops, or alters running playback. RUN snapshots the latest saved list into an immutable active copy with its own checksum and transport generation.
- Pass `expectedChecksum` to guard against concurrent edits; a mismatch returns `409 cue_list_conflict` with `currentChecksum` (keep-draft/reload is the client's decision).
- While the active snapshot diverges from the saved list, telemetry reports `contentStale: true`; `POST /api/v1/show/control` with `action: "restart"` re-snapshots the saved version without executing an end action.

#### Deletion protection

`DELETE /api/v1/cue-list` returns `409 cue_list_in_use` with a `references[]` array while the list is the active cue transport (`{"type":"activeTransport"}`) or referenced by a calendar schedule (`{"type":"schedule","index":N}`).

#### Cue transport telemetry

`GET /api/v1/show/status` `cue` (and `transport.cue` in `GET /api/v1/status`) reports: `running`, `state`, `pausedFrom`, `listIndex`, `mode`, `cueIndex`, `nextCueIndex`, `currentSceneIndex`, `nextSceneIndex`, `elapsedMs`, `remainingMs`, `manualFade` (Q15), `transitionProgress` (Q15), `generation`, `activeChecksum`, `savedChecksum`, `contentStale`, and `remoteDriven`. Pausing freezes hold/fade anchors and the in-flight fade; resuming continues the frozen transition over the remaining time with no visual restart.

> The legacy endpoints `POST /api/v1/cue/control` and `GET /api/v1/cue/status` remain as deprecated aliases with identical semantics; clients should migrate to `/api/v1/show/control` and `/api/v1/show/status`.

### Sync Health, Topology, and NodeSync Protocol v6

`GET /api/v1/sync` returns:
- `protocolVersion`: `6` (NodeSync v6 with packed 76-byte payload).
- `configuredRole`: `auto`, `master`, or `worker`.
- `activeRole`: Currently resolved role (`auto`, `master`, or `worker`).
- `running`: Boolean indicating if NodeSync UDP background task is active.
- `groupLabel`: Configured cluster group label.
- `syncEnabled`: Boolean indicating if multi-node sync is enabled.
- `clockLocked`: Boolean indicating bounded clock offset lock (< 5 ms).
- `clockHasEpoch`: Boolean indicating valid epoch reference.
- `masterAddress`: IPv4 string of the current leader node (or null for the leader itself).
- `transport`: Active playback transport mode (`standalone`, `scene`, `timeline`, `cue`).
- `transportGeneration`: Monotonic generation counter of the leader's transport commands.
- `transportApplyOk`: Boolean indicating if follower successfully applied remote transport state.
- `transportError`: Error string if follower failed to apply remote transport (`none`, `scene_missing`, `cue_list_missing`, `cue_index_invalid`, `runtime_unavailable`, `unsupported_transport`, `timeline_mismatch`, `timeline_invalid`, `cue_list_mismatch`).
- `remoteBpm`: Remote BPM broadcast from leader during timeline transport (or null).
- `remoteTimelineEnabled`: Boolean indicating if leader's timeline sequence is active.
- `cue`: Active cue playback telemetry (`listIndex`, `state`, `cueIndex`, `nextCueIndex`, `generation`, `elapsedMs`, `manualFadeQ15`).
- `peerCount`, `packetsReceived`, `packetsMissed`, `clockOffsetMs`, `clockJitterUs`.
- `peers[]`: List of acknowledged peers with address, ageMs, and latencyMs.

### Show Manifest and Content Parity

`GET /api/v1/show-manifest` returns compact content CRC32 checksums under schema 2:
```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "firmware": "0.10.0",
  "protocol": 4,
  "playbackHash": 182930411,
  "scheduleHash": 7174411,
  "showHash": 2851193042,
  "scenes": [
    { "index": 0, "checksum": 182736455, "motionChecksum": 98233441 }
  ],
  "timeline": { "checksum": 33182761 },
  "cueLists": [
    { "index": 0, "checksum": 9182771 }
  ],
  "schedules": { "checksum": 7174411 }
}
```
- `playbackHash`: Deterministic CRC32 computed across real-time playback assets (Scenes, Scene Motion tracks, Timeline sequence, and Cue Lists). Parity of `playbackHash` is required for cluster synchronization readiness.
- `scheduleHash`: CRC32 of calendar automation cues. Schedule divergence between nodes is considered optional and does not block cluster playback.
- `showHash`: Aggregate hash across all assets including calendar schedules.
- Hardware configuration (IP, Wi-Fi, channel mapping, brightness limits) is strictly separated and does not affect show hashes.

### Show Deployment Rules
- Show deployment distributes Show content (Scenes, Motions, Timeline, Cue Lists, and optional Schedules) from a source node to target nodes via sequential HTTP requests (`GET source` -> `PUT target`).
- **Never** uses `/api/v1/backup` or `/api/v1/restore` for Show deployment to avoid overwriting node hardware, networking, or credentials.
- When `mirrorExactly` is enabled:
  - Stale presets are deleted with `DELETE /api/v1/presets?index=N`.
  - Stale motion tracks are deleted with `DELETE /api/v1/scene-motion?index=N`.
  - Stale cue lists are deleted with `DELETE /api/v1/cue-list?index=N`.
- **Synchronized Cue Playback**: Under Show Transport v2 and NodeSync v6, live Cue playback is fully synchronized over UDP across the cluster. The Leader runs the authoritative cue list timing and crossfades, broadcasting cue indices, hold/fade states, paused-from phase, transition progress, and manual crossfade progress to all follower nodes at 10 Hz. Followers suppress local conflicting playback, render matching frames locked to the cluster clock, and fail closed with `cue_list_mismatch` when their local Cue List checksum diverges from the leader's.

### Diagnostics and Logs

`GET /api/v1/health` returns system telemetry including uptime, free heap memory, minimum free heap memory, tasks statistics, and other diagnostic data useful for monitoring node stability.

`GET /api/v1/logs` streams the last N lines of system logs (if the RAM-based log sink is enabled). It is useful for debugging connection or sync issues without attaching a serial monitor.

`GET /api/v1/audit` returns the ring-buffer of security and configuration changes. It includes timestamps, roles (e.g. `Admin`), event types (e.g. `ConfigUpdate`, `AuthFailure`), and descriptive messages.

### Firmware & Configuration Management

`GET /api/v1/backup` aggregates the current `DeviceConfig` (including network, tokens, physical outputs, and zones) and all 32 `SceneConfig` presets (including all 8 zones and 3 layers per zone) into a v2 JSON file downloaded as an attachment.

`POST /api/v1/restore` accepts a JSON payload in v2 or v1 format. It parses the JSON, updates the configuration and presets, logs an `Audit` event, and automatically restarts the node.

`POST /api/v1/ota` accepts a signed `.bin` firmware file via multipart or raw binary stream. The firmware is written to the alternate OTA partition. If successful, the node reboots into the new firmware. Note that the node will attempt to validate the new firmware upon boot and rollback if a crash occurs during early initialization.

### Protocol Configuration

The node supports incoming DMX streams via Art-Net and sACN.
`liveStreamLayer` in `protocol` configuration determines which layer (0–2, default: 2) incoming DMX color data is injected into across configured channels.

## Factory vs Signage Effects Boundary

The system operates two separate effect engines:
1. **Signage Effects (`/api/v1/effects`, `/api/v1/presets`)**: Production signage pipeline supporting multi-channel multi-layer blending (Solid, Breathe, Chase, Sweep, Reveal, Sparkle, Gradient, Fire, Aurora, ColorWave, StaticPulse).
2. **Factory Effects (`/api/v1/factory/effect`)**: Hardware diagnostic test routines time-bounded by the firmware for factory quality control and wiring validation (`identity`, `pixel_chase`, `rainbow`, `white_walk`, `pwm_walk`, `pwm_fade`, `combined_pulse`, `burn_in`, `blackout`).

> [!NOTE]
> Operational live faders and interactive manual overrides must use `PUT /api/v1/manual` and `DELETE /api/v1/manual`. The `/api/v1/factory/*` endpoints are strictly reserved for manufacturing bench diagnostics and hardware validation tests.

## Factory endpoints

Factory commands are deliberately time-bounded by the firmware. Their common
success response is `202 {"accepted":true}`.

| Method | Path | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/factory/status` | — |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/factory/effect` | `effect`, optional `brightness` (0–96), `durationMs` |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/factory/lane` | `lane`, `red`, `green`, `blue`, optional `brightness`, `durationMs` |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/factory/pwm` | `channel`, `duty` (0–4095), optional `durationMs` |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/factory/auto-loop` | `enabled` boolean |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/factory/abort` | — |

Available effects are `identity`, `pixel_chase`, `rainbow`, `white_walk`,
`pwm_walk`, `pwm_fade`, `combined_pulse`, `burn_in`, and `blackout`.
Lanes and PWM channels are numbered 0–7. `durationMs` must be a positive value
not greater than the firmware factory-test maximum.

`POST /api/v1/factory/abort` immediately queues a safe blackout and returns:

```json
{ "accepted": true, "action": "blackout" }
```

Connect to `GET /ws` with the WebSocket protocol. The node broadcasts factory
status JSON whenever its state changes. Clients should treat it as read-only and
use the HTTP command endpoints for all writes.

## Network Commissioning & Lifecycle (LG-028)

The node provides an operator-grade commissioning path that allows moving from Factory/Recovery SoftAP to the local LAN without rebooting the lighting runtime, losing active output, exposing passwords, or risking unreachability from a mistyped credential.

### Network Modes

1. **`ap_only`**: Standalone Access Point mode. Node hosts a SoftAP (default `192.168.4.1`) and does not connect to a station LAN.
2. **`sta_only`**: Station-only mode. Node connects to the configured Wi-Fi network. SoftAP is disabled. If connection fails, rollback occurs to the previous configuration.
3. **`sta_with_ap_fallback`**: Station with Recovery AP fallback. Node attempts to join the configured Wi-Fi LAN. If STA connection fails after configured retries, the node automatically spins up a Recovery SoftAP (`192.168.4.1`) in AP+STA mode so operators can reconnect and remediate credentials, while continuing background reconnect attempts with bounded backoff (5s, 10s, 30s, 60s max).

### Credentials & Security Invariants

- **Write-Only Passwords**: Stored Wi-Fi passwords are never returned in `GET /api/v1/network/config`. Responses contain only `"passwordSet": true`.
- **Zero Plaintext Logging**: Credentials are never printed in diagnostic logs, serial console messages, or audit trails.
- **Preservation by Default**: Submitting a blank password field preserves existing credentials. To explicitly clear credentials for an open network, clients must set `"clearPassword": true`.
- **Safe-Mode Locked**: When the node is in Safe/Recovery mode, network configuration is locked (`400 {"error":"safe_mode_network_locked"}`) to guarantee physical recovery access remains available.

### Asynchronous Lifecycle & Sockets Rebind

Reconfiguring Wi-Fi is an asynchronous runtime-owned operation:
1. `PUT /api/v1/network/config` strictly validates parameters (`ssid`, `password`, `apChannel` 1..13, `mode`).
2. If another apply operation is already in flight, returns `409 Conflict` (`{"error":"network_apply_in_progress"}`).
3. Returns `202 Accepted` (`{"accepted":true,"commandId":<id>,"applyPending":true}`) and allows the HTTP response to cleanly escape the socket before reconfiguration begins.
4. Runtime network transition shuts down network-dependent listeners (MQTT, NodeSync, sACN, Art-Net, mDNS, HTTP/API) while keeping `LightingRuntime`, `OutputController`, and active LED output running without interruption (zero blackout).
5. Wi-Fi reconfigures. Once network readiness is confirmed, network services are rebound.
6. The new configuration is persisted to NVS **only after** successful application.
7. **Transactional Rollback**: If the new network fails to achieve readiness, the runtime restores the previous configuration (or stays in recovery AP for `sta_with_ap_fallback`), leaves the previously known-good NVS configuration intact, and marks the command failed.

### Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/network/config` | Operator | Returns current network configuration (`mode`, `ssid`, `passwordSet`, `apName`, `apChannel`). Never returns password. |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/network/config` | Admin | Asynchronously queues a network configuration apply request. Returns `202 Accepted`. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/network/status` | Operator | Returns runtime network telemetry (`state`, `mode`, `staConnected`, `staIp`, `apActive`, `applyState`, `lastApplyError`, `persistedMatchesRuntime`). |

## Fleet Discovery, Presence & Immutable Identity (LG-030)

LumiGrid nodes automatically discover peer nodes on the local network via mDNS Zeroconf. The web dashboard connects to a single node, which queries the local subnet and reports the discovered fleet.

### Stable Immutable Hostname & Zeroconf Service

- **Immutable Hostname**: The node mDNS hostname is permanently derived from its factory-assigned MAC address (`lg-<mac>.local`, e.g. `lg-84f703c29110.local`), ensuring stability across operator renames and avoiding collision.
- **Display Name**: Friendly device names are advertised as the Zeroconf service instance name.
- **Dedicated Service**: Nodes advertise the product-specific Zeroconf service:
  ```text
  _lumigrid._tcp.local.
  ```
- **TXT Record Metadata**:
  - `id`: Immutable node identifier (`lg-84f703c29110`)
  - `family`: Hardware family (`led-node`)
  - `model`: Device model (`lg-led-v1`)
  - `fw`: Firmware version derived authoritatively from `esp_app_get_description()->version`
  - `hw`: Hardware revision (`A`)
  - `api`: HTTP API schema version (`1`)
  - `ws`: WebSocket protocol version (`2`)
  - `auth`: Node-backed authentication schema version (`1`)

### Presence & Reconciliation Contract

- **Reconciliation Key**: Nodes are uniquely keyed by immutable `NodeIdentity.id`. If a node's IP address changes via DHCP renewal, the existing entry is updated in place without duplicate records.
- **Self Exclusion**: Querying nodes exclude their own immutable ID from discovered peer lists.
- **Bounded Table**: Bounded table of 32 nodes max, managed in background worker tasks without blocking HTTP handlers.
- **Presence Timing**:
  - **Online**: `age <= 20s`
  - **Stale**: `20s < age <= 60s`
  - **Offline / Expired**: `age > 60s` (automatically pruned)

### Bootstrap Trust Boundary Guard

Bootstrap (`POST /api/v1/auth/bootstrap`) requires **both**:
1. `auth.provisioned == false`
2. Node is in genuine commissioning/recovery context (`CommissioningState::FactoryFirstBoot` or `CommissioningState::PhysicalRecovery`).

Nodes connected to customer infrastructure STA networks or ordinary LANs return `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "bootstrap_not_allowed"}`) to ensure remote unauthorized claiming cannot occur.

## Canonical Runtime State & API v1 Cutover (LG-031)

LumiGrid control plane maintains **one authoritative runtime-state model**: Schema 3 `RuntimeSnapshot`.

HTTP `GET /api/v1/status` and authenticated WebSocket state streaming (`/ws`) use the **exact same serialized contract**.

```text
Firmware runtime
      ↓
Canonical RuntimeSnapshot v3
      ↓
 ┌───────────────┬─────────────────┐
 │ GET /status   │ authenticated WS │
 └───────────────┴─────────────────┘
          ↓ identical state contract
      nodeStore
          ↓
 Overview / Scenes / Timeline / Cues /
 Live / Factory / Diagnostics / Network
```

### Architectural Invariants

1. **Observational & Side-Effect Free:** Collection and serialization perform zero mutations or bookkeeping transitions. Generation apply acknowledgment occurs strictly in the runtime renderer when frames commit to hardware.
2. **Stream Sequencing Independence:** WebSocket broadcasts include `streamSeq = ++ws_stream_seq` for packet-gap detection. HTTP `/api/v1/status` emits `streamSeq: 0` and does not affect the WebSocket sequence counter.
3. **Bounded Budget:** Serialization uses `FixedJsonWriter` within an 8192-byte max budget. Overflows abort cleanly without transmitting malformed JSON.
4. **Coalesced Broadcasts:** Status notifications utilize atomic CAS (`status_pending_`) collapsing rapid notifications to max 5 Hz.
5. **Decoupled Heavy Data:**
   - Static capabilities are excluded from the live snapshot (`GET /api/v1/capabilities`).
   - 1024-char raw DMX frame data is excluded from generic status (`GET /api/v1/dmx/frame`, role `Installer+`).
   - Binary pixel preview remains on an isolated binary WebSocket channel (header byte `1` or `76`).

### Save Timeline Document

```http

Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "expectedChecksum": 123456,
  "bpm": 120,
  "tracks": [ ... ]
}
```

#### Invariants:
1. **Separation of Persistence and Playback:** Saving a timeline persists content to NVS and recalculates `checksum`. It **never** starts or stops playback, mutates `active_sequence_`, or changes active playback BPM or anchor.
2. **Optimistic Concurrency:** If `expectedChecksum` does not match the stored checksum:
   ```http
   409 Conflict
   ```
   ```json
   {
     "error": "timeline_conflict",
     "currentChecksum": 789012
   }
   ```
3. **Missing Scene Reference Protection:** Every active block must reference an existing scene preset slot (`scene_exists(presetIndex)`). If any active step references a non-existent preset:
   ```http
   400 Bad Request
   ```
   ```json
   {
     "error": "timeline_scene_missing",
     "channel": 4,
     "step": 2,
     "presetIndex": 14
   }
   ```
4. **Successful Response:**
   ```json
   {
     "saved": true,
     "checksum": 789012,
     "commandId": 41
   }
   ```

- `POST /api/v1/certification/test/start`: Admin
- `POST /api/v1/certification/test/result`: Admin
- `POST /api/v1/certification/abort`: Admin

### Get Certification Plan
```http
GET /api/v1/certification/plan
Authorization: Bearer <operator-or-admin-token>
```
Returns active test definitions, profile requirements, tolerances, and required evidence sources (`automatic`, `operator_observation`, `instrument_measurement`).

### Get Certification Status
```http
GET /api/v1/certification/status
Authorization: Bearer <operator-or-admin-token>
```
Returns current session summary, passed/failed/pending/total counts, staleness flag, and individual test progress.

### Start Certification Session
```http
POST /api/v1/certification/start
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "profile": "production_unit",
  "serialNumber": "SN-2026-0042"
}
```

### Start Individual Certification Test
```http
POST /api/v1/certification/test/start
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "testId": "ADDR-A1"
}
```

### Submit Certification Evidence & Result
```http
POST /api/v1/certification/test/result
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "testId": "ADDR-A1",
  "passed": true,
  "evidenceSource": "operator_observation",
  "note": "Only A1 illuminated, chase complete, no flicker"
}
```

For instrument tests:
```http
POST /api/v1/certification/test/result
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "testId": "POWER-LIMIT-001",
  "passed": true,
  "evidenceSource": "instrument_measurement",
  "measuredValue": 3200.0,
  "unit": "mW",
  "note": "Measured with calibrated DC power meter"
}
```

### Abort Certification Session
```http
POST /api/v1/certification/abort
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
```

### Export Certification Report
```http
GET /api/v1/certification/report
Authorization: Bearer <operator-or-admin-token>
```
Returns a comprehensive JSON report containing all test evidence, measurements, attempt counts, and burn-in metrics. Never includes credentials, tokens, or Wi-Fi passwords.

history/2026-10-21/ARCHITECTURE.markdown:

# LumiGrid Architecture

> **Status:** **IMPLEMENTED** (Unless explicitly marked as PLANNED, PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED, or CONCEPTUAL)

The LumiGrid ecosystem consists of modular nodes designed for robust, real-time lighting control. Currently, the **LED Node** is the canonical implementation and the focus of the system.

## High-Level Topology

```mermaid
graph TD
    UI[LumiGrid Lander / Operator UI] -->|HTTP / WebSocket| Node[LED Node]
    Node --> |RMT| LEDs[Addressable LEDs]
    Node --> |I2C| PWM[PCA9685 PWM Drivers]
    Node --> |Art-Net / sACN| DMX[DMX Output]
```

## Internal Node Architecture

```text
LumiGrid
│
┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
│                             │
Embedded Node UI        External/Lander UI
FactoryApi              SvelteKit
│                             │
┌─────┴─────────────┐         │
│                   │         │
Signage Runtime     Factory Runtime
Effect Renderer     Factory Effects
Output Controller   Diagnostics
│                   │
┌─────┼─────────────┐         │
│     │             │         │
RMT   PWM           DMX       │
│     │             │         │
LEDs  PCA9685       Art-Net/sACN
```

## System Budgets & Hardware Constraints

To ensure stable operation on embedded hardware, the system enforces the following JSON budgets and physical hardware constraints:
- Normal API response `< 8 KB`
- Large diagnostic response `< 16 KB`
- Backup payload `< 32 KB`
- WebSocket frame `< 4 KB`
- JSON request body `< 8 KB`

### Physical Output Engine Contracts (LG-038)
- **Addressable Outputs**: 8 parallel RMT lanes, canonical maximum **256 pixels per lane** (2,048 pixels total). Submit-all-then-wait parallel transmission.
- **PWM Auxiliary Outputs**: 8 channels via PCA9685 at standard-mode **100 kHz I2C** clock, ~1017 Hz PWM frequency (prescale 5). Direct GPIO `/OE` line fast cutoff (<1 µs).
- **Framerate & Timing**: Target 40.0 FPS (25.0 ms frame period). Frame scheduler detects deadline misses and rebases without burst cycles.
- **Safety Realities**: Software E-Stop and PCA `/OE` cut off immediately; addressable blackout is serial protocol bound (~7.68 ms WS2812 / ~10.24 ms SK6812 for 256 pixels). Sub-5ms addressable physical cutoff requires future hardware load-switch / power-gate.

history/2026-10-21/CONFIGURATION.title: Configuration & Persistence
history/2026-10-21/CONFIGURATION.markdown:
> Historical document preserved on 2026-10-21. Use the [current documentation](../../README.md) for current behavior. Results below apply only to their recorded revision.

# Configuration & Persistence

> **Status:** **IMPLEMENTED** (Unless explicitly marked as PLANNED, PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED, or CONCEPTUAL)

LumiGrid employs a robust persistence layer to store the node's settings, scheduling, and effect presets.

## Transactional Persistence

All configuration writes follow a strict transactional policy:
1. Prepare
2. Validate
3. Write Backup
4. Write Primary
5. Commit
6. Verify
7. Update Cached State
8. Publish State Event

Failure at any stage returns an error safely, guaranteeing consistency. The configuration layer manages checksums, backup slots, and version migration handling seamlessly.

## Safe Data Handling

Firmware is heavily validated to ensure memory bounds, preventing string-safety vulnerabilities (e.g. legacy name migrations strictly enforce null-termination bounds) and avoiding excessive heap allocations during serialization.

history/2026-10-21/EFFECTS.title: Effects & Scene Engine
history/2026-10-21/EFFECTS.markdown:
> Historical document preserved on 2026-10-21. Use the [current documentation](../../README.md) for current behavior. Results below apply only to their recorded revision.

# Effects & Scene Engine

> **Status:** **IMPLEMENTED** (Unless explicitly marked as PLANNED, PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED, or CONCEPTUAL)

The LumiGrid effect system is a full scene-driven lighting engine capable of multi-layered blending and timeline sequences.

## Scene Model

The runtime supports a rich scene model containing:
- 32 discrete presets (scenes)
- 8 output zones
- 3 programmable layers per zone
- 4 distinct blend modes
- Global scene properties (brightness, transition times)
- Overlay/finishing effects (e.g. Strobe) applied on top of the base scene.

## Available Dynamic Effects

The node includes a library of dynamic effects, not just static animations. Effects are retrieved dynamically from the API (`GET /api/v1/effects`), allowing UIs to construct controls without hardcoded assumptions.

Implemented effects include:
- Solid
- Breathe
- Chase
- Sweep
- Reveal
- Sparkle
- Gradient
- Strobe
- Fire
- Aurora
- ColorWave
- StaticPulse

Effect parameters include `label`, `description`, `parameter label`, `unit`, `min`, `max`, and `default` to drive dynamic UI rendering.

## Timelines & Scheduling

The system includes a 16-step sequencer (timeline) across the 16 physical channels (A1–A8 addressable, P1–P8 PWM).
Calendar-based scheduling allows automated preset and sequence activation based on days-of-week and minute-of-day.

history/2026-10-21/FLASH_LAYOUT.title: LumiGrid production flash layout
history/2026-10-21/FLASH_LAYOUT.markdown:
> Historical document preserved on 2026-10-21. Use the [current documentation](../../README.md) for current behavior. Results below apply only to their recorded revision.

# LumiGrid production flash layout

LumiGrid production hardware uses 8 MB flash.

Partition Layout v2 requires one wired migration from Layout v1.
It cannot be installed safely using normal OTA.

## Layout v2

| Partition | Offset | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVS | `0x9000` | `0x4000` |
| OTA selection metadata | `0xd000` | `0x2000` |
| PHY | `0xf000` | `0x1000` |
| factory | `0x10000` | `0x250000` |
| ota_0 | `0x260000` | `0x250000` |
| ota_1 | `0x4b0000` | `0x250000` |
| littlefs reserve | `0x700000` | `0x100000` |

The final address is exactly `0x800000`. Each app slot holds 2,424,832 bytes.
The LittleFS-named partition retains the requested `spiffs` subtype; IDF can print
a naming warning. It is reserved, not mounted or used for production data. The
dashboard remains embedded and Scenes/configuration remain in NVS. No filesystem
content migration is needed.

## Build and wired migration on this workstation

Export `.lgbak` and record node ID/version before migrating a provisioned unit.
The current controller was never provisioned; its raw NVS was backed up privately
under `.pio/lg0384-private` instead. A raw NVS backup can contain credentials and
must never be committed. A normal `.lgbak` intentionally excludes authentication
and network secrets.

```powershell
Set-Location C:\Users\slavd\lumigrid\LumigridLedNode
$env:PLATFORMIO_BUILD_DIR = "$PWD\.pio\build-lg0384"
& C:\Users\slavd\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\Scripts\pio.exe run -e factory
& C:\Users\slavd\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\python.exe scripts\migrate_flash_v2.py --port COM3
```

The migration script validates the freshly built image headers and partition
binary, detects actual physical flash, saves NVS, writes the four artifacts,
then compares NVS byte-for-byte **before the first application boot**. It refuses
to overwrite an earlier migration backup. Archive those files privately before
an intentional repeat migration. It does not issue a full-chip erase.

The underlying write command is:

```powershell
& C:\Users\slavd\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\python.exe `
  C:\Users\slavd\.platformio\packages\tool-esptoolpy\esptool.py `
  --chip esp32 --port COM3 --baud 115200 --after no_reset write_flash `
  --flash_mode dio --flash_freq 40m --flash_size 8MB `
  0x1000 .pio\build-lg0384\factory\bootloader.bin `
  0x8000 .pio\build-lg0384\factory\partitions.bin `
  0xd000 .pio\build-lg0384\factory\ota_data_initial.bin `
  0x10000 .pio\build-lg0384\factory\firmware.bin
```

Do not preserve v1 OTA selection metadata: both OTA application addresses move.
Writing the fresh 8,192-byte initializer at `0xd000` resets selection; NVS at
`0x9000` is not erased. Full factory reset is a separate acceptance test, after
backup and migration-preservation checks.

## Build and runtime contracts

Factory and test targets explicitly declare 8 MB flash and use the production v2
table. The build validator enforces exact offsets/sizes, alignment, non-overlap,
NVS preservation, factory plus exactly two OTA slots, and the 8 MB end address.
After every image build, the storage report measures actual `firmware.bin` bytes:
below 75% is healthy, 75–85% warns, above 85% fails the build.

`/api/v1/info`, `/api/v1/health`, backup source metadata, OTA status and
Installer-level `/api/v1/diagnostics/storage` expose the layout/capacity. Physical
flash is read with pinned IDF's `esp_flash_get_physical_size`; configured flash
uses `esp_flash_get_size`. Runtime checks exact partition addresses and sizes.
Capacity/layout mismatch forces safe mode and outputs off, where startup can
reach recovery. A physically undersized module can fail in the bootloader before
application recovery is possible; it is not supported production hardware.

OTA rejects declared bodies above the next slot capacity with HTTP 413 before
`esp_ota_begin`. It reads and validates the image header, chip revision, 8 MB
header, project and version descriptor before starting an OTA write. Final IDF
image validation still applies; a valid descriptor alone does not authenticate
an unsigned image. Progress is based on declared image length.

Candidates require a continuous ten-second healthy local runtime interval.
The existing recovery worker polls the gate; no new permanent task is created.
API alone cannot confirm. Required planned services, valid configuration, Ready
state and non-critical memory must hold. Internet, STA, DNS and SNTP are not
requirements. Health loss restarts the dwell; fatal/critical conditions roll back,
and sixty seconds without successful verification times out. State schema 2
persists candidate boot/reset reason, dwell start/deadline and failure reason;
schema 1 identity/reason data migrates. Boot-relative timestamps restart on a
candidate boot, and a pending candidate reset is governed by IDF rollback.
Unattributed safe-mode recovery is conservatively not confirmed; firmware does
not invent evidence that it predates the candidate.

## Serial-only bench access

The PC stays on its current Wi-Fi. COM3 at 115200 baud provides bounded read-only
`diagnostics`, `memory`, and `storage` commands, plus a settled snapshot ten
seconds after startup. These use the existing recovery worker and UART FIFO;
no additional task or UART receive allocation is introduced. They expose no
credentials and cannot provision, reset, modify configuration or authorize OTA.

```powershell
& C:\Users\slavd\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\python.exe `
  scripts\capture_serial.py --port COM3 --seconds 60 --command diagnostics
```

The capture reconnects after USB interruption and flushes each chunk to the
acceptance log. Serial does not replace the authenticated HTTP OTA workflow or
the phone/browser setup acceptance. Use a separate device for AP access.

history/2026-10-21/GETTING_STARTED.title: history/2026-10-21/GETTING_STARTED
history/2026-10-21/GETTING_STARTED.markdown:
> Historical document preserved on 2026-10-21. Use the [current documentation](../../README.md) for current behavior. Results below apply only to their recorded revision.

FIRST POWER-ON

1. Connect to Wi-Fi:
   LumiGrid-Setup

2. Password:
   See serial console on first boot (random per-device WPA2 key)

3. Open:
   http://192.168.4.1

4. Create your Admin Access Key.

5. Continue through the setup wizard.

## Secure your controller

The dashboard detects a new controller and opens First Setup. Choose a new
Admin Access Key of 16–64 characters and confirm it. You can also select
**Generate Secure Key** and save the generated key before continuing.
Setup saves the key and signs you in as Administrator in one action.

Wi-Fi password and Node Access Key are separate credentials in distinct security domains.
The setup AP password is a random per-device WPA2 secret printed on the serial console.
It is never derived from MAC or chip ID. The setup AP password does not grant Admin access.

## Normal login and accounts

Open the controller's address and enter your permanent Node Access Key.
The browser uses a temporary session; it does not save the permanent key.
Administrator can create/change Installer and Operator keys in **Access**
from the dashboard's system navigation. Keys must be 16–64 characters.
Saved secrets are never displayed. Keep your Admin key somewhere safe.

Installer accounts support installation/configuration within their permitted
role. Operator accounts support normal lighting operation. Administrator owns
networking, credentials and maintenance. See [ACCESS.md](ACCESS.md).

## Network commissioning

After creating the Admin key, continue through identity, network, outputs,
safety, hardware validation and backup. In the embedded dashboard, the setup
guide provides Wi-Fi setup and links to output configuration, diagnostics and
backup. Apply your Wi-Fi name and password only after securing the controller.
Network changes may disconnect the browser. Connect your computer to the selected
network, find the controller's new address through your router, and sign in
with your permanent key. Review reported network status; a queued change is not
proof that the controller joined Wi-Fi successfully.

## Physical recovery

Recovery is distinct from first setup. A provisioned controller keeps its
permanent keys during reboot, Wi-Fi loss, configuration errors and OTA rollback.
The existing recovery AP policy and recovery safeguards still apply; recovery
never grants the universal temporary setup key on a deployed controller.
Use your existing Admin key for maintenance. Recovery access does not clear
ownership. If the Admin key is lost, a physical full factory reset is required.

## Physical full factory reset

With power on, hold the controller's BOOT button (GPIO 0) for at least five
seconds, then release it so the controller can reboot. This erases credentials,
controller configuration and network settings. Back up configuration first
when possible. Only this deliberate physical reset restores the first-power-on
setup credentials above. An ordinary reboot does not reset access.

history/2026-10-21/HARDWARE_CERTIFICATIO.title: LumiGrid Hardware Certification Specification & Bench Execution Plan (LG-037)
history/2026-10-21/HARDWARE_CERTIFICATIO.markdown:
> Historical document preserved on 2026-10-21. Use the [current documentation](../../README.md) for current behavior. Results below apply only to their recorded revision.

# LumiGrid Hardware Certification Specification & Bench Execution Plan (LG-037)

> **Status**: Hardware certification workflow implemented.
> **Baseline**: `main @ 80617e5d407ba0eb9474df8013071f99cfe4d918`
> **Important Notice**: Physical certification remains dependent on executing the plan on real reference hardware. A code commit cannot certify a PCB sitting on a bench.

---

## 1. Principles & Objectives

The purpose of LG-037 is to create the bridge between:
```text
software passes tests
```
and:
```text
this specific physical LumiGrid unit
was actually tested
against a known certification plan
with traceable evidence
```

### Core Axiom
```text
command accepted != hardware verified
```

- Firmware automatically verifies internal software state, NVS integrity, memory allocations, and network connectivity.
- Physical wiring, visual illumination, PWM duty, power clamp thresholds, and output timing require **operator observation** or **instrument measurement**.
- Firmware and browser APIs reject automated fake-passes for physical tests.

---

## 2. Evidence Sources

Every certification test definition explicitly specifies its required evidence source. The browser cannot downgrade this requirement:

1. **`AUTOMATIC` (`automatic`)**:
   - Firmware directly verifies internal state (e.g., API responds, NVS checksum valid, recovery state asserted).
2. **`OPERATOR OBSERVATION` (`operator_observation`)**:
   - Requires physical human inspection (e.g., A4 illuminates exclusively, RGB color order correct, chase pattern completes across full length, zero flicker, E-stop blackouts physical outputs).
3. **`INSTRUMENT REQUIRED` (`instrument_measurement`)**:
   - Requires measurement with calibrated bench equipment (e.g., oscilloscope duty cycle, calibrated DC power meter / current shunt, logic analyzer multi-node skew).
   - Numerical value and measurement unit (`percent`, `mW`, `us`) are mandatory. Firmware plan enforces pass/fail tolerances.

---

## 3. Certification Profiles

| Profile | Target | Required Scope |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`development`** | Fast bench bring-up | Boot, basic A/P outputs, safety, recovery, network. Serial number optional. |
| **`production_unit`** | Manufactured unit qualification | All A1–A8, all P1–P8, crosstalk, safety, recovery, power limit, 15–30 min burn-in. **Non-empty serial number & valid hardware revision mandatory.** |
| **`release_candidate`** | Firmware/hardware release validation | Full matrix: DMX, backup/restore, OTA rollback, extended burn-in (1h/8h/24h/72h), multi-node physical timing skew with oscilloscope/logic analyzer. |

---

## 4. Test Catalog & Invariant Categories (Plan v1)

| Test ID | Category | Evidence Source | Dev | Prod | RC | Description / Requirement |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| `BOOT-001` | BOOT | `AUTOMATIC` | Req | Req | Req | Boot sequence & immutable node identity assertion |
| `BOOT-OUTPUT-SAFE` | BOOT | `OPERATOR OBSERVATION` | Req | Req | Req | Power-on output inhibit: no flash/glitch before runtime |
| `BOOT-REBOOT-001` | BOOT | `AUTOMATIC` | Req | Req | Req | Reboot configuration persistence across warm resets |
| `BOOT-SAFE-001` | BOOT | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Opt | Req | Safe Mode boot & recovery partition isolation |
| `NET-AP-001` | NETWORK | `AUTOMATIC` | Req | Req | Req | Access Point reachability, DHCP server, HTTP API |
| `NET-STA-001` | NETWORK | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Req | Req | Station association, DHCP acquisition & mDNS discovery |
| `NET-RECONNECT-001`| NETWORK | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Req | Req | Network disconnect/reconnect resilience without reboot |
| `NET-DHCP-001` | NETWORK | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Opt | Req | DHCP route reconciliation & lease renewal |
| `ADDR-A1`..`ADDR-A8`| ADDRESSABLE | `OPERATOR OBSERVATION` | Req | Req | Req | Independent port tests: Red → Green → Blue → White → Chase → Blackout |
| `ADDR-XTALK` | ADDRESSABLE | `OPERATOR OBSERVATION` | Opt | Req | Req | Crosstalk isolation: active A1 with A2–A8 fully off |
| `PWM-P1`..`PWM-P8` | PWM | `OPERATOR OBSERVATION` | Req | Req | Req | Stepped duty (0% → 25% → 50% → 75% → 100% cap → 0%) |
| `PWM-XTALK` | PWM | `OPERATOR OBSERVATION` | Opt | Req | Req | PWM crosstalk isolation & neighboring pin silence |
| `SAFE-ESTOP-LOGIC` | SAFETY | `AUTOMATIC` | Req | Req | Req | Software E-stop state latching & command rejection |
| `SAFE-ESTOP-PWM` | SAFETY | `INSTRUMENT REQUIRED` | Req | Req | Req | PCA9685 /OE direct fast cutoff & zero PWM voltage |
| `SAFE-ESTOP-ADDRESSABLE`| SAFETY | `OPERATOR OBSERVATION` | Req | Req | Req | Physical addressable strip blackout observation |
| `SAFE-DISABLE-001`| SAFETY | `OPERATOR OBSERVATION` | Req | Req | Req | Output disable / OE pin shutdown verification |
| `SAFE-WATCHDOG-001`| SAFETY | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Opt | Req | Live control source loss fallback trigger |
| `POWER-LIMIT-001` | POWER | `INSTRUMENT REQUIRED` | Opt | Req | Req | Calibrated bench PSU current shunt: measured mW within tolerance |
| `DMX-ARTNET-001` | DMX | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Opt | Req | Art-Net 4 universe reception & port routing |
| `DMX-SACN-001` | DMX | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Opt | Req | ANSI E1.31 sACN reception & priority arbitration |
| `REC-BACKUP-001` | RECOVERY | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Req | Req | Streaming `.lgbak` export & secret exclusion verification |
| `REC-RESTORE-001` | RECOVERY | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Opt | Req | Full restore preflight validation and reboot apply |
| `REC-INTERRUPT-001`| RECOVERY | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Opt | Req | Interrupted restore recovery flag survival & AP fallback |
| `OTA-GOOD-001` | OTA | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Opt | Req | Valid OTA candidate flash, reboot, confirmation |
| `OTA-ROLLBACK-001`| OTA | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Opt | Req | Invalid image rollback to previous active partition |
| `BURN-001` | BURN-IN | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Req | Req | Continuous burn-in job (15m–30m prod, 1h–72h RC) |
| `API-001` | API | `AUTOMATIC` | Req | Req | Req | Canonical HTTP `/api/v1` contract conformance |
| `WS-001` | API | `AUTOMATIC` | Req | Req | Req | WebSocket Schema 3 telemetry stream monotonicity |
| `SYNC-ID-001` | MULTI-NODE | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Opt | Req | Discovery & distinct immutable node IDs across fleet |
| `SYNC-LEADER-001` | MULTI-NODE | `AUTOMATIC` | Opt | Opt | Req | Leader election stability & follower lock |
| `SYNC-SCENE-001` | MULTI-NODE | `OPERATOR OBSERVATION` | Opt | Opt | Req | Visually synchronized scene transition |
| `SYNC-TIMING-001` | MULTI-NODE | `INSTRUMENT REQUIRED` | Opt | Opt | Req | Oscilloscope/logic analyzer inter-node optical skew (<5 ms) |

> [!NOTE]
> **Physical Timing Realities (LG-038):**
> - **Total Test Count**: Plan v1 contains **38 tests** across 10 categories.
> - **Addressable Capacity**: Strictly capped at **256 pixels per lane** (2,048 pixels total per node).
> - **PWM / I2C Clock**: PCA9685 operates at standard **100 kHz I2C** clock with prescale 5 (~1017 Hz PWM).
> - **Honest E-Stop Cutoff**:
>   - PCA9685 `/OE` is asserted HIGH directly via GPIO (<1 µs) without waiting on I2C transactions.
>   - Addressable LED blackout is protocol-bound to serial wire transmission: ~7.68 ms for 256 pixels of WS2812 (30 µs/px) and ~10.24 ms for SK6812 RGBW (40 µs/px).
>   - Sub-5ms addressable physical blackout requires a future hardware power-gate / load switch.
>   - Parallel RMT driver and microsecond telemetry are fully implemented in firmware; physical bench validation remains pending oscilloscope/meter measurement on physical hardware.

---

## 5. Hardware Fingerprinting & Staleness Rules

Certification results become **STALE** when underlying hardware-relevant reality changes:
- Firmware version upgraded (`1.2.0` → `1.3.0`)
- Hardware revision changed
- Plan version incremented
- Addressable channel strip length, pixel order, or chip type modified
- PWM output allocation modified
- Power limiter wattage changed
- DMX universe patch changed

> **Non-Invalidating Changes**: Scene changes, Cue list edits, Timeline edits, and display name changes do **NOT** invalidate hardware qualification.

---

## 6. Execution Protocol & Safety Gates

1. **Exclusivity**: Only one certification session can be active per controller.
2. **FactoryRunner Integration**: Physical output tests are commanded through `FactoryRunner` with owner tagged as `Certification`. Brightness caps (LG-035) remain enforced.
3. **Safe Timeouts**: Physical tests timeout and automatically blackout after a bounded duration (default: 10s for channel tests; 5 minutes maximum for operator evaluation). No LED output is left on indefinitely.
4. **Failure Auditing**: A test failure requires a mandatory reason category (`no_output`, `wrong_port`, `wrong_color_order`, `partial_strip`, `flicker`, `crosstalk`, `unstable`, `other`) and descriptive note. Attempt counters are monotonically incremented.
5. **Persistence**: Dual-slot NVS storage (`cert_a` / `cert_b` in `hw_cert` namespace) with CRC32 protection guarantees survival across reboots.

---

## 7. Recommended First Real Bench Plan

Upon deploying this firmware to bench units, execute tests in this sequence:
1. `BOOT-OUTPUT-SAFE`
2. `ADDR-A1`
3. `ADDR-A8`
4. `PWM-P1`
5. `PWM-P8`
6. `SAFE-ESTOP-001`
7. Complete all `ADDR-A1`..`ADDR-A8`
8. Complete all `PWM-P1`..`PWM-P8`
9. `ADDR-XTALK` & `PWM-XTALK`
10. `NET-RECONNECT-001`
11. `REC-BACKUP-001`
12. Reboot verification
13. `BURN-001` (15-minute qualification)

history/2026-10-21/HARDWARE_VALIDATION.markdown:
> Historical document preserved on 2026-10-21. Use the [current documentation](../../README.md) for current behavior. Results below apply only to their recorded revision.

# LumiGrid Hardware Validation Matrix & Physical Bench Status

> **Baseline Commit**: `ea586e39aca19df0d051e2534cf336c73316f582`
> **Date**: October 2026
> **Scope**: Physical hardware validation for LumiGrid LED Node v1.0 (A1–A8, P1–P8, power, thermal, sync, and recovery).

---

## 1. Physical Hardware Validation Policy

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Software simulation and unit tests (e.g. `RuntimeHardeningTests`, `FactoryRunner` unit verification) certify only **software lifecycle and algorithmic correctness**.
> Physical hardware validation milestones (`[PASS]`) MUST NOT be claimed without real physical hardware bench measurement on connected physical fixtures, power analyzers, oscilloscopes, or multi-node test networks.

All physical milestones remain explicitly tracked below as `[PENDING BENCH]` until physical test execution is completed.

---

## 2. Validation Matrix

| Test ID | Domain | Test Scenario | Hardware Setup | Verification Criteria | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| **HW-BOOT-01** | Power / Boot | Power-on transient and strapping protection | Physical ESP32 on calibrated bench PSU | No false strapping pin latches on boot, GPIO0 stabilizes within 3s grace period | `[PENDING BENCH]` |
| **HW-A1A8-01** | Addressable | A1–A8 WS2812 / SK6812 parallel RMT signal integrity | 8x LED strips (up to 256 px/lane) attached to RMT output pins | 800 kHz bit timing, clean rise/fall times (<50ns), zero flicker or frame drop at 40 FPS under true 8-lane parallel submission | `[PENDING BENCH]` |
| **HW-P1P8-01** | PWM | P1–P8 PCA9685 I2C output drive | 8x low-voltage LED loads / MOSFET gates | ~1017 Hz PWM waveform (prescale=5), linear duty cycle response (0–100%), 100 kHz I2C bus stability, no bus lockup | `[PENDING BENCH]` |
| **HW-ESTOP-01** | Safety | Runtime E-Stop / blackout trip | Software/runtime E-stop command; no dedicated physical E-stop GPIO | PCA9685 /OE asserted HIGH immediately (<1 µs); addressable blackout protocol-bound (~7.68 ms for 256 px WS2812 / ~10.24 ms SK6812); latched state prevents re-enable. No addressable power gate is present; physical <5 ms addressable cutoff requires future hardware | `[PENDING BENCH]` |
| **HW-PWR-01** | Safety / Power | Dynamic power limiter | DC lab power supply with current shunt | Total system power draw clamped to configured `max_power_mw` without reboot | `[PENDING BENCH]` |
| **HW-THERM-01**| Thermal | 24-hour continuous burn-in at full load | Thermal chamber or sealed enclosure | Board temperature remains within safe operating envelope; no thermal throttling crashes | `[PENDING BENCH]` |
| **HW-SYNC-01** | Fleet Sync | Multi-node optical synchronization | 3 physical nodes with photodiodes on oscilloscope | Frame start optical alignment within <15 ms across nodes running UDP NodeSync | `[PENDING BENCH]` |
| **HW-RESET-01**| Recovery | Physical GPIO0 factory reset | Physical button hold for 5 seconds | Blackout, full NVS erase, wait for button release, clean reboot into unprovisioned AP | `[PENDING BENCH]` |
| **HW-OTA-01**  | Recovery / OTA | Bad firmware image automatic rollback | Physical node flashed with fault-inducing candidate | Bootloader detects unconfirmed candidate failure and rolls back to previous partition | `[PENDING BENCH]` |

---

## 3. LG-035, LG-037 & LG-038 Output Engine Stabilization Status

The software architecture and endpoints for factory validation, physical output engine stabilization, and traceable hardware certification are implemented:
- **True 8-lane parallel RMT driver**: submits all active channels simultaneously before waiting, bounded wait timeouts (`addressable_wire_time_us + 1200us`), drains all channels on timeout, zero per-frame heap allocation.
- **Canonical Addressable limit**: exactly 256 pixels max per lane (replaces outdated 144 / 300 references).
- **PCA9685 safety**: 100 kHz standard mode I2C, init register readback verification (MODE1, MODE2, PRE_SCALE=5 / ~1017 Hz), fast fail-safe asserting `/OE HIGH` directly via GPIO without I2C transaction.
- **No catch-up bursts**: lighting scheduler detects frame deadline misses and rebases without burst cycles.
- **Microsecond commit telemetry**: `GET /api/v1/diagnostics/output` and WebSocket live streaming of addressable, PWM, total commit duration, and frame deadline misses.
- **Factory test stages**: deterministic sequenced stages (Red, Green, Blue, White, Chase, Blackout for addressable; 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%, 0% for PWM).
- **Split E-Stop certification**: `SAFE-ESTOP-LOGIC` (Automatic), `SAFE-ESTOP-PWM` (Instrument), `SAFE-ESTOP-ADDRESSABLE` (Operator). 38 tests total in Plan v1.
- `FactoryRunner` state machine (`Idle`, `Running`, `Completed`, `Aborted`, `Failed`) with time-bounded burn-in job execution.
- Dual-slot NVS persistence (`hw_cert` namespace: `cert_a` / `cert_b`) with CRC32 protection.
- Versioned certification plans (Plan v1) with `Development`, `ProductionUnit`, and `ReleaseCandidate` profiles.
- Operator console at `/dashboard/certification` and embedded summary in `dashboard.html`.

See [`docs/HARDWARE_CERTIFICATION.md`](file:///c:/Users/slavd/lumigrid/docs/HARDWARE_CERTIFICATION.md) for full certification catalog, evidence rules, and bench execution plan. Physical certification remains dependent on executing the plan on real reference hardware with oscilloscopes and meters.


## LG-038.3 memory and service lifecycle acceptance

All physical gates for this change are **UNMEASURED**. Software compilation and fixture tests do not certify heap headroom, stack margins, maximum loaded topology, or 30-minute stability. See [RUNTIME_MEMORY_BUDGET.md](RUNTIME_MEMORY_BUDGET.md) for scratch costs, task lifetimes, unchanged engineering gates and the complete measurement record.
