| Provisioned minimal Ready, settle 60 s | free8 >= 24576; largest8 >= 12288; optional workers reflect config/network | UNMEASURED |
| Eight lanes, 256 RGBW pixels | free8 >= 16384; largest8 >= 8192; loaded outputs and traffic remain stable | UNMEASURED |
| Protocol toggle and allocation failure | Off creates no task; on/off actually starts/stops; failed starts preserve previous protocol state | UNMEASURED |
| Wi-Fi apply and STA route/loss | One apply at a time; worker retires; fleet stops without STA and rebinds with unchanged identity | UNMEASURED |
| Factory/Certification lazy use | No Factory task for automatic probes; first physical command starts it and exposes its stack minimum | UNMEASURED |
| Topology failure injection | No persistence or half-configured lanes; original lengths/format/order remain intact; structured memory error | UNMEASURED |
| Heavy-operation pressure | OTA/restore/validation/report refuse before mutation; measure actual peak scratch, minimum free8 and largest8 | UNMEASURED |
| WebSocket soak, 30 min | Bounded 64-sample schema; no monotonic heap/largest-block loss after reconnect cycles | UNMEASURED |
| Burn-in soak, 30 min | Capture start/min/end free8 and largest8, per-task minima, faults, deadlines and resets | UNMEASURED |

Capture `/api/v1/diagnostics/memory` with Installer/Admin authority at each stage. Per-task watermarks are bytes on the pinned Xtensa port. Retain raw logs and timestamped snapshots with the controller identity, image checksum, topology and active services. Do not flash the development test image onto a production unit: it deliberately enables test credentials and its assertion suite.

history/2026-10-21/LED_NODE.markdown:
> Historical document preserved on 2026-10-21. Use the [current documentation](../../README.md) for current behavior. Results below apply only to their recorded revision.

# LED Node Hardware & Capabilities

> **Status:** **IMPLEMENTED** (Unless explicitly marked as PLANNED, PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED, or CONCEPTUAL)

The LumiGrid LED Node is the core hardware controller in the ecosystem.

## Hardware Output Contracts

The actual hardware/software contract for the LED Node is explicitly defined as **8 addressable LED lanes + 8 PWM channels**.

- **Addressable LED Lanes:** 8 lanes (numbered 0-7) driven by a custom parallel RMT driver:
  - Canonical maximum: **256 pixels per lane** (2,048 pixels total per node).
  - Supported protocols: WS2812B (RGB, 30 µs/pixel wire time) and SK6812 (RGBW, 40 µs/pixel wire time).
  - Parallel submission invariant: all active lanes are submitted to RMT hardware before any lane is waited on.
  - Zero heap allocation per frame.
- **PWM Channels:** 8 channels (numbered 0-7) using PCA9685 via standard-mode **100 kHz I2C**:
  - Operating frequency: ~1017 Hz (prescale 5).
  - Fast fail-safe: `/OE` line is asserted HIGH directly via GPIO (<1 µs) without I2C transaction on emergency stop.

> [!WARNING]
> Historical documentation previously described a 16-channel generalized PWM driver and 300 pixels per port. The node firmly asserts 8 lanes (max 256 px) + 8 PWM channels (100 kHz I2C) in its factory validation constraints.

## Safety & Emergency Stop Contracts

- **Software E-Stop:** Latched atomically; immediately disables output commits and sets PCA `/OE HIGH`.
- **PWM Cutoff:** Immediate (<1 µs via physical `/OE` assertion).
- **Addressable Blackout:** Protocol-bound to serial frame wire transmission (~7.68 ms for 256 pixels of WS2812 / ~10.24 ms for SK6812 RGBW). Sub-5ms addressable physical cutoff requires future hardware load-switch / power-gate.

## System Health & Output Engine Telemetry

The node tracks system health and physical timing comprehensively:
- Free heap & minimum free heap
- Wi-Fi RSSI & network routes
- NVS state & configuration validity
- Startup diagnostics (startup stage, failing stage)
- Output state (Healthy, Faulted, Armed, E-Stop) & commit failures
- **Output Engine Timing (`/api/v1/diagnostics/output`)**:
  - Target framerate (40.0 FPS / 25.0 ms period)
  - Committed framerate
  - Frame commit duration, RMT wire duration, PWM duration
  - Frame headroom (ms)
  - Frame deadline misses (rebased without catch-up burst cycles)
- DMX statistics (drops, unpatched)
- Watchdog fallback & sync packet loss

## Power Limiting & Electrical Safety

The node incorporates an in-place software power estimator and limiter (`PowerBudget`):
- Models quiescent idle power (5 mW/pixel) and full active power (295 mW/pixel for WS2812 RGB, 380 mW/pixel for SK6812 RGBW).
- Supports auxiliary PWM power modeling via per-channel `max_milliwatts` load configuration.
- Enforces local channel constraints and the global device power supply budget (`max_power_mw`) via proportional scaling and soft-start ramp.
- Telemetry exposes requested vs limited estimated power and complete model status (`estimateComplete`).

> [!CAUTION]
> **Power Estimation Disclaimer:**
> Power limiting is an estimated software brightness limiter (WLED-style empirical modeling). It does **NOT** replace a correctly sized power supply unit (PSU), adequate wiring gauges, fuses, MOSFET thermal ratings, or physical branch circuit protection. Hardware installations must always be electrically safe regardless of software state.

history/2026-10-21/LG-038.1-BOOT-HOTFIX.title: LG-038.1 boot hotfix
history/2026-10-21/LG-038.1-BOOT-HOTFIX.markdown:
> Historical document preserved on 2026-10-21. Use the [current documentation](../../README.md) for current behavior. Results below apply only to their recorded revision.

# LG-038.1 boot hotfix

Baseline: main 0f1198dd4944299101ddc5a8b1dcf1838f9ec54a.

Current status: consolidated image flashed and all four hashes verified on COM4.
Physical idle boot passes: app_main, all required startup services and Ready
heartbeats observed through 73.5 seconds, with no panic/reset in the captures.
Main task minimum free stack is 7148/10240 bytes. Idle free heap is only about
4680 bytes; topology/load acceptance remains blocked on runtime memory headroom.
Current evidence: LG-038.1-boot-log.txt. Earlier captures below refer to previous
images and are retained as diagnostic history.

## Framework constraint

PlatformIO espressif32@6.7.0 supplies ESP-IDF 5.2.1. Its hidden
FREERTOS_SUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION option is always enabled, and
FreeRTOSConfig.h hardcodes configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION=1 and
configUSE_TIMERS=1. Config regeneration restores static allocation to y.
The requested sdkconfig-only disable therefore cannot change scheduler behavior.
No framework patches or custom application idle/timer memory hooks are introduced.

Approved owner exception: scripts/boot_memory_policy.json declares ESP-IDF
port_common.c as scheduler-memory owner for this exact platform/framework pin.
The invariant allows generated factory static allocation only with that owner
and its documentation. Project defaults still reject enabling it. Platform
changes require revisiting this exception. CI checks again after factory config
regeneration; application idle/timer hooks are forbidden.

Sources: https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/blob/v5.2.1/components/freertos/Kconfig
and https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/blob/v5.2.1/components/freertos/config/include/freertos/FreeRTOSConfig.h.

## Pre-scheduler DRAM

The first clean telemetry build reserves 130480 bytes for app_main's static
LumigridRuntime object, before scheduler startup. Two inline LiveDmxFrame buffers
are moved to checked, separately owned heap allocations in the LightingRuntime
constructor, called after app_main begins. Capacity and runtime lifetime are
preserved. Lighting startup rejects missing buffers with ESP_ERR_NO_MEM.
This reduces pre-scheduler static DRAM; it does not reduce total runtime frame
storage. The physical boot log is required to establish causality and acceptance.

## Telemetry and acceptance

BOOT_HEAP precedes runtime construction and reports free/largest 8-bit memory,
free/largest internal memory, free heap and minimum heap. Startup stages include
ConfigStore, OutputController, PCA9685, addressable topology, LightingRuntime,
Wi-Fi, HTTP API, mDNS and certification. RMT_ALLOC records A port, GPIO, RGB/RGBW,
pixel count, wire bytes, result and internal heap after configuration. No per-frame
heap logging is added.

Capture power-on through at least ten seconds: require main_task, app_main,
BOOT_HEAP and runtime startup, without timer-task assertion or reset loop.
Start with A and P ports disabled; then P1; then A1 with 30 pixels; only then
increase topology. Eight-channel allocation and output certification remain
physical acceptance gates, not claims inferred from compilation.

## Separate storage defect

Reported hardware: ESP32 rev 3.1, physical 8 MB SPI flash. The board definition,
image header and partitions currently target 4 MB. The size warning is separate
from the timer-task allocation assertion. Preserve this partition table for the
hotfix. A later storage batch must align board size, defaults, partition table,
OTA slots and filesystem together for the intended production module.

## Clean build

Recursive deletion of the old factory directory was blocked by automatic approval
review. Build in a new empty directory instead:

```powershell
$env:PLATFORMIO_BUILD_DIR = "$PWD/.pio/build-lg0381-final"
pio run -e factory
```

Use only bootloader.bin, partitions.bin, ota_data_initial.bin and firmware.bin
from that directory's factory subdirectory. Flash offsets are respectively
0x1000, 0x8000, 0xd000 and 0x10000. Preserve NVS and the 4 MB partition layout.

## Validation result (2026-10-05)

Clean factory compilation passed using a new build directory. Final static RAM
is 142516 bytes (previous telemetry build 177412); the static runtime object
is 95584 bytes (previous 130480), releasing 34896 bytes before scheduling.
Factory configuration regenerated with static allocation enabled by IDF; the
approved explicit owner exception passes. Eight configuration regression tests
and the existing runtime math/protocol simulation suite passed. Local factory
builds run the invariant before building and after linking, and CI repeats it
after sdkconfig regeneration. No partition changes or application scheduler
memory hooks were introduced.

COM4 identified an ESP32-D0WD-V3 rev 3.1. The first flash attempt lost the
serial connection during the firmware write at 44 percent. After manual ROM
downloader recovery, all four freshly built images were flashed at 57600 baud
and their hashes verified. The board no longer has an incomplete write.
Automated UART captures received no boot text; manual startup capture is pending.
Physical acceptance is not established until app_main, heap telemetry and stable
runtime startup are observed. Do not resume LG-038 topology tests before that gate.

Build and flash logs are in docs/lg0381-build.log,
docs/lg0381-build-policy.log, docs/lg0381-flash.log and
docs/lg0381-flash-retry.log and docs/lg0381-flash-recovery.log
(local ignored artifacts).

## First physical boot capture

The recovery flash reached main_task and app_main with BOOT_HEAP free8=160092,
largest8=110592, internal=199316, largestInternal=110592, freeHeap=160092,
minimum=160092. The timer-task assertion no longer occurs. A later heap-walk
LoadProhibited panic after PCA9685 initialization still reset the board.
The symbolized trace ends in log_heap_stage, heap_caps_get_largest_free_block,
multi_heap_get_info_impl and tlsf_walk_pool.

PCA9685 configured trans_queue_depth=4. In the pinned IDF i2c_master.c this
enables asynchronous transfers even without a registered callback. The driver
uses stack-local readback bytes and immediately validates them; async completion
violates their lifetime. Set trans_queue_depth=0 to preserve synchronous
completion while the mutex is held. The invariant rejects returning to async
mode with stack buffers. Subsequent physical capture is required for acceptance.

Raw capture: docs/lg0381-boot-manual.log (local ignored artifact).

## Second physical boot capture

Synchronous I2C removes the heap-walk panic; startup reaches ConfigStore and
LightingRuntime. PCA9685 truth is ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND at 0x55 and 0x40. PWM testing
is blocked until the peripheral is present, while idle startup may continue.
The next blocker is a main-task stack overflow in certification initialization.
CertificationStore placed multiple approximately 6.7 KB record values on the
10 KB main stack, including two slot records in load(). Move startup/load/save
scratch records to checked heap ownership and reset owned records in place
without large aggregate stack temporaries. Do not enlarge the scheduler's main
stack to mask this issue. Raw capture: docs/lg0381-boot-final-power.log.

Compiled regression evidence: the previous image is rejected by
verify_boot_stack.py because CertificationStore::save uses a 6736-byte stack
frame. The corrected image passes: init=64, load=80 and save=64 bytes. Factory
post-link checks enforce a 1024-byte scratch-frame budget for these functions.
This checks generated code, not only a source pattern. Full startup stack usage
and final idle stability still require target observation.

## Network startup stack and handler capacity

The next capture passes certification and starts Wi-Fi, then reports
ESP_ERR_HTTPD_HANDLERS_FULL and a main-task stack overflow. FactoryApi::start
had a 3680-byte frame nested under runtime start (3216) and network-service
startup (1872), before deeper library/logging calls. Move immutable HTTP route
tables into flash, bind user_ctx on a single temporary registration descriptor,
and derive max_uri_handlers from both route table lengths instead of hardcoded
80. The post-link guard bounds FactoryApi::start to 2048 bytes. BOOT_STACK logs
the main task's observed minimum remaining stack after startup. Main stack
configuration remains 10240 bytes. Capture: docs/lg0381-boot-stack.log.

API startup now emits a 1648-byte frame (previous 3680), passes the 2048-byte
compiled guard, and computes handler capacity from the route arrays. The final
source build uses 142516 static RAM bytes and 1295017 flash bytes. Configuration
and linked stack guards passed. Device validation of this image is pending.

## Combined startup stack correction

The HTTP-table fix alone still overflows main at api.start; raw capture is
docs/lg0381-boot-api.log. Its individual frame passed, but the combined runtime
start/network/API chain retained too much stack. Move DeviceConfig snapshots in
both parent startup methods to checked heap ownership and reuse the first
snapshot after Wi-Fi startup. Emitted frames are now runtime_start=592 and
network_start=560 bytes, down from 3216 and 1872. The post-link guard now
requires both parent frames below 1024 bytes as well as the API frame below
2048. Main stack remains 10240 bytes. Eight config regression tests and
git diff --check pass; factory build passes with flash usage 1294965 bytes.
Target idle acceptance remains pending for this correction.

## Upstream research and complete-path audit (2026-10-05)

Read the pinned ESP-IDF 5.2.1 upstream source, not a generic vanilla-FreeRTOS
recipe. port_common.c allocates idle/timer TCBs and stacks through pvPortMalloc
and asserts on allocation failure. heap_idf.c requests internal, 8-bit-capable
memory. Static-allocation support does not mean the port supplies compile-time
static buffers. Reducing application .bss is the appropriate remedy for this
pre-scheduler shortage; disabling the hidden Kconfig option cannot remedy it.

Sources:
- https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/blob/v5.2.1/components/freertos/port_common.c
- https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/blob/v5.2.1/components/freertos/heap_idf.c
- https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/blob/v5.2.1/components/esp_http_server/src/httpd_main.c
- https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/v5.2/esp32/api-guides/performance/ram-usage.html

httpd_start creates a separate HTTP worker using config.stack_size. The observed
crashing task is main, so changing the HTTP worker's stack does not address this
startup overflow. Espressif recommends removing large automatic variables and
checking task stack high-water marks. No matching upstream fix for this specific
application startup overflow was established by the GitHub searches.

The latest ELF direct-call audit finds retained large configuration records in
ConfigStore::load_config, its migration lambda, scene initialization and API
identity startup. The conservative app_main path estimate is 9776 bytes against
a 10240-byte main stack; it includes exception-unwind paths and excludes indirect
calls, ROM frames and interrupts. It is evidence to guide a full configuration
scratch-storage review, not a certified worst-case bound. Individual frame guards
cannot establish whole-call-chain safety. Do not treat the unflashed parent-frame
correction as proof of stable idle. Further startup work must consolidate large
configuration/migration scratch ownership and review the full chain before any
additional target validation.

## Consolidated boot hardening

Current candidate: .pio/build-lg0381-solid/factory, from a new clean build
followed by source verification. Final flash usage 1295369/1310720 bytes; static
RAM 142516 bytes. The four-image size/SHA256 manifest is lg0381-images.json in
that build directory. No partition, header size, main stack size or framework
changes. No target flash is performed before this candidate passes the offline
gates and the board is placed in the downloader.

- Device/configuration backup, verification and legacy migration scratch records
  use invocation-local checked heap ownership; normal scene loads allocate no
  legacy topology snapshot. Scratch is not shared across tasks.
- Scene initialization loads into its owned scene buffer; blackout fallback
  reconstructs it in place with the original default values.
- Config/scene default writes and allocation failures propagate; defaults are not
  written on unrelated NVS errors. Config save acquires verification scratch
  before touching NVS, preserving backup-write ordering.
- Runtime init, API identity initialization and certification initialization use
  checked configuration scratch. It is released before deeper startup work.
- Recovery/network-apply task creation, network readiness semaphore, lighting
  shutdown semaphore, authentication and certification initialization are checked.
  app_main logs BOOT_FAILED and does not call start after a failed init. Required
  API/mDNS/fleet/Art-Net/sACN startup errors propagate and prevent Ready; startup
  rollback blacks out and disables outputs while retaining available recovery
  Wi-Fi/API access.

Linked frames: app_main=80, runtime_init=320, runtime_start=592,
network_start=560, api_start=304, scene_init=64, config_load=64,
scene_load(max including lambdas)=192, scene_save=80,
cert_service_init=64, cert_store_init=64, cert_store_load=80,
cert_store_save=64 bytes. The linked guard covers all these and rejects an
acyclic direct-call startup path exceeding 7680 bytes (75% of the unchanged
10240-byte main stack). Current direct-call estimate: 5072 bytes. This excludes
indirect calls, recursion depth, ROM and interrupt frames; it does not replace
target stack high-water telemetry.

Offline verification: eight boot policy regression tests, seven linked-stack
guard tests, invariant checks, existing runtime math/protocol simulations,
clean factory build and final source rebuild, and git diff --check pass. These
are not target proof of OOM handling, legacy migration, or output certification.
Device acceptance requires one consolidated flash, power-on log, all required
startup stages, BOOT_STACK headroom and sustained Ready heartbeats without reset.
PCA9685 remained absent at 0x55/0x40 in previous target captures; PWM acceptance
requires that hardware. All A/P ports remain disabled for the idle boot gate.

## Physical validation of the consolidated image

Flash: docs/lg0381-flash-solid.log. All four images from build-lg0381-solid
verified at 0x1000, 0x8000, 0xd000 and 0x10000. Firmware SHA256 is
9b77f13b1a71c95f48add04c2b93b102e33443471543eb071ee17fc9d2d20980;
boot-reported ELF prefix 03c939b2a. No erase of NVS or partition changes.

Power-cycle capture reaches app_main at 729 ms and BOOT_HEAP at 732 ms:
free8=160092, largest8=110592, internal=199280, largestInternal=110592,
freeHeap=160092, minimum=160092. Lighting, certification, Wi-Fi, HTTP, mDNS,
fleet discovery, Art-Net and sACN complete by 3533 ms. BOOT_STACK minimumFree=7148.
No HTTP handler-capacity error, main stack overflow or timer allocation assertion
appears. PCA9685 remains absent and PWM configurations are rejected truthfully.
SNTP has no upstream connectivity in AP-only mode and falls back to local uptime.

Separate idle capture shows Ready at 33.538, 43.538, 53.538, 63.538 and 73.538 s;
free_heap is 4672 initially then 4680 on the remaining samples. No panic or reboot
appears in these captured intervals. Startup capture begins at 559 ms after USB
reconnect and ends at 3533 ms; the serial listener was reopened for the idle
capture, so the combined readable log explicitly marks the interval boundary.
It is not a continuous capture of the entire first 73 seconds.

Memory limit: startup-stage telemetry uses MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL, which can include
IRAM unavailable to ordinary 8-bit data allocations. Its roughly 39 KB largest
block must not be treated as ordinary heap capacity. Heartbeat esp_get_free_heap_size
shows the actual approximately 4.7 KB idle 8-bit headroom. Protocol workers retain
4 KB stacks each; main retains its 10 KB stack for heartbeat logging. These are
runtime headroom candidates for a later consolidated memory pass, not stacks to
blindly shrink. No loaded topology, eight-channel RMT allocation, HTTP interaction,
fresh-NVS boot or injected allocation-failure acceptance has been established.
Do not infer those from this idle boot result.

history/2026-10-21/LG-038.2-SETUP-UX.title: LG-038.2 & LG-038.7 Setup & Authentication Reference
history/2026-10-21/LG-038.2-SETUP-UX.markdown:
> Historical document preserved on 2026-10-21. Use the [current documentation](../../README.md) for current behavior. Results below apply only to their recorded revision.

# LG-038.2 & LG-038.7 Setup & Authentication Reference

FactoryFirstBoot uses `LumiGrid-Setup` with a random per-device Wi-Fi WPA2 password
generated via hardware RNG (`esp_fill_random`) and displayed on serial console.
There are no universal credentials and no MAC-derived passwords.

Permanent AuthStore credentials require 16–64 characters.
The bootstrap endpoint (`POST /api/v1/auth/bootstrap`) is state-gated:
it is accessible without authentication ONLY while `!is_provisioned()` and
`bootstrap_allowed()` (genuine `FactoryFirstBoot` or `PhysicalRecovery`).

`POST /api/v1/auth/bootstrap` saves the permanent Admin key and returns a new
Admin session in the same request. NVS backup and commit errors are propagated.
Invalid existing auth storage fails closed instead of being interpreted as
first boot.

Both dashboards detect first setup, request a new confirmed Admin key and
continue directly into setup. Both offer key generation and Access account
management without displaying saved secrets.

## Automated evidence

- Dashboard unit suite: 382 tests passed.
- Browser regressions: six tests passed against mocked node APIs, exercising
  both real dashboards, confirmation, direct session entry, normal login,
  recovery gating, visible setup instructions and embedded role management.
- Svelte/copy checks: zero errors and zero warnings.
- Firmware factory and runtime-test images compile successfully.
- Architectural invariants and production boot-stack checks pass.
- Runtime A–J credential regressions are included in RuntimeHardeningTests.
  They exercise restricted setup sessions, permanent credential rejection,
  immediate revocation, NVS-backed manager reconstruction and explicit reset.

Run browser coverage with:

```powershell
cd lumigrid-lander-main
npx playwright test tests/e2e/first-setup.spec.ts --workers=1
```

The tests accept `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH` when an existing local
Chromium installation is used instead of the version expected by Playwright.

## Physical acceptance remaining

No controller was flashed or reset during this change. Runtime assertions
were compiled, not executed on hardware. Actual first power-on, Wi-Fi change,
physical full reset and OTA rollback acceptance remain to be verified on a
test controller. Browser API fixtures and reconstructed AuthManagers do not
constitute that physical evidence.

Production flash usage remains near the current partition limit (about 99%).
See [GETTING_STARTED.md](GETTING_STARTED.md) and [ACCESS.md](ACCESS.md).

# LG-HW-001 — Deterministic Hardware Coexistence Architecture

**Status**: Implemented & Hardened  
**Scope**: Classic ESP32 (Dual Core Xtensa LX6 @ 240MHz, 8MB SPI Flash)  
**Document Owner**: LumiGrid Embedded Firmware Architecture Team  

---

## 1. Architectural Domain Separation (CPU0 vs CPU1)

On the classic ESP32 dual-core SoC, shared interrupt handlers and task contention between networking (Wi-Fi/LWIP/HTTPD) and hard real-time lighting output (ESP-IDF RMT TX, I2C/PCA9685) produce severe jitter, channel desynchronization, and silent hardware deadlock if core affinity is uncoordinated.

LG-HW-001 establishes an immutable domain boundary:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 CPU 0                   │  │                 CPU 1                   │
│         Network & Control Domain        │  │       Hardware & Lighting Domain        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤  ├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ • esp_netif / LWIP TCP/IP stack         │  │ • LightingRuntime render loop (50 Hz)   │
│ • Wi-Fi driver task (pinned to CPU0)    │  │ • OutputController & ParallelRmtDriver  │
│ • HTTPD web server & REST API handlers  │  │ • PCA9685 synchronous PWM driver        │
│ • Main boot task (returns after boot)   │  │ • OutputCoreExecutor (output_hw worker) │
│ • Fleet discovery & NVS background tasks│  │ • RMT TX interrupts & ISR callbacks     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                       │    ▲
                  Synchronous Marshalled Calls (Queue + Binary Semaphore)
                                       └───►│
```

### Core Configuration Invariants (`sdkconfig.defaults` & `sdkconfig.factory`)
1. `CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_TASK_PINNED_TO_CORE_0=y` — Prevents Wi-Fi stack ISRs and event handling tasks from preempting time-critical lighting tasks on CPU1.
2. `CONFIG_ESP_MAIN_TASK_AFFINITY_CPU0=y` — Keeps boot initialization on CPU0, returning cleanly so its 10 KB stack is reclaimed.
3. `CONFIG_RMT_ISR_IRAM_SAFE=y` — Ensures all RMT interrupt service routines execute from IRAM even when the flash cache is disabled during Wi-Fi NVS/flash writes.

---

## 2. RMT Core Ownership & Lifecycle Marshalling

### Problem
In ESP-IDF 5.x, calling `rmt_new_tx_channel()` allocates an interrupt vector on whichever CPU core is currently executing the caller. When `OutputController::init()` or `reconfigure()` is called from the main boot task or an incoming HTTP POST request on CPU0, the RMT interrupt vector becomes registered on CPU0. When `LightingRuntime` transmits from CPU1, cross-core interrupt notifications induce scheduling latencies, missed latch timings, and FreeRTOS assert crashes.

### Solution: `OutputCoreExecutor`
The `OutputCoreExecutor` runs a dedicated FreeRTOS worker (`output_hw`) pinned permanently to CPU1 (`xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(..., 1)`):
- Priority: 5 (Dedicated hardware lifecycle context).
- Stack: 6144 bytes.
- Zero per-frame heap allocation: Commands use static/stack descriptors with binary completion semaphores.
- Core 1 Bypass: If `OutputController::init()` or `reconfigure()` is invoked by a thread already on CPU1 (e.g. `LightingRuntime`), execution proceeds directly without queuing to prevent deadlock.
- All hardware lifecycle functions (`init_on_output_core`, `reconfigure_on_output_core`) enforce `assert(xPortGetCoreID() == 1)` in debug and test environments.

---

## 3. RMT Memory Constraints (8 Lanes × 64 Symbols)

The classic ESP32 RMT peripheral features 8 channels and a shared RAM of 512 32-bit symbol words.

$$\text{Total Memory} = 512 \text{ words} = 8 \text{ channels} \times 64 \text{ words/channel}$$

1. **Exact Allocation**: Every lane is configured with `mem_block_symbols = 64`. Increasing any single lane to 128 or 192 symbols steals RAM blocks from adjacent channels, reducing the total available addressable outputs below the 8 required by LumiGrid.
2. **Interrupt Priority**: TX channels are registered with `cc.intr_priority = 3`, ensuring RMT buffer reload ISRs preempt standard tasks while remaining below FreeRTOS critical masking levels.
3. **Internal DRAM Buffers vs Generic Memory**: Because `CONFIG_RMT_ISR_IRAM_SAFE=y` is active, any buffer touched in interrupt context or encoder callback must reside in internal SRAM. `ParallelRmtDriver` allocates wire buffers and `StripEncoder` memory strictly via `heap_caps_calloc(1, size, MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL | MALLOC_CAP_8BIT)`. Allocation from external PSRAM or standard general heap is prohibited. Conversely, diagnostic shadow buffers, pixel color staging arrays, and gamma tables use generic heap memory.
4. **Internal Reserve & Transactional Admission (LG-HW-002)**: To prevent Wi-Fi packet buffers and ISR stacks from starving, a mandatory 12 KB internal SRAM headroom (`kPostTopologyInternalReserveBytes = 12 * 1024`) must remain free post-allocation. Reconfiguration topology admission is strictly transactional: see [LG-HW-002](LG-HW-002-TRANSACTIONAL-OUTPUT-WIFI.md) for candidate staging, rollback, and admission formulas.

---

## 4. PCA9685 Synchronous I2C & Fail-Safe Architecture

The 8-channel PWM subsystem is driven by an NXP PCA9685 controller at I2C address `0x55` on `I2C_NUM_0` (SDA: GPIO 21, SCL: GPIO 22, 100 kHz).

### Invariants:
1. **Legacy Synchronous Driver**: Preserves `#include "driver/i2c.h"` synchronous master mode with 100 ms timeouts. Prevents asynchronous queue allocations, race conditions with HTTP workers, and dynamic heap churn.
2. **Output Enable Fail-Safe (`/OE` on GPIO 25)**:
   - Configured as active-low GPIO output.
   - Initialized to logic `HIGH` (disabled/high-impedance) before I2C initialization begins.
   - Only asserted `LOW` after successful PCA9685 register configuration and clean all-off channel initialization.
   - If I2C communication fails or errors exceed thresholds, `/OE` is immediately driven `HIGH`, cutting power/duty to external MOSFET drivers.
3. **Core Pinning**: Initialized exclusively on CPU1 via `OutputCoreExecutor`.

---

## 5. Factory Hardware Coexistence Soak Mode

To qualify deterministic coexistence under maximum stress, firmware provides the `FactoryEffect::HardwareCoexistence` pattern (ID: `hardware_coexistence` or `coexistence`):

- **6 Continuous Addressable Patterns** (cycling every 1000 ms across all 8 lanes × 256 pixels = 2048 LEDs):
  1. *Moving Pixel (Sparse)*: Single pixel traveling across the entire strip to verify WS2812 latch reset margins.
  2. *Alternating*: High-frequency spatial toggles.
  3. *Checkerboard*: Alternating multi-pixel segments.
  4. *Full White / Saturated Color*: Maximum current demand and maximum high-bit RMT symbols.
  5. *All Black*: Complete latch timing verification.
  6. *Deterministic PRNG Pattern*: Pseudo-random data testing symbol decoding variation.
- **Simultaneous 8-Channel PCA9685 Modulation**: Sweeps all 8 PWM channels with phase-offset sine duty cycles.
- **Zero Allocations**: Pre-allocated frame buffers; zero `malloc`/`new` in the 50 Hz render loop.

---

## 6. Telemetry & Diagnostics API

Telemetry is exposed via the authenticated `/api/v1/diagnostics/output` endpoint:

```json
{
  "rmt": {
    "allocation_core": 1,
    "interrupt_priority": 3,
    "iram_safe": true,
    "active_lanes": 8,
    "total_frames": 18000,
    "failed_frames": 0,
    "lanes": [
      {
        "lane": 0,
        "submissions": 18000,
        "completed": 18000,
        "submit_failures": 0,
        "wait_timeouts": 0,
        "other_failures": 0,
        "max_submit_us": 42,
        "max_wait_us": 8200,
        "last_error": "ESP_OK"
      }
    ]
  },
  "pwm": {
    "init_core": 1,
    "transactions": 144000,
    "transaction_failures": 0,
    "consecutive_failures": 0,
    "last_error": "ESP_OK"
  }
}
```

---

## 7. Soak Stress Test Script

The automated stress tool `scripts/hardware_coexistence_soak.py` bombards the node with concurrent network activity while the hardware soak mode runs:

```bash
python scripts/hardware_coexistence_soak.py \
  --host 192.168.4.1 \
  --admin-key <ADMIN_TOKEN> \
  --duration 300 \
  --workers 4
```

### Pass Criteria:
- Duration $\ge 300$ seconds.
- `rmt.failed_frames == 0`
- `rmt.lanes[*].wait_timeouts == 0`
- `pwm.transaction_failures == 0`
- Zero watchdog panics or core resets.

---

## 8. Known Remaining Hardware Risks & Roadmap

1. **RMT Memory Limits on Classic ESP32**:
   - The 8-lane × 64-symbol limit is the physical ceiling for classic ESP32 RMT. Any future channel expansion (e.g., 16 addressable outputs) will require migrating addressable transport to I2S LCD parallel mode (GDMA).
2. **I2C Bus Contention**:
   - The PCA9685 shares `I2C_NUM_0`. Ensure no other high-rate sensors or peripherals are added to this bus to prevent frame render delays.
3. **Power Ground Jitter**:
   - Full-white pattern on 2048 LEDs pulls substantial current. External 5V/12V power distribution must maintain common ground reference to prevent GPIO signal edge degradation.

# LG-HW-002 — Transactional Output & Wi-Fi Fault Containment

**Status**: Implemented & Certified  
**Scope**: Classic ESP32 (Dual Core Xtensa LX6 @ 240MHz, 8MB SPI Flash)  
**Document Owner**: LumiGrid Embedded Firmware Architecture Team  
**Predecessor**: [LG-HW-001 — Deterministic Hardware Coexistence Foundation](file:///c:/Users/slavd/lumigrid/docs/LG-HW-001-RMT-WIFI-PCA-COEXISTENCE.md)

---

## 1. Architectural Mission

LG-HW-001 established fundamental domain separation (Wi-Fi pinned to CPU0, RMT/PCA9685 execution pinned to CPU1, IRAM-safe RMT ISR at priority 3, and legacy synchronous I2C). However, real-world deployment exposed two catastrophic failure modes:
1. **Destructive Output Reconfiguration**: When applying new device configurations or testing topology changes, failures in memory allocation, RMT channel creation, or I2C bus transactions would leave previous healthy output hardware deallocated, blacked out, or marked dead (`topology_valid_ = false`), creating unrecoverable dark states.
2. **Wi-Fi Fallback AP State Poisoning & Destructive NVS Erases**: Subsystem startup failures in `WifiService` or `ConfigStore` previously triggered automatic `nvs_flash_erase()` calls, wiping production calibration, Wi-Fi credentials, and device identities. Furthermore, fallback Access Point (`WIFI_MODE_APSTA`) states never properly transitioned back to pure Station (`WIFI_MODE_STA`) upon upstream router reconnection.

LG-HW-002 introduces **true transactional output lifecycle management**, **deterministic internal SRAM admission gates**, **centralized non-destructive NVS runtime ownership**, and **state-machine corrected Wi-Fi fallback AP containment**.

---

## 2. Memory Admission & Accounting Split

### 2.1 The Two-Pool Problem on Classic ESP32
The ESP32 possesses ~320 KB total SRAM, partitioned into internal data RAM (DRAM) and instruction RAM (IRAM). Due to `CONFIG_RMT_ISR_IRAM_SAFE=y`, RMT transmission buffers, interrupt descriptors, and `StripEncoder` instances **must reside exclusively in internal DRAM** (`MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL | MALLOC_CAP_8BIT`). If internal DRAM drops below ~10–12 KB, Wi-Fi driver packet buffers (`pbuf`), TCP sockets, or FreeRTOS ISR stacks fail immediately, crashing or halting the CPU.

Conversely, generic frame staging buffers, pixel color arrays (`ColorRgbw`), and gamma LUTs do not require internal IRAM safety and can utilize general 8-bit memory.

### 2.2 Memory Admission Formula
Before any output reconfiguration is attempted, `check_output_memory_admission()` calculates the deterministic requirements across all enabled lanes:

$$\text{internal\_bytes} = \sum_{\text{enabled lanes}} \left( \text{pixels}_l \times 3 + \text{kRmtStripEncoderOverhead} + 64 \times 4 \right) + \text{kRmtDriverInternalOverhead}$$

$$\text{generic\_bytes} = \sum_{\text{enabled lanes}} \left( \text{pixels}_l \times \text{sizeof(ColorRgbw)} + \text{sizeof(PixelOrderMapping)} \right) + \text{sizeof(AddressableDriver)}$$

Where:
- $\text{kRmtStripEncoderOverhead} = 400 \text{ bytes}$ per enabled lane (internal DRAM for `rmt_encoder_t` state machine).
- $\text{Wire symbols} = 64 \times 4 = 256 \text{ bytes}$ per lane internal channel descriptor.
- $\text{kPostTopologyInternalReserveBytes} = 12 \times 1024 = 12\,288 \text{ bytes}$ (mandatory reserved headroom for Wi-Fi/LWIP).
- $\text{kGenericReserveBytes} = 16 \times 1024 = 16\,384 \text{ bytes}$.

### 2.3 Strict Admission Gating
Reconfiguration is rejected **prior to touching any hardware or freeing any memory** if:
1. $(\text{free\_internal} - \text{internal\_required}) < \text{internal\_reserve}$
2. $\text{largest\_internal} < \max(\text{lane\_wire\_size})$
3. $(\text{free\_8bit} - \text{generic\_required}) < \text{generic\_reserve}$

Rejected requests return `ESP_ERR_NO_MEM`, log an explicit telemetry line (`OUTPUT_ADMISSION reject reason=...`), increment failure counters, and leave active outputs completely untouched.

---

## 3. 9-Step Transactional Reconfiguration Sequence

Output reconfiguration executes as an atomic 9-step state machine on CPU1:

```
[ Step 1: Validate Config ]
         │ (reject -> abort, keep old)
[ Step 2: Check Memory Admission ]
         │ (reject -> abort, keep old)
[ Step 3: Prepare Staged Candidate ]
         │ (channel create / alloc fail -> cancel candidate, keep old)
         ▼ (PRE-SWAP THRESHOLD: No changes to active outputs occurred yet)
[ Step 4: Gate PCA9685 /OE HIGH ] ────────── Disables external PWM loads
         ▼
[ Step 5: Blackout Old Active Output ] ───── Zeroes LEDs on old topology
         ▼
[ Step 6: Commit / Swap Candidate ] ──────── Swaps active pointer & channels
         │ (post-swap failure triggers rollback!)
[ Step 7: Blackout New Active Output ] ───── Zeroes LEDs on new topology
         │ (failure triggers rollback!)
[ Step 8: Clear PCA9685 Channels ] ───────── Writes all-zero duty to PWM registers
         │ (failure triggers rollback!)
         ▼
[ Step 9: Store Snapshot & Publish ] ─────── topology_valid = true, generation++
```

### 3.1 Pre-Swap Failure Safety
If failure occurs in Steps 1, 2, or 3:
- Candidate structures are destroyed via `cancel_candidate()`.
- Active outputs are **not** blacked out.
- Active output channels remain fully valid and enabled.
- `topology_valid_` remains `true`.
- `topology_generation_` does not increment.
- Reconfigure failure telemetry increments.

### 3.2 Post-Swap Best-Effort Rollback
If a failure occurs during Steps 6, 7, or 8 (after the swap boundary):
1. PCA9685 `/OE` is immediately forced `HIGH` (outputs disabled).
2. `rollback_to_last_good_topology()` is triggered.
3. The driver reads `last_known_good_snapshot_` and restores the previously working lane count, pixel lengths, and color orders.
4. If rollback succeeds:
   - Restored topology is blacked out.
   - PCA is cleared and `/OE` restored.
   - `topology_valid_` remains `true`.
   - `topology_rollbacks_` increments.
5. If rollback fails:
   - `/OE` is latched permanently `HIGH` (safe unpowered state).
   - `topology_valid_` is set to `false`.
   - `topology_rollback_failures_` increments.
   - An alarm is logged to telemetry.

---

## 4. Centralized Storage Ownership (`NvsRuntime`)

### 4.1 Elimination of Destructive NVS Erases
Previously, any initialization failure in `WifiService` (`ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES`) or `ConfigStore` triggered an immediate `nvs_flash_erase()`. Under weak power supplies or transient brownouts, devices would wipe their own configuration.

In LG-HW-002:
- `components/storage/NvsRuntime` is the single centralized authority for NVS initialization.
- Subsystems (`ConfigStore`, `WifiService`, `LumigridRuntime`) call `NvsRuntime::initialise()` idempotently.
- `nvs_flash_erase()` is completely removed from all automated startup sequences.
- If NVS is corrupted or lacks free pages, `NvsRuntime` sets `destructive_recovery_required_ = true` and logs:
  `STORAGE_NVS init_failed reason=... destructiveRecoveryRequired=1`.
- Destructive formatting requires explicit operator confirmation (such as a 5-second physical button press on boot).

---

## 5. Wi-Fi Fallback AP Lifecycle Correctness

### 5.1 Fallback Transition Flow
When station connection fails or credentials fail to connect:
1. `WifiService` enables the Fallback Access Point, switching from `WIFI_MODE_STA` to `WIFI_MODE_APSTA` (or `WIFI_MODE_AP`).
2. Station retry attempts continue in the background using bounded exponential backoff.
3. When station connection succeeds (`IP_EVENT_STA_GOT_IP`):
   - Rather than immediately calling blocking `esp_wifi_set_mode()` inside the FreeRTOS event callback context, `WifiService` arms an asynchronous one-shot timer (`schedule_exit_fallback_ap(500)`).
   - If STA remains connected when the timer fires, `perform_exit_fallback_ap()` calls `esp_wifi_set_mode(WIFI_MODE_STA)`.
   - `is_fallback_ap_` is cleared, and `fallback_exit_attempts_` is updated.
4. If STA disconnects while the exit timer is running, the timer is cancelled and the fallback AP remains alive.

### 5.2 Wi-Fi Diagnostics & Actual Radio Mode
`WifiDiagnostics` reports both logical and true hardware RF state:
- `actual_mode`: Read directly from `esp_wifi_get_mode()`, preventing UI/telemetry drift where firmware claims STA mode while the softAP radio is still transmitting.
- `start_attempts`, `start_failures`
- `reconnect_attempts`, `reconnect_failures`
- `fallback_activations`, `fallback_exit_attempts`, `fallback_exit_failures`
- `disconnect_events`, `last_disconnect_reason`, `last_error`

---

## 6. Output Lock Contention Telemetry

`OutputController::lock()` monitors mutex acquisition latency:
- If `xSemaphoreTakeRecursive(mutex_, 0)` succeeds immediately, no contention occurred.
- If acquisition blocks, high-resolution microsecond timers track wait time:
  - `output_lock_contentions_`: Total count of blocking lock attempts.
  - `output_lock_max_wait_us_`: Peak duration spent waiting for the output mutex.
- `lifecycle_max_us_`: Peak execution time of output reconfiguration or hardware lifecycle operations.

---

## 7. Soak Test Script Lifecycle Management

`scripts/hardware_coexistence_soak.py` implements end-to-end qualification:
1. **Target Topology Validation**: Verifies node is configured for 8 lanes × 256 pixels + 8 PWM channels.
2. **Baseline Telemetry Capture**: Records starting error counts and memory states.
3. **Automated Effect Management**:
   - Posts `POST /api/v1/factory/effect` with `effect: hardware_coexistence`.
   - Continuously polls `GET /api/v1/factory/status` verifying `activeEffect == "hardware_coexistence"`.
   - Always issues `POST /api/v1/factory/abort` in a Python `finally:` block so node is never left in an unmanaged test loop.
4. **Concurrent Load & Wi-Fi Cycling**:
   - Executes 20 Hz telemetry and status polling.
   - Optional `--exercise-wifi-reconnect` triggers station reconnect cycles during heavy rendering.
5. **Delta Validation**:
   - Zero RMT timeouts or dropped frames.
   - Zero PCA9685 I2C errors.
   - Zero reboots or task watchdogs.
   - Internal SRAM reserve $\ge 12 \text{ KB}$ maintained throughout test.

> Historical document preserved on 2026-10-21. Use the [current documentation](../../README.md) for current behavior. Results below apply only to their recorded revision.

# LG-HW-003 — PCA Bus Recovery + RMT Transmission Integrity

## 1. Executive Summary

LG-HW-003 transitions LumiGrid's physical output subsystems from architectural coexistence into active peripheral fault resilience, diagnosis, and transport integrity verification.

Following the stabilization of dual-core memory and lifecycle coexistence in LG-HW-002, HW-003 addresses:
1. **PCA9685 / I2C Bus Recovery**: Eliminating unbounded/100 ms I2C stalls in the 20 ms render path, classifying transport faults via GPIO line inspection, executing standards-based I2C bus clearing (up to 9 SCL pulses with open-drain recovery), verifying chip state registers post-recovery, and strictly upholding the `/OE` safety contract.
2. **RMT Transmission Integrity**: Registering IRAM-safe TX-done event callbacks backed by lock-free internal SRAM ledgers, validating generated RMT symbol counts against wire payload formulas, enforcing submit-to-completion parity, tracking scheduling latency margins against deadline near misses, and classifying overall RMT health.
3. **Qualification Framework**: Providing diagnostic telemetry in `/api/v1/diagnostics/output`, extending the coexistence soak harness with delta counters and qualification classification (`PASS` / `MARGINAL` / `FAIL`), and establishing an empirical decision gate for retaining the 8-lane RMT architecture versus prototyping an I2S-parallel DMA transport.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Transport Integrity vs. Physical Signal Verification**:
> RMT TX-done callbacks and symbol count validation prove that the ESP-IDF/RMT driver and peripheral generated the exact intended symbol stream. They do **not** physically prove that remote LED chips correctly decoded the electrical pulses. True physical signal integrity requires bench oscilloscope/logic analyzer measurement or external loopback.

---

## 2. PCA9685 / I2C Fault Classification & Bus Recovery

### 2.1 Bounded 10 ms Transaction Timeout
The legacy I2C implementation waited up to `pdMS_TO_TICKS(100)` (100 ms) per transaction. In a 20 ms (50 FPS) or 25 ms (40 FPS) lighting schedule, a 100 ms timeout caused catastrophic frame deadline misses and scheduling queue stalls.
At 100 kHz I2C clock speed, a 33-byte PCA9685 multi-byte PWM frame requires ~3.3 ms to transfer.
HW-003 establishes:
```cpp
constexpr uint32_t kPcaTransactionTimeoutMs = 10;
```
This is strictly enforced across register read, register write, multi-byte PWM frame commit, and recovery verification transactions.

### 2.2 Physical Line Telemetry & Fault Classification
Rather than treating every I2C error generically, the driver samples the physical SDA and SCL GPIO levels upon any transaction error:
```cpp
struct PcaBusState {
    bool sda_high;
    bool scl_high;
};
```
Fault conditions are explicitly classified into `PcaFaultKind`:
- `None`: Healthy operation.
- `TransportError`: Generic I2C driver error.
- `Timeout`: Transaction timed out; lines are idle (SCL=HIGH, SDA=HIGH).
- `DeviceNotResponding`: NACK from slave address or registers.
- `SdaStuckLow`: SCL=HIGH, SDA=LOW. A slave device (or PCA9685) was interrupted during a read and holds the SDA line low. Candidate for standard clock-pulsing bus recovery.
- `SclStuckLow`: SCL line is physically pulled low (SCL=LOW). Clock line is held low by external fault or hardware contention. Software must **not** pulse SCL when SCL is stuck low.
- `RegisterVerificationFailed`: PCA registers (`MODE1`, `MODE2`, `PRE_SCALE`) readback does not match expected configuration.
- `RecoveryFailed`: Software bus-clear or chip reconfiguration failed.

### 2.3 Standards-Based SDA-Stuck Bus Clear Algorithm
When `recover_bus()` is invoked:
1. `/OE` remains strictly **HIGH** (outputs disabled).
2. The legacy ESP-IDF I2C driver is safely uninstalled (`i2c_driver_delete(kI2cPort)`).
3. SCL and SDA GPIOs are configured as open-drain outputs with pull-ups enabled. Both lines are released HIGH.
4. Line levels are sampled:
   - If **SCL is LOW**: The bus cannot be cleared via software clock pulses. The driver records `PcaFaultKind::SclStuckLow`, restores I2C driver, leaves `/OE` HIGH, and returns `ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT`.
   - If **SCL is HIGH and SDA is LOW**: The driver sends up to 9 SCL pulses (5 µs low, 5 µs high open-drain). After each pulse, SDA is sampled. As soon as SDA releases HIGH, pulsing terminates immediately.
5. If SDA is successfully released HIGH, a standard I2C STOP condition is generated:
   - Drive SDA LOW
   - Release SCL HIGH (wait 5 µs)
   - Release SDA HIGH (wait 5 µs)
6. The ESP-IDF legacy I2C master driver is cleanly reinstalled (`i2c_param_config` + `i2c_driver_install`).

### 2.4 /OE Safety Contract & Chip Reinitialization
- **Safety Contract**: Physical output enable (`/OE`, active low) must **never** be driven LOW (enabled) during recovery.
- **State Recovery**: Bus recovery alone does not guarantee the PCA retained its PWM oscillator state or registers.
- Recovery sequence strictly verifies:
  1. `MODE1`: `SLEEP = 0`, `AI = 1` (Auto-increment enabled)
  2. `MODE2`: `OUTDRV = 1` (Totem pole output drive)
  3. `PRE_SCALE`: `0x05` (~1017 Hz PWM at 25 MHz oscillator)
  If any register diverges or verification fails, the complete chip initialization sequence is re-executed (Sleep -> Prescale -> Mode2 -> Wake -> 500 µs oscillator wait -> Restart -> Zero frame).
- A zero frame (`ALL_LED_OFF = 4096`) is committed to ensure no glitch upon subsequent output un-gating.
- `/OE` remains strictly HIGH. Only the output engine (`OutputController`) may lower `/OE` after a subsequent valid rendered frame is committed.

### 2.5 CPU1 Output Core Executor Integration
PCA bus recovery operates under the existing `OutputCoreExecutor` pinned exclusively to CPU1:
```cpp
esp_err_t execute_pca_recovery(OutputController* controller);
```
Recovery cannot execute concurrently with output commits or topology reconfigurations. When `LightingRuntime::clear_output_fault()` detects `OutputFaultDomain::PcaI2c`, it schedules PCA recovery on CPU1 and re-arms output only upon verified completion.

---

## 3. RMT Transmission Integrity Architecture

### 3.1 IRAM-Safe TX-Done Callbacks
In ESP-IDF 5.2, RMT channel completions can trigger registered callbacks:
```cpp
rmt_tx_register_event_callbacks(chan, &callbacks, &user_data);
```
HW-003 establishes an atomic ledger residing permanently in internal SRAM (`DRAM_ATTR static RmtIsrLedger s_ledgers[8]`):
```cpp
struct RmtIsrLedger {
    std::atomic<uint32_t> completions{0};
    std::atomic<uint32_t> last_num_symbols{0};
};
static_assert(std::atomic<uint32_t>::is_always_lock_free);
```
The callback is attributed with `IRAM_ATTR`:
```cpp
static bool IRAM_ATTR on_rmt_tx_done(
    rmt_channel_handle_t channel,
    const rmt_tx_done_event_data_t* event,
    void* user_data
) {
    if (user_data && event) {
        auto* ledger = static_cast<RmtIsrLedger*>(user_data);
        ledger->completions.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        ledger->last_num_symbols.store(static_cast<uint32_t>(event->num_symbols), std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    return false;
}
```
**Strict ISR Safety Rules**:
- Zero heap allocations (`malloc`, `free`, `new`).
- Zero logging calls (`ESP_LOG*`).
- Zero blocking operations or FreeRTOS queues.
- Execution time < 1 µs.

### 3.2 Symbol Count Formula Validation
Each WS2812/SK6812 frame generated by LumiGrid's custom encoder consists of:
- 1 symbol per bit of pixel wire data (`wire_len * 8`)
- 1 symbol for the reset/latch code
- 1 EOF symbol appended by the ESP-IDF driver
```cpp
expected_symbols = wire_len * 8 + 2;
```
For 256 pixels:
- **RGB (WS2812)**: 768 wire bytes $\to$ $768 \times 8 + 2 = 6,146$ symbols.
- **RGBW (SK6812)**: 1024 wire bytes $\to$ $1024 \times 8 + 2 = 8,194$ symbols.

If `actual_symbols != expected_symbols`, the driver marks the lane and frame as `Faulted` and increments `symbol_count_mismatches`. The frame is not accepted merely because the driver wait returned `ESP_OK`.

### 3.3 Submit-to-Completion Parity
Each lane maintains `submitted_generation` (incremented on each successful RMT submit) and compares it against the ISR-updated `completions` counter after bounded wait:
```cpp
if (completed_gen != L.submitted_generation) {
    ldiag.completion_mismatches++;
    L.state = LaneState::Faulted;
}
```
Any discrepancy indicates missed interrupts or buffer state drift, immediately faulting the lane.

### 3.4 Latency & Deadline Margin Instrumentation
- **Wire Overhead**: Tracks `overhead_us = wait_us - wire_time_us`, recording `max_wait_over_wire_us`.
- **Near-Deadline Near Misses**: A threshold margin of 3 ms:
  ```cpp
  constexpr uint32_t kRmtNearDeadlineMarginUs = 3000;
  ```
  If actual completion occurs within 3000 µs of the timeout expiration budget, `deadline_near_misses` is incremented. This provides an early warning indicator that interrupt refill or Wi-Fi CPU0/1 contention is encroaching on the 64-symbol hardware buffer limit.

### 3.5 RMT Health Classification
- `Faulted`: Any frame failure, timeout, completion mismatch, or symbol count mismatch.
- `Marginal`: Zero functional failures, but `deadline_near_misses > 0`.
- `Healthy`: Zero failures and full timing margin.

---

## 4. Diagnostics & API Schema

The `/api/v1/diagnostics/output` endpoint exposes the complete HW-003 telemetry model:
```json
{
  "output": {
    "faultDomain": "none",
    "topologyValid": true,
    "topologyGeneration": 1
  },
  "rmt": {
    "health": "healthy",
    "frames": 90000,
    "failedFrames": 0,
    "deadlineNearMisses": 0,
    "lanes": [
      {
        "lane": 0,
        "submissions": 90000,
        "completed": 90000,
        "txDoneCallbacks": 90000,
        "completionMismatches": 0,
        "symbolMismatches": 0,
        "lastExpectedSymbols": 6146,
        "lastActualSymbols": 6146,
        "maxSubmitUs": 142,
        "maxWaitUs": 8015,
        "maxWaitOverWireUs": 55,
        "deadlineNearMisses": 0,
        "lastError": 0
      }
    ]
  },
  "pwm": {
    "healthy": true,
    "recoveryRequired": false,
    "lastFaultKind": "none",
    "transactions": 90010,
    "transactionFailures": 0,
    "recoveryAttempts": 0,
    "recoverySuccesses": 0,
    "recoveryFailures": 0,
    "busClearAttempts": 0,
    "busClearSuccesses": 0,
    "busClearFailures": 0,
    "driverReinstalls": 0,
    "lastSdaHigh": true,
    "lastSclHigh": true,
    "lastTransactionUs": 3120,
    "maxTransactionUs": 3304
  }
}
```

---

## 5. Qualification Framework: PASS / MARGINAL / FAIL

The coexistence soak script (`scripts/hardware_coexistence_soak.py`) evaluates post-soak delta counters:

| Metric | PASS | MARGINAL | FAIL |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Device Resets** | 0 | 0 | $\ge 1$ |
| **RMT Failed Frames** | 0 | 0 | $\ge 1$ |
| **RMT Completion Mismatches** | 0 | 0 | $\ge 1$ |
| **RMT Symbol Mismatches** | 0 | 0 | $\ge 1$ |
| **RMT Deadline Near Misses** | 0 | $> 0$ | Any timeout |
| **PCA Failures / Recovery Failures** | 0 | 0 | $\ge 1$ |
| **Topology Drift / Validity** | 0 drift, valid | 0 drift, valid | Invalid or drifted |
| **Internal DRAM Reserve** | $\ge 12\text{ KB}$ | $\ge 12\text{ KB}$ | $< 12\text{ KB}$ |
| **Wi-Fi State Drift** | 0 | 0 | APSTA without fallback |

---

## 6. Decision Gate: 8-Lane RMT vs. I2S Parallel Prototype

LumiGrid uses all 8 classic ESP32 RMT blocks allocated as $8 \times 64$ symbols (512 symbols total).
Following a 1-hour physical soak run under maximum network and rendering load:

### Keep Current 8-Lane RMT Architecture If:
1. 0 RMT failed frames.
2. 0 symbol count mismatches.
3. 0 completion parity mismatches.
4. `deadlineNearMisses` rate is effectively zero.
5. Stable Wi-Fi STA throughput and frame rate without core stalls.

### Trigger I2S-Parallel Transport Migration If:
1. Reproducible symbol corruption or completion mismatches under Wi-Fi traffic.
2. `deadlineNearMisses` consistently accumulate, demonstrating that 64 symbols offer inadequate refill buffer time during flash/cache or radio activity.
3. Sustained 8-lane operation cannot coexist with HTTP and network load without dropping frames.

# LG-HW-004 — Electrical Boot Safety + Power-Step Control + Reset Forensics

## 1. Executive Summary

LG-HW-004 resolves electrical transients, boot-time output glitches, and post-reset recovery below the normal driver layer.

Prior to LG-HW-004, the controller presented several electrical and forensic risks:
1. **Boot Glitches & Floating Pins**: Between MCU power-on and driver initialization, the PCA9685 `/OE` line could float or be driven low by pull-downs, and addressable LED data lines (A1–A8) floated, resulting in flash bursts or random color artifacts on connected LED fixtures.
2. **First-Frame Output Transients**: Output drivers could transmit normal lighting frames before zero/black output was established on the wire.
3. **Reset-Loop Misclassification**: Warm reboots (OTA updates, operator software restarts) were lumped into a single boot counter, causing false trips into Safe Mode.
4. **Brownout & Watchdog Forensics**: Brownout events and watchdog resets were not tracked with RTC memory forensics or early serial banners.
5. **Sudden Inrush Power Steps**: Large lighting steps (e.g., cold boot directly into 100% white, or blackout exit) caused severe current spikes on the DC power bus, potentially triggering power supply collapse or brownout resets during Wi-Fi association transients.
6. **Unsafe Post-Abnormal Reboot Restoration**: After a panic, brownout, or watchdog crash, the system could immediately slam the power rails with heavy load before power supplies and networking stabilized.

HW-004 resolves all of these failure modes while strictly maintaining:
- 8 × Addressable LED lanes (WS2812/SK6812)
- 8 × PCA9685 PWM channels (100 kHz I2C, address 0x55)
- 8 × 64 RMT symbol architecture with CPU0/CPU1 core affinity split
- Unchanged API surfaces and binary footprint bounds

---

## 2. Early Electrical Output Safety (`BoardOutputSafety`)

### 2.1 Earliest Application Entry Point
At the very beginning of `app_main()`, before any other subsystem (NVS, Wi-Fi, logging, heap allocation, I2C, or RMT), `lg::board::force_outputs_safe_early()` is executed:

```cpp
esp_err_t force_outputs_safe_early() {
    // 1. Immediately drive PCA /OE HIGH (disable PWM channels)
    gpio_reset_pin(kPcaOe);
    gpio_set_direction(kPcaOe, GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT);
    gpio_set_level(kPcaOe, 1);
    s_diag.pca_oe_high_at_bootstrap = (gpio_get_level(kPcaOe) == 1);

    // 2. Drive all 8 ALED pins LOW so they do not float before RMT takes ownership
    s_diag.aled_low_mask = 0;
    for (uint8_t i = 0; i < kAledCount; ++i) {
        gpio_num_t pin = kAledPins[i];
        gpio_reset_pin(pin);
        gpio_set_direction(pin, GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT);
        gpio_set_level(pin, 0);
        if (gpio_get_level(pin) == 0) {
            s_diag.aled_low_mask |= static_cast<uint8_t>(1u << i);
        }
    }

    s_diag.early_safety_applied = true;
    return ESP_OK;
}
```

### 2.2 Electrical State Guarantees
- **PCA9685 `/OE`**: Pin `GPIO_NUM_25` is immediately driven **HIGH** (logic 1), forcing all PCA9685 output MOSFETs/drivers into high-impedance / disabled state.
- **ALED Pins (A1–A8)**: `GPIO_NUM_16, 4, 17, 18, 19, 23, 26, 27` are driven **LOW** (logic 0). WS2812/SK6812 protocol requires data low at idle (>280 µs reset pulse). Driving them LOW eliminates floating high-impedance states that cause first-pixel false triggers.
- **No `gpio_hold_en`**: Normal GPIO output mode without RTC hold registers prevents latching pins into un-reconfigurable states during peripheral driver initialization.

---

## 3. First-Black & First-Zero Output Confirmation Gates

### 3.1 ParallelRmtDriver First-Black Frame Contract
To eliminate transient color flashes upon driver bring-up, `ParallelRmtDriver` enforces a first-black gate:
1. `first_black_frame_confirmed_` is initialized to `false`.
2. Any `commit()` call containing non-zero pixel wire data before a verified all-zero frame has completed is rejected with `ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE`.
3. When an all-zero (black) frame successfully completes across all configured lanes, `first_black_frame_confirmed_` transitions to `true` and records telemetry via `lg::board::record_first_addressable_black()`.
4. The gate resets to `false` on any driver reconfiguration, release, or fault clearing.

### 3.2 Pca9685Driver Zero-First Output Enable Contract
The PCA9685 hardware output enable (`/OE` active low) is governed by a strict zero-first rule:
1. `enable_outputs(true)` asserts `zero_confirmed_`. If a zero frame has not yet been committed to chip registers, `/OE` is kept HIGH.
2. In both `init()` and `recover()`, `ALL_LED_OFF = 4096` is committed over I2C to write zero duty to all channels, and `lg::board::record_first_pwm_zero()` is called.
3. `/OE` is lowered only after the software output controller verifies valid frame generation.

---

## 4. RTC Reset Forensics & Safe Mode Classification

### 4.1 RTC-Backed Boot State
A dedicated struct resides in RTC slow memory:
```cpp
struct RtcBootState {
    uint32_t magic;                       // 0x4C474253 ('LGBS')
    uint32_t total_boots;
    uint32_t consecutive_abnormal_boots;
    uint32_t last_boot_sequence;
    bool     previous_boot_reached_ready;
};
```
If `magic != kRtcBootMagic` (power loss, cold boot), the state is cleanly initialized.

### 4.2 Abnormal vs Normal Reset Classification
Reset reasons are classified according to root cause:
- **Abnormal Resets**:
  - `ESP_RST_PANIC` (Software crash / assertion / abort)
  - `ESP_RST_INT_WDT` (Interrupt watchdog timeout)
  - `ESP_RST_TASK_WDT` (Task watchdog timeout)
  - `ESP_RST_WDT` (Other watchdog resets)
  - `ESP_RST_BROWNOUT` (VDD droop below brownout detector threshold)
  - Increments `consecutive_abnormal_boots`.
- **Normal Resets**:
  - `ESP_RST_POWERON` (Cold power switch on)
  - `ESP_RST_SW` (Clean software reboot / OTA restart / operator reboot)
  - `ESP_RST_DEEPSLEEP`
  - Does **not** increment `consecutive_abnormal_boots`.

### 4.3 Safe Mode Criterion & Healthy Boot Confirmation
- **Safe Mode Trigger**: Mandated **only** when `consecutive_abnormal_boots >= 3`. Normal reboots can never trigger Safe Mode.
- **Healthy Boot Dwell**: After reaching `StartupState::Ready`, the runtime task dwells for 30,000 ms. Once 30 seconds of stable operation elapse, `lg::board::confirm_healthy_boot()` is called, resetting `consecutive_abnormal_boots = 0` and recording `previous_boot_reached_ready = true`.

### 4.4 Early Serial Banner & Brownout Detector
Before logging or Wi-Fi start, a structured serial banner is output:
```text
BOOT_RESET reason=power_on abnormal=0 consecutive=0 total=1 previousReady=0 session=0x4C470001
```
`sdkconfig.defaults` explicitly mandates:
```text
CONFIG_ESP_BROWNOUT_DET=y
```
A compile-time `#error` check in `ResetForensics.hpp` prevents building firmware with brownout protection disabled.

---

## 5. Bounded Power-Step Control (`PowerBudget`)

### 5.1 Per-Frame Power Step Limitation
To protect power supplies and prevent ground bounce / voltage droop, `PowerBudget` enforces a ramp rate limit:
```cpp
max_step_mw = max_power_mw * frame_period_ms / ramp_ms;
```
- Default `ramp_ms = 750 ms`.
- For a 100 W budget at 25 ms frame period, maximum allowable increase per frame is:
  $$\Delta P_{\max} = 100{,}000 \times \frac{25}{750} \approx 3{,}333\text{ mW}$$
- Current granted power cannot exceed `previous_granted_power + max_step_mw`.

### 5.2 Global Proportional Scaling
When power is restricted by step limiting or the total budget:
- Both addressable color brightness ($R, G, B, W$) and PWM channel duty cycles ($0.0 \dots 1.0$) are scaled globally by a uniform factor $S$:
  $$S = \frac{P_{\text{granted}}}{P_{\text{requested}}}$$
- Relative color balance and channel-to-channel ratios are preserved exactly. Channels are **not** turned on sequentially or in a staircase pattern.

### 5.3 Soft-Start Triggers on High-Risk Transitions
`restart_soft_start()` is invoked to reset granted power to 0 mW and begin the 750 ms ramp on:
1. Boot un-quarantine / output enable.
2. Blackout exit.
3. Channel topology reconfiguration.
4. Scene / preset change.
5. Manual override engagement.
6. Fault recovery re-arming.
7. Wi-Fi connection association / reconnect transient events.

---

## 6. Abnormal Reset Output Quarantine

When an abnormal reset (`BROWNOUT`, `PANIC`, `WDT`) occurs:
- Physical lighting output is placed under a **1000 ms quarantine dwell**.
- Addressable LEDs remain black; PCA `/OE` remains HIGH.
- Wi-Fi, HTTP API, network discovery, and diagnostics boot normally with zero delay.
- Once uptime reaches 1000 ms, quarantine expires, and `LightingRuntime` automatically initiates soft-start ramping.

---

## 7. Diagnostics & Verification Endpoints

### 7.1 `/api/v1/diagnostics/output`
Extended with four diagnostic blocks:
- `reset`: `reason`, `reasonStr`, `abnormal`, `consecutiveAbnormalBoots`, `totalBoots`, `previousBootReady`, `currentBootConfirmed`, `safeModeMandated`, `quarantineActive`, `bootSessionId`, `brownoutDetectorEnabled`.
- `bootOutput`: `earlySafetyApplied`, `pcaOeHighAtBootstrap`, `aledLowMask`, `firstAddressableBlackConfirmed`, `firstPwmZeroConfirmed`, `firstOutputCommitMs`.
- `powerTransient`: `lastRequestedMw`, `lastGrantedMw`, `maxStepMw`, `powerRampActive`, `rampElapsedMs`, `rampTargetMs`, `stepClamps`, `wifiTransientClamps`, `quarantineClamps`.
- `activationTiming`: `quarantineDwellMs`, `quarantineExpired`, `softStartElapsedMs`, `outputsArmed`, `firstSafeFrameMs`.

### 7.2 `/api/v1/factory/boot-safe`
Returns bench verification state:
```json
{
  "oeLevel": 1,
  "oeHigh": true,
  "addressableMask": 0,
  "addressableAllLow": true,
  "resetReason": "power_on",
  "abnormalReset": false,
  "brownoutDetectorEnabled": true,
  "outputsArmed": true,
  "quarantineActive": false,
  "firstBlackConfirmed": true,
  "firstZeroConfirmed": true
}
```

---

## 8. Verification & Qualification Results

1. **Invariants Validation (`check_invariants.py`)**: Passed with 0 errors. Verified early safety call order, GPIO pin sets, brownout detector requirement, first-black frame gating, and absence of warm-boot safe mode.
2. **PlatformIO Test Environment (`pio run -e test`)**: Compiles and runs all runtime hardening test suites including `test_lghw004_boot_safety_power_and_forensics()`.
3. **Soak Test Lifecycle Harness (`scripts/hardware_coexistence_soak.py`)**: Enhanced with `bootSessionId` session tracking and classified reboot reporting (`FAIL: POWER/BROWNOUT`, `FAIL: PANIC`, `FAIL: TASK_WDT`, `FAIL: INT_WDT`).
