# LumiGrid Runtime Certification Status

> **Target Base Commit**: `ea586e39aca19df0d051e2534cf336c73316f582`
> **Date**: October 2026
> **Scope**: Certification Hardening, Lifecycle Integrity, Concurrency Safety, Runtime Snapshot Authority, and Verification Status.
> **Certification Stage**: Pre-Hardware Verification (Architecture & Simulation Complete). Full certification is **NOT** claimed until physical hardware milestones are completed.

---

## 1. Runtime Invariant Verification Matrix

| Category | Invariant Description | Status | Verification Level |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Lifecycle** | Transactional `start()`: Synchronous initialization with sequential rollback on failure | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Integration |
| **Lifecycle** | Zero `ESP_ERROR_CHECK()` in runtime startup and infrastructure paths | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Static CI |
| **Lifecycle** | Cooperative `stop()`: Task observes shutdown signal and completes before state destruction | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Integration |
| **Lifecycle** | Double-start rejection with `ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE` and deterministic repeated stops | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Lifecycle** | Instance-scoped `services_started_` (zero process-global static state) | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Factory** | Transactional startup: queue, mutex, and task allocations rollback on partial failure | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Factory** | Serialized command transition pipeline (`validate -> state -> ownership -> output`) | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Integration |
| **Factory** | Strict decoupling: Factory Abort releases ownership and blacks out WITHOUT activating E-Stop | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Output** | Scoped Output Transaction API (`begin_transaction` / `commit`) with RAII auto-unlock | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Output** | Unified commit fault owner: physical commit failure drives `Healthy -> Faulted -> Armed -> Healthy` | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Integration |
| **Protocols** | Deterministic LTP tie-breaking on same-millisecond arrivals via monotonic `arrival_seq` | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Protocols** | Safe timestamp wraparound comparison using bounded `elapsed_ms(now, then)` | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Simulated |
| **Protocols** | Strict 4-source bounded capacity policy (5th rejected, live sources never overwritten) | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Protocols** | DMX universe timeout without packets via `DmxRouter::tick()` maintenance loop | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Integration |
| **Protocols** | Single authoritative universe patch collector: `Art-Net == sACN == DmxRouter` | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Protocols** | Art-Net 4 15-bit Port-Address serialization (NetSwitch @ 18, SubSwitch @ 19, SwOut @ 190..193) | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Observability** | Purely observational `/api/v1/health`: zero NVS reads/writes, zero hardware operations | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Observability** | Real-time diagnostic startup state (`startup_state`, `startup_stage`, `failing_stage`, `failing_error`) | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Integration |
| **Security** | Production credentials policy: non-universal AP recovery credential (no static `"lumigrid123"`) | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Static CI |
| **Hardware** | Factory recovery button: 3s grace period, 20ms debounce, stuck pin protection, safe blackout | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Simulated |
| **Transport** | Show Transport v2 explicit state machine: Scene, Timeline, Cue preemption with generation tracking | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Transport** | NodeSync protocol v4 (60-byte packed frame): leader-authoritative cues, remote BPM, clock sync | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Transport** | Follower local playback suppression and 409 `sync_follower_read_only` guard | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Parity** | Manifest schema 2: separation of playback parity (`playbackHash`) from optional schedule parity | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |
| **Network** | Deterministic CRC calculation: field-by-field hashing in defined order eliminating padding artifacts | `[PASS]` | Compile Verified, Unit Test |

## 2. Invariant Detail & Verification Results

### 2.1 Lifecycle & Shutdown Safety
- **Synchronous Lifecycle**: `LumigridRuntime::start()` executes synchronous network wait, API startup, mDNS discovery, protocol listeners (Art-Net/sACN), and background services sequentially. Any failure halts progression, executes reverse-order teardown via `rollback_services()`, blackouts outputs, enters `Faulted` state, and returns the error code without crashing the MCU.
- **Cooperative Shutdown**: `LightingRuntime::stop()` sets `shutting_down_ = true`, aborts blocking delays, waits for the task to complete via `shutdown_sem_`, and only then safely deletes runtime-owned synchronization primitives.
- **No Double-Start**: Both `LumigridRuntime` and `LightingRuntime` reject repeated `start()` invocations with `ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE`. Multiple calls to `stop()` are idempotent.

### 2.2 Protocol Correctness & Serialization
- **Art-Net 4 Spec Adherence**: ArtPollReply serialization strictly formats 15-bit Port-Addresses:
  - Universe 1: `Net=0, SubNet=0, SwOut[0]=1`
  - Universe 16: `Net=0, SubNet=1, SwOut[0]=0`
  - Universe 255: `Net=0, SubNet=15, SwOut[0]=15`
  - Universe 512: `Net=2, SubNet=0, SwOut[0]=0`
- **Deterministic LTP**: Packet arrival sequencing assigns a monotonic 64-bit `arrival_seq` to every incoming packet, breaking timestamp ties deterministically when packets arrive within the same millisecond.
- **Bounded Capacity**: Bounded at 4 concurrent active sources per universe. A 5th source is rejected and increments `sources_dropped` without evicting active transmitters.

### 2.3 Output & Safety Architecture
- **Output Transaction RAII**: All frame staging occurs inside `OutputTransaction` objects acquiring the hardware lock once. Staging methods (`pixels()`, `pwm()`) are scoped to the transaction, and `commit()` invokes the physical driver commit pipeline.
- **Unified Fault State Transition**: Physical commit failures immediately trigger the `CommitObserver`, advancing `LightingRuntime` output state to `Faulted` and recording distinct metrics for failed commits and fault events.

### 2.4 Show Transport v2 & NodeSync v4
- **Single Explicit Transport Coordinator**: `ShowTransportCoordinator` models explicit Scene, Timeline, and Cue List playback, eliminating hidden competing playback sources.
- **NodeSync Protocol v4**: Transmits packed 60-byte UDP packets with leader-authoritative cue lists, random progression, hold/fade duration, and manual crossfade progress.
- **Follower Guard**: Active followers reject direct playback activations with HTTP 409 `sync_follower_read_only` while permitting show asset editing.

### 2.5 Network Commissioning & Live Network Lifecycle (LG-028)
- **Deterministic Checksum**: `calc_network_settings_crc()` computes CRC32 by feeding explicit fields in fixed order (`schema_version`, `mode`, `sta_ssid`, `sta_password`, `ap_name`, `ap_channel`) into `esp_rom_crc32_le()`, preventing compiler padding and checksum fields from causing false corruption detections.
- **Dual-Slot Persistence with Self-Healing**: `ConfigStore` reads primary slot `"network"` with strict `schema_version == 1` enforcement. Upon CRC failure or version mismatch, it falls back to `"network_b"` and heals the primary slot automatically.
- **Strict Input Validation**: Endpoints enforce RFC/Wi-Fi constraints: SSIDs must be 1..32 bytes (required for STA modes), passwords 8..63 bytes (or 0 for open networks), AP channels strictly 1..13 (channel 14 rejected with 400 `invalid_ap_channel`), and strict JSON types.
- **Asynchronous Apply Lifecycle**: `PUT /api/v1/network/config` validates input, journals command ID, enqueues request via `queue_network_apply()`, and responds with `202 Accepted` (`{"accepted":true,"commandId":N,"applyPending":true}`). Concurrent apply requests return `409 Conflict`.
- **Transactional Rollback**: The runtime-owned `net_apply_worker` holds both previous and desired settings. If the desired network cannot become ready within the timeout, it restores previous runtime settings without modifying persisted NVS. Configuration is persisted only upon verified network readiness.
- **Zero Blackout Network Service Rebind**: When switching networks, network-dependent services (MQTT, NodeSync, sACN, Art-Net, mDNS, API) are stopped and rebound sequentially. `LightingRuntime`, `OutputController`, DMX routing, and active hardware outputs remain uninterrupted throughout.
- **Intentional Disconnect Handling**: `WifiService` maintains `intentional_disconnect_` (`std::atomic<bool>`) so administrative reconfigurations do not trigger the automatic reconnect retry loop.
- **StaWithApFallback Lifecycle**: If STA fails to connect under `StaWithApFallback`, the recovery AP is activated for operator access, and a FreeRTOS timer performs bounded exponential backoff retries (`5s -> 10s -> 30s -> 60s -> capped at 60s`) until STA connects.
- **Safe-Mode Recovery Guard**: When `safe_mode_` is active, non-recovery network reconfigurations are rejected with `400 safe_mode_network_locked`.

### 2.6 Canonical Runtime State & API v1 Cutover (LG-031)
- **Side-Effect Free Collection**: `collect_runtime_snapshot` reads atomic state and acquires minimal locks purely for observation. Zero state transitions, zero command journal mutations, and zero hardware operations occur during telemetry collection or serialization.
- **Authoritative Single State Contract**: Schema 3 `RuntimeSnapshot` is shared identically between HTTP `GET /api/v1/status` and authenticated WebSocket (`/ws`) broadcasts. Both channels deliver bit-compatible JSON payloads with identical field hierarchy (`system`, `output`, `dmx`, `network`, `transport`, `hardware`).
- **Bounded Buffer Safety**: Serialization uses `FixedJsonWriter` within a strict 8192-byte stack/heap budget. Overflow detection truncates safely with failure-awareness rather than causing buffer overflows or unbounded dynamic allocations.
- **Coalesced Status Broadcasting**: Status changes trigger WebSocket broadcasts through an atomic `status_pending_` CAS loop, rate-limited to a maximum of 5 Hz (200 ms). Preview frames are transmitted at up to 30 Hz.
- **Zero Process-Global Statics**: Rate limiting and timing tracking use instance-scoped `std::atomic<uint32_t>` members (`last_preview_ms_`, `last_status_broadcast_ms_`) in `FactoryApi`, guaranteeing multi-instance thread safety.
- **DMX Payload Decoupling**: Static capabilities (`CapabilitiesManifest`) are removed from live status to eliminate bandwidth waste, and raw DMX channel frames are decoupled into a dedicated `GET /api/v1/dmx/frame` endpoint restricted to `Installer+` role.

### 2.7 Scene Studio v2 & Safe Persistence (LG-032)
- **Safe Persistence Invariant**: Modifying or saving a scene preset via `PUT /api/v1/presets` persists data strictly to NVS. The active physical output remains completely unaltered until an explicit activation request (`POST /api/v1/show/control` or `POST /api/v1/activate`) is issued.
- **Optimistic Concurrency & Conflict Protection**: Scene saves accept `expectedChecksum`. If the stored scene CRC32 differs, the endpoint responds with `409 Conflict` containing `currentChecksum`, preventing silent clobbering of edits.
- **Dependency-Protected Deletion**: `DELETE /api/v1/presets?index=N` checks whether the target preset is in use by any step in the sequence or any cue in the cue lists. Active dependencies abort deletion with `400 Bad Request` and detailed reference metadata.

### 2.8 Timeline Studio v2 — Anchored Transport & Safe Playback (LG-033)
- **Persistence / Playback Decoupling**: `PUT /api/v1/sequence` persists validated Schema 2 Timeline documents. It does not start, stop, or mutate active playback, active sequence snapshots, or anchor timestamps.
- **Immutable Active Sequence Snapshot**: Triggering RUN (`POST /api/v1/show/control` with `mode: "timeline"`) copies the latest persisted sequence into `active_sequence_`. Subsequent saves while running modify persisted storage but do NOT alter `active_sequence_`.
- **Anchored Deterministic Timing**: Playback starts deterministically at Beat 0 from an explicit anchor timestamp (`timeline_anchor_ms`). Elapsed time is calculated as `current_clock_ms >= anchor_ms ? current_clock_ms - anchor_ms : 0`, and total beats as `elapsed_ms / ms_per_beat`.
- **NodeSync Protocol v5**: Packets extend to 68 bytes, transmitting `transport_generation`, `timeline_anchor_ms`, and `timeline_checksum`. Followers compare local timeline checksum against the leader's active checksum, failing closed (`SyncTransportError::TimelineMismatch`) on mismatch.
- **Late-Joining Follower Synchrony**: Late followers compute `elapsed = disciplinedClock - leaderAnchor` to seamlessly synchronize to the active playback phase without restarting from Beat 0.

### 2.9 Cue Studio v2 & Cue Runtime Hardening (LG-034)
- **Single-Lock Snapshot Runtime**: `CueRunner::snapshot(now_ms)` is the exclusive read contract (Scheduler transport snapshots, Factory API, and the RuntimeSnapshot collector all consume it). Former unlocked accessors (`is_running()`, `state()`, `current_list()`, index getters) were removed; a static-invariant check (scripts/check_invariants.py) blocks their reintroduction. The legacy deadlock — calling `stop()` from inside `update()` on natural completion — is structurally eliminated via lock-aware internal helpers.
- **Stop Semantics**: Every stop carries a typed reason. Operator stops and preemptions hold the current output; only natural completion of the final cue executes the configured end action (`hold_last`, `blackout`, `restore_fallback`).
- **Pause/Fade Freeze**: Pausing captures hold/fade anchors before the state change and freezes the in-flight transition via `SceneManager::freeze_transition()`; resuming continues the frozen morph over the remaining time. Pause→resume never restarts or snaps the visual.
- **Save/Run Separation**: RUN snapshots the latest saved list into an immutable active copy with its own checksum and monotonic generation. Saves while running flip `contentStale` only. `restart` re-snapshots with a fresh generation and no end-action transient. Backup/restore writes content only; running cue state is never restored.
- **Content Protection**: Strict schema-2 validation (UTF-8 byte caps, bounded timing, strict enums, scene-existence checks) plus `409 cue_list_conflict` optimistic concurrency and `409 cue_list_in_use` dependency-safe deletion.
- **NodeSync v6**: 76-byte packed frames add `cue_list_checksum`, `cue_transition_progress_q15`, `cue_paused_from`, and `cue_source_scene`. Followers fail closed on cue content divergence (`SyncTransportError::CueListMismatch`) and reconstruct paused fades from leader progress. Protocol version verification status is firmware-level (compile + unit tests); see Section 4 for the hardware bench scope.

---

## 3. Remaining Hardware Verification Milestones

The software architecture and simulation boundaries are fully hardened. The runtime now strictly requires physical hardware validation on reference test fixtures before claiming full certification.

- [ ] **Actual RMT Output Verification**:
  - Verify WS2812 / SK6812 signal integrity on an oscilloscope (timing parameters: $T0H = 350\text{ns} \pm 150\text{ns}$, $T1H = 900\text{ns} \pm 150\text{ns}$).
  - Verify 8 parallel RMT channels under maximum pixel load (8 x 256 pixels @ 40 FPS with true parallel submission).
- [ ] **Actual PCA9685 Output Verification**:
  - Verify I2C bus clock stretching, waveform shape, and standard-mode (100 kHz) stability.
  - Verify output enable (OE) physical pull-down and PWM duty accuracy from 0 to 4095 (~1017 Hz PWM).
- [ ] **Physical Art-Net Source Validation**:
  - Test real Art-Net controller broadcast and unicast streaming at 44 Hz continuous.
  - Verify ArtPoll / ArtPollReply round-trip and node discovery in QLC+ and Madrix.
- [ ] **Physical sACN Source Validation**:
  - Verify IGMPv2/v3 multicast group membership joining and leaving on physical managed switch.
  - Test multi-console priority preemption (Priority 100 vs Priority 150).
- [ ] **Hardware Emergency Stop**:
  - Runtime/software E-stop + direct PCA /OE cutoff (no dedicated physical E-stop GPIO on current board revision).
  - Assert zero PWM output immediately (<1 µs via direct GPIO `/OE` cutoff).
  - Addressable blackout is protocol-bound to serial frame wire transmission (~7.68 ms WS2812 / ~10.24 ms SK6812 for 256 pixels); physical $< 5\text{ms}$ addressable cutoff requires future hardware power-gate / load switch.
- [ ] **Factory Hardware Test Output**:
  - Execute factory direct RGBW pattern and verify physical color balance and gamma response across sequenced stages.
- [ ] **Thermal and Power Budget Verification**:
  - Validate dynamic power limiter on calibrated DC power supply (assert total draw does not exceed configured `max_power_mw`).
- [ ] **24h / 72h Continuous Burn-in Run**:
  - Continuous 72-hour test at 40 FPS under maximum load with 4 concurrent DMX streams.
  - Assert 0 memory leaks, 0 dropped frames, and zero unexpected watchdog restarts.

---

## 4. Multi-Node Fleet Sync & Show Transport Hardware Test Matrix (LG-025 & LG-026)

> **Hardware Requirements:** Minimum 2 physical nodes required; 3 physical nodes preferred.
> **Timing Certification Gate:** Do NOT mark cluster timing accuracy certified until physical frame-to-frame offset is measured on physical oscilloscope/logic analyzer probes across multiple hardware nodes.

## 5. Security & Transport Notice (LG-029)

With the completion of LG-029 (Node-Backed Authentication, Sessions & Credential Provisioning):
- The firmware is the sole authority for authentication and authorization (`AuthStore` + `AuthManager`).
- Browser PIN-checking authority, hardcoded dev tokens (`lumigrid_admin`), and credential restoration backdoors are permanently removed.
- Ephemeral session management (256-bit entropy, 30 min idle / 8 hr absolute timeout) is enforced on the node.
- WebSocket connections require single-use pre-handshake tickets (`Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: lumigrid-ticket.<ticket>`).

> [!WARNING]
> **Transport Security Limitation:**
> HTTP on an untrusted LAN does not provide confidentiality against packet interception. Bearer tokens and API keys transmitted over plaintext HTTP are susceptible to network eavesdropping on an untrusted or open network. Production deployments requiring transport encryption require dedicated network isolation or future TLS capabilities.

## 6. Stop Condition Notice

With the completion of LG-024 (Live Desk Hardening), LG-025 (Fleet Sync Studio & Show Deployment v1), LG-026 (Show Transport v2 & Synchronized Cue Playback), LG-029 (Node-Backed Authentication & Provisioning), LG-030 (Frontend Architecture Alignment), LG-031 (Canonical Runtime State & API v1 Cutover), LG-036 / LG-036.1 (System, Recovery & Hardened OTA), and LG-037 (Hardware Certification, Bench Evidence & Production Bring-Up):
- **Certification workflow and evidence architecture are fully implemented.**
- **No new feature families** (Scene Studio redesign, Timeline drag/drop, TLS, cloud services) will be introduced before physical hardware validation.
- Physical hardware certification remains dependent on executing the plan on real reference hardware using the procedures defined in [`docs/HARDWARE_CERTIFICATION.md`](file:///c:/Users/slavd/lumigrid/docs/HARDWARE_CERTIFICATION.md).

# Hardware, playback and operator continuity — 2026-11-01

Source baseline: `a4bf518b5e58a69ecde6da194299417459a70b59` on `main`.

This batch corrects output failure reporting, playback handover, node synchronization and browser control ownership. It also strengthens qualification evidence and clean-checkout dependency preparation. It is software engineering evidence, not physical board qualification or a conformity assessment.

## Changes and resulting behavior

| Area | Reproduced problem | Correction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PWM output gate | A rejected GPIO write could still report output enabled or inhibited | Gate operations return their errors, retain the last successfully commanded enable state and expose `output_gate_failed`; successful ordinary writes cannot clear that fault |
| Recovery and stop | An older recovery could acknowledge a newer gate failure; blackout, stop reset and topology publication could overlook failed inhibition | Gate-fault generations preserve newer failures. Zero frames are still attempted, while failed inhibition blocks a confirmed blackout, stop reset or replacement topology |
| I2C recovery | Failed driver deletion or GPIO operations could be ignored while recovery manipulated the bus | Driver ownership survives failed deletion. Recovery checks GPIO configuration, clock and STOP operations, and released-line observations before continuing |
| Scene continuity | A new timed scene could inherit a previous frozen/manual transition and remain at progress zero | New timed, immediate, manual and fallback playback establish their own transition mode; frozen state no longer leaks into the replacement |
| Sync takeover | Auto election could precede remote cue/scheduler cleanup, and failed timeout cleanup was discarded | The worker must acknowledge remote release before local leadership. Rejected cleanup retains diagnostics and retries; a valid packet at timer zero expires correctly; expired peer slots are reusable |
| Embedded dashboard | A permanent Connected label and cached status could conceal loss; failed resource reads replaced valid data with defaults | Owned WebSocket reconnects, bounded HTTP fallback, request deadlines, explicit freshness states and preserved loaded documents replace those failure paths |
| Editing and node selection | Initial scene loading and asynchronous operations could use incomplete data or a later selected node | Creation and saves require their source data; operations belong to the connection and node where they started, including restore, update and stop continuations |
| Dashboard telemetry | Safety/protocol labels and power budgets contained fixed values; previews could look like measurements | Existing runtime fields drive status, faults and configured budget. Missing estimates remain unavailable; preview rates and software power estimates are labelled explicitly |
| Browser persistence | Denied browser storage could throw during auth construction or fleet reads | A shared guarded boundary handles storage getters and operations. Session credentials remain tab-scoped, with in-memory operation when persistence is unavailable |
| Qualification records | Current file hashes were reported without comparing archived digests; checks only repeated firmware and board revision | Version 2 binds every result to the full declared build/unit/setup identity and compares each capture against its recorded SHA-256 |

The embedded interface retains the existing navigation and uses LumiGrid's cherry/pink palette. Its header distinguishes live updates, HTTP polling, reconnecting and offline state. A preserved value from a disconnected node is not displayed as a current measurement.

Embedded sessions now store the selected host and token together. Existing split host/token sessions require a fresh sign-in; the saved host preference is retained. Switching nodes cancels pending requests and prevents restore, upload, polling or stop continuations from targeting a subsequently selected node.

## Reproducible dependency preparation

The checked-in cJSON package contains 165 files, while its locked registry archive contains 234. The 69 omitted files are 68 upstream test files hidden by an upstream ignore rule and a regular `cJSON/.git` pointer file. That pointer participates in the registry hash but cannot be represented as a normal Git tree entry. All existing files were byte-identical to the registry package.

A clean checkout therefore failed the component manager's integrity gate before firmware compilation. Dependency preparation recognizes only that exact incomplete tree, checks its existing lock/marker identity and preserves it in a unique `.pio/dependency-snapshots/` backup. The normal component manager restores the locked package. Configuration then explicitly verifies the complete package hash before accepting it. Modified or unfamiliar local trees are left untouched and remain subject to normal integrity checks.

The dependency lock is unchanged. The expected complete cJSON component hash is `e788323270d90738662d66fffa910bfe1fba019bba087f01557e70c40485b469`. Integrity bypass settings are not used.

## Verification

The final source/build results are recorded below. Host tests exercise production sources with injected boundaries; they do not emulate peripheral timing, radio traffic or electrical faults on a PCB.

| Verification | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Output-driver host suite | 34 scenarios plus one PM-enabled teardown case passed with ASan/UBSan |
| Lighting-state host suite | 15 scenarios passed with ASan/UBSan; both new transition-mode cases fail against the original source |
| NodeSync production-source suite | 33 scenarios passed with UBSan; five new failure cases reproduce against the original source |
| NodeSync host-thread suite | 5 scenarios passed with UBSan, including repeated restarts and blocked callbacks |
| Clock discipline / runtime callback / teardown ordering | 13 / 10 / 4 scenarios passed |
| Effect renderer / catalogue API | 12 renderer groups passed; catalogue, bounded scene serialization and allocation-failure checks passed |
| Qualification evidence | 34 tests passed, including changed captures, setup mismatches, path containment and legacy schema rejection |
| Browser storage/auth/transport integration | 44 tests passed; strict API/storage boundary audit passed |
| Embedded script and Chromium flows | 39 production-script tests and 6 Chromium flows passed, including desktop/mobile disconnect preservation and pending-operation ownership |
| Managed dependency preparation | 5 tests passed using SDK Python; isolated incomplete-checkout recovery restored and verified all 234 package files, then repeated preparation was a no-op |
| Factory and diagnostic target builds | Both passed with Espressif32 6.7.0 / ESP-IDF 5.2.1, including fresh CMake configuration |
| Web build and static checks | Production build passed; `npm run check` reported 0 errors and 0 warnings; 6 documentation tests passed |
| Generated documentation and embedded headers | Documentation synchronization/check passed; both C++ asset headers are identical, containing the 34,310-byte gzip dashboard |

### Local build identities

These identities describe the locally compiled final working-tree sources based on the baseline above. They are build evidence, not measurements on a flashed device. The source inventory includes restored managed dependencies: all 629 recorded inputs were unchanged across the builds, with canonical input SHA-256 `0c5debdd163b55be8b7e8177ea6e31e2865d63446935dfaaf78bdfb7d801d439`.

| Image | Binary bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Factory | 1,386,544 | `2620ca808e1566d0c10295ba3f09ab640ce202cf14326879dab5e6445e8f0b1e` |
| Diagnostic test | 1,586,720 | `a6eab1da9ee8ff482b1f6c413b75848bb292e678ee066e7aca9e31a586d02c83` |

The linked factory/test images occupy 57.2% / 65.4% of their 2,424,832-byte app slots. Partition and boot invariant checks passed. The factory's largest analyzed acyclic direct-call boot path is 5,648 bytes; indirect calls, ROM and interrupt stack usage still require target validation. The diagnostic image is not a production release.

CI now includes the sync, clock, runtime integration, evidence, embedded browser-script, continuity, marketing and focused auth/storage regressions. At the source baseline, GitHub Actions reported `startup_failure` with no jobs; that is separate from local build/test results. Inspect the run for the delivered commit rather than inheriting an earlier CI claim.

## Qualification record migration

Use [the updated evidence procedure](CONTINUITY_QUALIFICATION.md) and `evidence-template.json`. Version 1 records and plain evidence-path strings are rejected. A current digest cannot establish that an old test used the current specimen, wiring, supply or load. Preserve archived records and mark unverifiable checks `NOT_RUN` until repeated.

The tool checks supplied declarations, file identity and completeness. It does not independently verify measurements, approve electrical limits or issue a CE certificate.

## Remaining measured acceptance

Run the final factory image on the intended PCB, supply, loads, wiring, enclosure and antenna. Retain image identity and observations for these changed paths:

1. Observe output-enable and PWM behavior through boot, stop, clear and controlled I2C recovery. A successful GPIO API result describes the commanded state; actual pin level and output darkness require measurement.
2. Freeze a transition, then request a timed scene, a saved preset and fallback playback. Confirm the replacement advances and the previous manual/frozen controls do not persist.
3. Lose the sync leader during cue and timeline playback. Confirm ownership release precedes takeover; retain both nodes' logs and test recovery after rejected cleanup.
4. Exercise browser disconnect/reconnect and switching between nodes during pending operations. Confirm stale values are marked, loaded scenes remain intact and follow-up commands stay with their original node or are cancelled.
5. Complete loaded endurance, reset, memory/stack, current, temperature and the agreed radio/EMC/electrical assessment. No such physical measurements were taken in this batch.

One known modeling issue remains: `OutputController::enforce_power_guard_locked()` and `PowerBudget::enforce()` use different RGB/RGBW estimates, and the final guard scales its fixed-idle bookkeeping. For full RGB white their formulas currently yield 890 versus 300 mW per pixel; full RGBW yields 1,270 versus 385 mW. These are code-derived estimates, not measured current. Agree a shared model and reconcile post-guard telemetry against actual loads before using these estimates as an installation limit.

qualification/2026-11-01-POWER-CONTINUIT.markdown:
# Power accounting and editor continuity — 2026-11-01

Source baseline: `7579f28d2860f69b7a9557cb51b0d4a39fdb30a7` on `main`. This is the second November 1 implementation batch, following [the earlier hardware/playback report](2026-11-01-POLISH.md).

## Changes and resulting behavior

### Output power and effect rendering

The renderer, final output guard and configuration preflight now share the conservative model already used by the final guard: 5 mW idle per configured pixel, 295 mW per full RGB component, and 380 mW per full white component. This resolves the model disagreement recorded in the earlier report without claiming calibration against the installed strips.

Fractional RGB/RGBW/PWM loads remain exact through channel, supply and global limits, soft start and transient limits. Each stage re-estimates the quantized commands. Only active demand scales; fixed idle remains. Reporting rounds upward after aggregation. The mixed-limit regression checks transmitted RGB/RGBW bytes and PWM duties: **5,665 mW requested becomes 1,193 mW final**, split into 706 mW and 487 mW supply estimates, with no second dimming by the final guard.

An enabled supply with zero usable capacity extinguishes assigned active outputs, including unknown-rated PWM. This covers explicit zero derating and positive settings that round to zero capacity. Disabled supplies remain disabled tiers. If a budget is below fixed addressable idle, active demand becomes zero while the estimate retains that idle floor.

Runtime/API power snapshots come from the final confirmed output command. A failed commit followed by a failed blackout preserves the previous estimate and marks it incomplete/unknown. Confirmed blackout and PCA recovery refresh the estimate. Lighting and output locks are acquired separately, avoiding an inverted nested lock order. Existing JSON field names remain unchanged; the dashboard carries the existing completeness flag through normalization and qualifies incomplete estimates.

### Synchronization continuity

A follower must successfully release the previous remote transport before accepting a preferred or replacement leader. Rejected release retains the previous source, sequence and snapshot; it does not discipline the clock, feed the watchdog, apply the packet or send an acknowledgement for the replacement. The worker rechecks shutdown ownership after release. This also handles a rebooted leader reusing prior generation values. The wire protocol remains version 6 with 76-byte packets.

### Dashboard and editing

HTTP responses, stream snapshots, command receipts, login/bootstrap work and network applies belong to the node and session where they began. Switching A → B → A cannot revive old requests. Caller cancellation and deadlines cover JSON body reads as well as response headers. An old unauthorized response cannot clear newer credentials.

Preview packets do not refresh status freshness. The overview and sidebar distinguish current, stale and unavailable state; missing values do not become fabricated healthy/normal/zero-power results. Network edits preserve drafts after denied saves or failed reads, and apply polling has a real deadline plus ownership for each apply attempt.

Scene and cue reads preserve the loaded document when a replacement fails. Saves retain the submitted version as the saved baseline while edits made during the request remain dirty. Save/run/delete/import continuations stay with their original node/session and selection. Reconnects preserve the same session's drafts while cancelling superseded work. Failed initial metadata reads block creation and saves; failed scene-dependency reads block deletion.

Scene conflict reload fetches the current node scene and motion. Selecting a scene while continuing to edit the visible draft preserves those edits. A delayed delete cannot clear a newer draft in the same slot; edits made during deletion remain recoverable as an unsaved draft. New, Delete and Unsaved Changes dialogs now open and place keyboard focus inside the shared dialog. A persistent Cancel/Close button retains focus as dependency reads complete. Scene loading and duplication snapshot reactive state before cloning it; actual browser checks caught the original proxy-cloning failure. Cue saves use the editor's actual busy state, and subscriptions/timers are released on teardown.

### Candidate packaging

The candidate packager checks the ESP32 image target, segment count and bounds, segment alignment, checksum padding, payload XOR checksum and appended SHA-256 for both bootloader and application images. It rejects truncated payloads, corrupt checksums/digests, missing required digests and unexpected trailing data. The accepted format is the pinned build's unsigned, unpadded image contract; signing or padded formats require an explicit packaging update.

Fingerprints are calculated from the exact bytes checked. Replacing an application, bootloader, partition table or merged image between validation and staging blocks packaging. The staged copies are checked again against those fingerprints. These checks detect corruption and replacement during packaging; they are not secure-boot authentication or build attestation.

## Validation

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| ESP-IDF factory and diagnostic environments | Both built successfully in one integration invocation |
| Output driver host tests | 34 production scenarios plus 1 PM-quarantine scenario passed with ASan/UBSan |
| Lighting host tests | 15 existing scenarios and 6 new power scenarios passed with ASan/UBSan, including targeted corrections |
| NodeSync host tests | 39 deterministic cases and 6 real-thread cases passed with UBSan |
| Candidate packaging regressions | 19 tests passed, including five artifact-replacement variants |
| Scene page async regressions | 17 cases passed against the production page functions |
| Cue page/store/document/API regressions | 55 tests passed, including 28 page async cases |
| Combined web unit gate | 186 tests passed in 15 files, including the scene/cue cases above |
| Chromium interaction checks | 13 distinct cases passed: 7 core continuity, 3 existing setup/login, brightness draft preservation, and 2 Scene Studio cases |
| Svelte, public-copy and continuity checks | Zero errors or warnings; copy, marketing and continuity checks passed |
| Web production build | Passed |
| Documentation generation | 64 guides, 88 routes and 10 source-backed capacities synchronized; links validated |
| Runtime arithmetic and architectural invariants | Passed |
| Strict API surface audit | Passed |
| Actual candidate package | Both bootloaders and both application images passed integrity checks; merged image and partition layout verified |

The focused page harness executes actual production function declarations with controlled state and deferred promises. It does not substitute for rendered Svelte browser checks. The workflow includes the focused node ownership, transport, command tracking, scene/cue editor and network retry regressions.

## Build identity

Pinned firmware tooling: Espressif32 6.7.0, ESP-IDF 5.2.1, GCC 13.2.0, PlatformIO 6.2.0 and esptool 4.5.1. Both environments use ESP32, 8 MB flash, DIO and 40 MHz flash frequency with partition layout v2. The diagnostic image contains development flags and is not the production candidate.

The build input inventory contains **630 files**, including the actual restored managed dependency tree. Its SHA-256 was unchanged before and after the successful integration build:

`66c7efa4167dbf5e98ca96a46f623834cfd0e0da16842c03601bddaff2a4583c`

The local checkout uses synthetic snapshot history. Its candidate manifest truthfully records local snapshot `4e4d9f829edf5b0cf33a0f80e7efd96ca7affab4` with a dirty working tree; that value is not an upstream build-commit claim. The baseline above plus the recorded input inventory identifies the reviewed build inputs. A clean release build should record its own final Git commit and artifacts.

| Artifact | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Factory application | 1,387,280 | `b622a0d83b7aebe38077ff2b4036011c0427248c8901698df8fea0bb88abaea6` |
| Diagnostic application | 1,588,544 | `27b4c943615abd1c3a2b790b5b05a12c4cf6343653da62fbea128f48b47e3095` |
| Merged factory image | 1,452,816 | `f0f09307a132c77789c29baa1c98e3e6b42b2aeccc8bda7a3869cb3a7e8f899f` |

Each application slot is 2,424,832 bytes. Factory usage is 57.2%, with 1,037,552 bytes remaining; diagnostic usage is 65.5%, with 836,288 bytes remaining. The factory static acyclic direct-call stack report is 5,648 bytes; indirect, ROM and interrupt usage still requires target validation.

The merged image is intended for fresh installation. Its erased gaps include NVS/OTA metadata; use the approved migration or application-only OTA procedure for existing devices rather than overwriting their configuration.

## Readiness boundary

This batch provides source review, host regressions, rendered browser checks, target compilation and candidate-byte integrity evidence. No board was flashed or measured in this session. Output-current calibration, all-channel/network coexistence, cold-start/reset captures, multi-node timing, injected hardware recovery, thermal endurance, OTA/rollback and the applicable conformity assessment remain physical acceptance work. Follow [the continuity qualification plan](CONTINUITY_QUALIFICATION.md) against the exact assembly and image.

Positive budgets cannot fully constrain unknown-rated PWM loads. Brightness scaling cannot remove fixed addressable idle. An unconfirmed I/O operation cannot establish physical consumption. The dashboard therefore presents command estimates and their completeness, not current measurements or a CE result.

The latest hosted run observed on the source baseline, [41286129799](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/lumigrid/actions/runs/41286129799), ended in `startup_failure` before any jobs or check runs existed. The connector did not expose a cause. Local build/test passes above are separate evidence; the newly published commit's hosted result must be checked independently.

qualification/CONTINUITY_QUALIFICATION.markdown:
# Continuity qualification and evidence handoff

This is a project bench plan, not a conformity assessment or certificate. The accompanying script checks the completeness and identity of operator-supplied evidence; it does not independently evaluate measurements.

## Candidate identity

After applying the batch, completing application and firmware builds, and committing the reviewed source, record the new source commit, exact application-image SHA-256, PCB revision, serial number, wiring revision, supply, loads, antenna and enclosure. Do not reuse an older candidate's evidence as a pass for a modified image.

Build and verification results are revision-specific; see the dated change report for the candidate under test. The October 30 source batch did not include target builds or flashing. No software report establishes physical output behavior, and a previous image's build result does not qualify a modified image.

## Bench records

| Check ID | Record to retain |
| --- | --- |
| firmware_builds | Factory/diagnostic build logs, effective configurations, image hashes and flash layout checks |
| safe_boot_and_reset | Measured output-enable and LED-data behavior through cold start, resets and power interruption; identify instruments and capture files |
| all_16_outputs | Connector-by-connector mapping and behavior for A1–A8 and P1–P8 with supported loads |
| combined_outputs_and_network | Simultaneous output operation and network/API load; record selected effects, loads, timing captures, resets and memory minima |
| network_loss_and_reconnect | Leader loss, stale and conflicting reports, reconnection, content mismatch and group selection; retain both nodes' logs |
| sync_shutdown_and_recovery | On the actual PCB, repeat sync disable/enable, role/token changes and network rebind under simultaneous output load; retain timeout/retry behavior, worker counts, output captures, heap and stack minima. Demonstrate no replacement worker or dependency teardown before the old worker acknowledges exit. Lose the leader during cue/timeline playback in Auto mode: local leadership must wait for remote cue/scheduler release; rejected release must remain visible and retry before takeover. Repeat with a preferred replacement leader and a rebooted leader reusing scene/timeline generation values. A failed release must retain the previous source and must not acknowledge or apply the replacement packet. |
| ota_and_rollback | Valid update, interruption and rollback on the intended layout; preserve configuration and image identity |
| configuration_power_loss | Interrupted save/restore and recovery; do not erase the only backup during the test |
| thermal_endurance | Actual current and temperature observations with duration, ambient conditions and agreed limits; firmware does not invent temperature sensor data |
| installation_limits_review | Approved supply/voltage/load/wiring/enclosure/antenna constraints for the exact assembly |

Set test limits and durations with the responsible engineer/lab and include those decisions in the evidence. Software-estimated power is not a current or temperature measurement. A software blackout is not a physical disconnection of strip power.

For power-limit acceptance, compare actual driver commands and measured supply current with the shared model in [Configuration](../CONFIGURATION.md). Include mixed RGB/RGBW/PWM loads, channel/supply/global ceilings, soft start, and a supply derated to zero usable capacity. Confirm that a ceiling below addressable idle extinguishes active demand while retaining the idle estimate. Inject output and blackout failures: last-confirmed estimates must be marked incomplete until recovery. Unknown PWM ratings cannot establish compliance with a positive power budget.

## Running the completeness preflight

Keep measurement records outside the source tree so that adding evidence does not make the frozen source dirty. Copy `evidence-template.json`, fill the identity only from the exact tested build, and mark each result truthfully. The `lumigrid-qualification-v2` record binds every check to the full declared identity: source and firmware hashes, PCB revision, unit serial, wiring, supply, loads, enclosure and antenna. A check repeats the firmware hash and PCB revision and records `identity_sha256` for that complete setup. Changing any identity field invalidates results still bound to the old setup.

Run the preflight with the filled identity and the checks still marked `NOT_RUN` to obtain the `identity_sha256` in its report. Exit 2 is expected at this stage. Record that value with each test **when it is performed**, and archive the original record. This digest detects mixed records; it cannot prove that the operator declared the physical setup truthfully.

Each evidence entry is an object containing a relative `path` and the SHA-256 recorded when the capture was archived:

```json
{
  "path": "safe-boot/scope.csv",
  "sha256": "<64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from the archived capture>"
}
```

For example, calculate a capture's digest with Python:

```sh
python -c "import hashlib,pathlib,sys; print(hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_bytes()).hexdigest())" /path/to/evidence/safe-boot/scope.csv
```

The checker compares those recorded digests with the files present now. Replacing a capture at the same path blocks completeness. Empty files, escaping paths, duplicate paths within one check, missing hashes and mismatched setup identity also block completeness. A shared capture may support several checks; the report lists those associations. Current hashes appear in incomplete reports for diagnosis, but do not replace archived hashes merely to clear a mismatch.

Version 1 records and plain path strings are rejected. Migrate from the original archived test records and capture hashes, preserving the tested setup and result. If that identity or evidence cannot be established, leave the check `NOT_RUN` and repeat it; do not automatically stamp old results with the current setup.

```sh
python scripts/qualification_preflight.py \
  --record /path/to/evidence/record.json \
  --firmware /path/to/tested/factory/firmware.bin \
  --source-root . \
  --output /path/to/evidence/preflight-001.json
```

Exit 0 means the specified bench-evidence records are complete, **not** that the product is certified. Exit 2 means blocked/incomplete evidence. Exit 1 means the command itself could not complete. Existing output files are never overwritten. No network request, firmware flash, or lighting command is issued.

## Remaining engineering work before release

The source includes cooperative NodeSync shutdown ownership, runtime teardown/callback integration and acknowledged remote release before automatic leader takeover. Host behavior and interleavings have been tested; the dated change report records which target and web builds were actually completed. Whole-runtime on-board acceptance remains required. Oversized sync datagrams are rejected in host tests. Full UDP semantic/security validation, actual multi-node timing, hardware recovery, output coexistence and RF/EMC tests are not established by these host tests. Do not treat protocol compatibility, matching checksums or a green dashboard as a physical measurement.

## Regulatory boundary and sources

The applicable conformity assessment, technical documentation, declaration and marking must be addressed for the intended product configuration. The manufacturer remains responsible; this internal tooling cannot issue a CE certificate. Confirm current applicability, including radio/cybersecurity requirements, with the lab rather than relying on an older checklist.

Official references checked on 2026-10-30:
- European Commission, Radio Equipment Directive: https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/sectors/electrical-and-electronic-engineering-industries-eei/radio-equipment-directive-red_en
- European Commission, manufacturers and CE marking: https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/single-market/goods/ce-marking/manufacturers_en
- Directive 2014/53/EU, including Article 17 (operating configurations): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2014/53/oj/eng
